<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of determining critical days in an illness. It moves from the basic calculation of 90-degree increments to a more sophisticated explanation of why these days vary based on the Moon's actual speed in the sky, rather than following a simple seven-day calendar.</meta>

<page-num>38</page-num>
<header>BOOK</header>

And on the fourteenth day, the Moon generally reaches the opposite sign, which is why the fourteenth day is also called <term>critical<note>original: "critica"; a day when a disease reaches a turning point, for better or worse.</note></term>. From then, on the twentieth or twenty-first day, the Moon will reach the second "fourth aspect" <note>This refers to the second square aspect, 270 degrees from the starting point.</note>. But on the 27th or 28th day, the Moon returns to the sign and the place in which it was at the beginning of the illness. There is also a certain similarity of the fourth day to a critical day, and likewise the 11th and 17th.

And know that the motion of the Moon varies because of the distance of the center of its circle from the center of the Earth, and because of the motion which it has in its <term>epicycle<note>In pre-modern astronomy, an epicycle was a small circle the center of which moves around the circumference of a larger one; this was used to explain the varying speeds of planets.</note></term>. Hence it is that on some days the Moon moves 15 degrees, on others 13, and sometimes less than 13.

Therefore, when the Moon is swift in its course, it reaches the fourth aspect <note>the square, or 90-degree mark</note> after six days and some hours from the start of the illness, counting from the hour the sick person took to their bed until a similar hour. But if the Moon is slow, it does not reach the fourth aspect until 7 full days and nearly a half; and according to the common reckoning of men, this will be on the ninth day, for then the Moon reaches its fourth aspect, which is why many have said the ninth day would be critical. If, however, the Moon is at an average speed, it reaches the fourth aspect about five hours before the seventh full day. It is fitting, moreover, for the opposite aspect <note>the opposition, or 180-degree mark</note> to occur on the 14th day. In the same way, due to average motion, it is fitting for the day of crisis to be the 20th or 21st day. The reasoning is the same for the 27th or 28th day. Even the fifth day sometimes produces a crisis when the Moon is in a <term>sextile aspect<note>An angle of 60 degrees, considered a harmonious or helpful positioning.</note></term> to its place where it was at the beginning of the illness. Likewise, on the 11th day the Moon will sometimes be in a <term>trine aspect<note>An angle of 120 degrees, generally viewed as very favorable in medical astrology.</note></term> if its course is slow. Similarly, this happens on the 9th day if it is fast.

From these things it clearly appears that those who say the 7th, 14th, 20th, and 27th days will always be critical are greatly mistaken, since critical days vary according to the differing motion of the Moon, as has been said.

**Fourth.** If, at the start of the illness, the Moon is in aspect with a planet that is under the rays of the Sun <note>term: combust; a planet is "under the rays" when it is so close to the Sun that its own influence is overwhelmed or hidden.</note>, do not make a judgment, just as if there were no aspect at all. If there are 12 degrees between Mercury and the Sun, its testimony will be mediocre, and if its latitude is northern, its testimony is firm.

**Fifth rule.** It must be considered when the Moon reaches a degree that is similar in longitude to the degree of its own place—namely, the longitude of the Moon measured from the meeting of the two circles at the equinoctial points (such as Aries or Libra) or from the solstitial points (such as Cancer and Capricorn). **Eighth rule.** If the Moon, at the start of the illness, is in a sign of the same nature as the sickness <note>for example, a "cold and dry" Moon in a "cold and dry" sign like Virgo during a "cold and dry" melancholy illness</note>, it is a bad sign; but if it is in a sign of the opposite nature, it is good for the illness.

**Ninth.** The conjunction <term>conjunction: when two celestial bodies appear at the same point in the zodiac</term> of the Moon with the Sun is a very bad sign. It is even worse if there are fewer than 6 degrees between the Sun and Moon and the Moon has not yet reached the node <note>the points where the Moon's orbit crosses the path of the Sun</note>. However, if they are joined in the head of Aries or Leo, the evil is somewhat diminished. If they are 12 degrees apart, it is not a complete evil. 6 **Tenth rule.** The conjunction of the Moon with Saturn signifies evil and the prolongation of the illness. If Saturn is slow in its motion, the evil will increase; if fast, the evil will be diminished. If it is retrograde <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward in the sky</term> and the person is cured before it reaches its opposition to the Sun, they will later suffer a relapse. If it is retrograde after the opposition to the Sun, the evil is diminished. If the Moon in this conjunction with Saturn is fast in its course, it is a bad sign, for it signifies a long duration and a bad end. If it is slow in its course, the evil is diminished. If the Moon is increasing in light <note>waxing</note>, Saturn will do only a little harm; but if it is decreasing in light <note>waning</note>, this is evil upon evil. If Saturn is "oriental" from the Sun <note>rising in the east before the Sun</note> and the illness arises from coldness, the evil is lessened. But if the illness is from heat, the evil will be doubled. If Saturn is "occidental" from the Sun <note>setting after the Sun</note> and the illness is hot, the evil is lessened; but if it is from coldness, it will be evil upon evil.

7 Likewise, if Saturn is at its furthest distance <note>apogee; its highest point from Earth</note> and the illness is caused by retention or restriction <note>such as constipation or urinary blockage</note>, the evil is doubled.

If, however, it is in its lower "abside" <note>perigee; its lowest point</note>, that is, the shortest distance, or opposite its highest point, its evil is diminished. If it is in the lower place and the illness is from a "solution of the belly" <note>diarrhea or purging</note>, evil is added upon evil; 8 but if it is at its highest point or near it, its evil is lessened. The Moon joined to a retrograde planet signifies vomiting. If the Moon is in one of the houses of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, the evil is diminished, unless the illness is a cough. ...and it is still better **11** if it is not the lord <term>lord: the planet that "rules" or has the most influence over a specific zodiac sign or house</term> of a bad house <note>original: malæ domus; in astrology, the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses are considered "bad" as they relate to illness, death, and hidden enemies</note> with respect to the rising sign at the start of the illness. Similarly, its power is greater if it is at the apogee <note>original: auge; the point in a planet's orbit furthest from the Earth</note> of its epicycle <note>original: parui circuli; a small circular orbit used in ancient astronomy to explain planetary motion</note> or its eccentric <note>original: ecentrici; an orbital path that is not centered on the Earth</note>, as was previously stated regarding Saturn. Indeed, the opposite and square (90-degree) aspects of Jupiter are all good, except that they carry a small amount of labor and weariness for the infirm; but in the trine (120-degree) and sextile (60-degree) aspects, no higher planet is better.

**Twelfth rule.** The Moon joined to Mars is a bad sign. **12** if the Moon is waning in light, the evil is diminished; conversely, if it is waxing <note>original: aucta lumine</note>, it signifies "pain upon pain." If Mars is positioned after its opposition to the Sun, the evil is lessened. But if it is in the part where the Sun is with respect to its small circle <note>the epicycle</note>—that is, before the opposition—it is a bad sign. If Mars is at its apogee or near it, and the sickness arises from "dryness," it signifies an increase of evil. However, if it is opposite its apogee, the evil is diminished. If it is at the lowest point of its eccentric circle and the illness is from "humidity," it is "evil upon evil"; if the illness is from dryness, the evil is diminished. The sextile and trine aspects, however, foretell a good outcome. If the Moon is in the house of Mars or in its exaltation <term>exaltation: a specific sign where a planet’s influence is particularly strengthened</term>, its evil is diminished.

**Thirteenth rule.** If the Moon is joined to Venus, it is as was said concerning Jupiter. If the sick person is a youth or a woman, this is better than if they are an old person. If the sickness arises from "heat," Venus will be more effective than Jupiter; if from "coldness," Jupiter is more effective than Venus.

**Fourteenth rule.** If the Moon is joined with Mercury while it is not "under the rays of the Sun" <note>original: sub radijs Solis; a planet is "combust" or weakened when too close to the Sun, here defined as needing to be more than 12 degrees away</note>, and Mercury is "occidental" <note>setting in the west after the Sun</note>, and they are joined in the house of a fortunate star <term>fortunate star: a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</term>, it signifies a half-measure of good. **15** In the house of an unfortunate star <term>unfortunate star: a "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars</term>, it signifies a half-measure of evil. If it is in its own house, it signifies a little good; but if it is in the house opposite its own houses <note>its "detriment," where a planet's power is frustrated</note>, it signifies a little evil. Its square aspect signifies less evil than the opposite aspect; the sextile signifies a little good, but the trine signifies more good.

**Fifteenth rule.** If the Moon is in conjunction with both Saturn and Jupiter, consider which of them "conquers" the other, as I shall explain: for the one that is near its apogee, or at the greatest distance in its eccentric circle or near it, will conquer the one that is near the closer distance...

And if one planet has a northern latitude, and another is on the northern middle line, the former will prevail; if both are northern, the one which has the greater latitude will prevail. And if Saturn prevails in this conjunction, the sick person will die; nevertheless, because of Jupiter, it will be a little less [burdensome] for the sick person in their illness, and they will not be too heavily weighed down, although they will still fear for themselves. But if Jupiter prevails, the infirm person will escape death, though this will be after great danger, thoughts of dying, and the fear of death.

**The sixteenth rule.** If the Moon is in opposition **19** to Saturn and Jupiter, the sick person will indeed be strong but will not escape death, unless Saturn is retrograde and Jupiter is direct <term>direct: moving forward in the zodiac, which is the "healthy" or strong state for a planet</term>.

If however the Moon is with Saturn and Mars, or Mercury, in opposition or square <term>square: a harsh 90-degree angle between planets</term>, this is bad for the sick person.

**The eighteenth.** All aspects of the Sun and Moon are universally good, except for the opposite aspect from Aquarius or Libra; because then the good will be diminished.

**The nineteenth.** If the Moon is joined to Saturn and the Sun, and it is in their opposition, it is half a "good sign"; but if it is in the fourth aspect <note>the square aspect</note>, it is nearly half good.

**The twentieth rule.** If the Moon is with Saturn and opposite the Sun, and Mars is in the fourth aspect, it is neither good nor bad; similarly if the Sun is with Mars.

**The twenty-first rule.** If the Moon is with Mars and the Sun is in opposition, it is a bad sign; if it is in the fourth aspect, it is a medium sign of evil. And if the Moon is with Mars, the aspect of Venus is more profitable than that of Jupiter; if however it is with Saturn, the aspect of Jupiter is more profitable than that of Venus.

And whatever has been said about the wandering stars <note>the planets</note>, this must also be understood regarding the fixed stars **20** of the first and second honor <note>first and second magnitude; the brightest stars</note>, and especially those which have a small latitude and are around the ecliptic and in the circle of signs. For if the Moon is joined to those which have the nature of Jupiter or Venus, it is good...

### EXPLANATIONS.

1. Regarding the first rule: if you do not remember which sign is the house of the planets, which is the exaltation, which is the fall, or the opposite house, look for this in Chapter 6 of Book 1.

2. Regarding the second rule: the Moon is "without aspect" when it is either not joined to any planet or does not regard any planet, whether exactly <note>original: "partiliter"; occurring at the precise degree</note> or within its orb <note>original: "platice"; occurring within a wider range of degrees</note>, by the rays of a sextile [✶], square [□], trine [△], or opposition [☍]. By the term "aspect," conjunction [☌] is also understood, although it is technically named improperly <note>strictly speaking, a conjunction is a union, not an aspect/angle, but astrologers often group them together</note>.

3. Northern latitude: if you wish to know the latitude of the Moon, you will find the table of the Moon's latitude in the ephemerides <term>ephemerides: tables providing the predicted positions of celestial bodies for every day of the year</term>, by which you will easily learn it; this is on page 65. You will also easily learn the latitude of the other planets from the ephemeris, for you will find it at the end of each month, serving that same month.

4. In a movable sign: he taught this in Chapter 2 of Book 1. Of an equal nature: you have the natures of the signs in Chapter 2 of the first book, and the nature of the disease in Chapter 6 of that book.

5. Regarding signs of long ascension: Cancer [♋], Leo [♌], Virgo [♍], Libra [♎], Scorpio [♏], and Sagittarius [♐], as was said in the first book, are signs of long ascension <note>these signs take a longer time to rise over the eastern horizon than others</note>.

6. The tenth rule: seek the method from the first book by which you may distinguish when a planet is either fast or slow in its motion; for we taught that in Chapter 5.

7. The same applies if Saturn [♄] should be in longitude <note>referring to its distance from the Earth</note>. So that you may know when a planet is in longitude—whether at its longer or shorter distance—I have transferred a little table here from Magini’s ephemeris <note>Giovanni Paolo Magini (1555–1617) was an Italian astronomer famous for his highly accurate planetary tables</note>, in which you will see it easily.

### BOOK FOUR.
#### SUMMARY OF CHAPTER I.

*The physician uses intermediate causes as if they were primary ones for judging; the astronomer judges from the position of the stars, which are more universal causes and naturally set effects in motion. For this reason, astrology is superior to medicine.* <note>The author argues that while a doctor looks at symptoms (intermediate causes), the astrologer looks at the heavens (universal causes) which govern those symptoms.</note> *The material of the entire book is divided into two parts: first, a treatise on urine not seen, and then on urine that is seen.* <note>This refers to the practice of "astrological uroscopy," where a practitioner would predict the appearance and nature of a patient's urine using a horoscope before actually inspecting the physical sample.</note> *To discern the qualities of the urine, at the hour the request is made, the physician must cast a <term>figure of the heavens</term> <note>original: "figuram coeli"; a horoscope or astrological chart showing the positions of the stars at a specific moment</note> and place the planets within that figure. Then, you should ask the bearer of the request who he is in relation to the sick person and assign him his proper place in the figure. Second, the <term>almuten</term> <note>original: "almutes"; from Arabic 'al-muta'izz', referring to the planet that holds the most power or "dignity" over a specific point in the zodiac</note> must be sought. From all these factors, you should judge in the manner the author teaches all those things which physicians observe in urines when they examine them.*

SINCE the primary and principal causes of change in these lower realms—and the forces that drive them—are the movements of celestial bodies, as Ptolemy maintained in the first book of the *Quadripartitum* <note>original: "quadripartiti"; referring to Ptolemy’s four-part work on astrology, the *Tetrabiblos*</note> when he said that a power exists in the reality of matter <note>original: "materia alathia"; from the Greek 'aletheia' (truth/reality)</note> which, reaching earthly things, compels them to change. Indeed, it forces these same things to naturally undergo mutability. Because the ultimate cause is the readiness of matter to receive this movement from the celestial bodies, there must be intermediate causes running between the primary cause and this ultimate one (since one does not go from one extreme to another except through a middle ground). These intermediate causes adapt matter to various conditions. And now, since a physician’s judgment consists for the most part in the subject matter, he accepts some of these intermediate causes as primary to himself—such as compositions, <term>complexions</term> <note>original: "complexiones"; the specific balance of the four qualities—hot, cold, moist, and dry—within a person</note>, the time, and things of that sort.

The astronomer, however, claims for himself the less common and more specific of these causes, namely the "agents," such as the state and arrangement of the signs [of the zodiac] and stars, and the complexions of things. And just as a physician predicts the outcome through signs—such as phlegm, urine, the pulse, and the outward appearance of the body—so does the astronomer, through the moving cause, naturally anticipate the effect by a conjectural foresight. For this reason, the astronomer's consideration is far more worthy, since it does not require the physical presence of the subject matter. The physician's subject, however, through which and around which he works, is tangible and visible. For this reason, the ancients and Ptolemy (in the first book of the *Quadripartitum*) joined the science of the stars to medical teaching, so that by proceeding in both ways, they might reach a more certain end in their operations. For when the nature of the illness has been foreseen, along with whether medication will help and at what time, then finally the physician may approach usefully and profitably, and he will earn praise from his work. And since one consideration of the physician revolves around the judgment of urine, I have decided to hand down the rules of the ancient astronomers in this brief treatise. First, the judgment of urine not seen; thereafter, briefly, following the intention of physicians, the judgment of urine that has been seen and the contents of the urine. Before learning this, certain things must be noted. This treatise has two parts: The first teaches how to judge urine not seen through seven notable points. The second is on the judgment of urine seen, in which eight considerations occur, as will be clear in what follows.

First to be noted: When someone brings you urine asking for it to be inspected, you must <term>erect a figure of the heavens</term> <note>original: "Erigas... cœli figuram"; cast an astrological chart or horoscope for the specific moment of the request</note> at the hour of the petition and place the stars according to their positions. Once this is erected, you must ask if the bearer of the urine is the one to whom the urine belongs, or if it is someone else related by no blood, such as a friend or a servant. In that case, give the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: "ascendens"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the chart</note> to the owner of the urine, and the fifth house from the ascendant to the liver. If, however, the bearer of the urine is the brother of the sick person...

...third house from the east <note>The "east" refers to the Ascendant or the first house of the zodiacal wheel.</note> is assigned to the <term>lord of the urine</term> <note>original: "domino urinae"; the patient to whom the urine belongs</note>, and the fifth house from that one (which is the seventh house relative to the east) shall be the location of the liver. But if the bearer of the urine is a servant, the sixth house is assigned to the lord of the urine, and the tenth—which is the fifth from the sixth house—is assigned to the liver. If it is a son, the fifth is assigned to the lord of the urine, and the ninth to the liver; and so it goes for others.

However, other seekers of the stars, such as <term>Leopold</term> <note>Likely Leopold of Austria, a 13th-century astrologer</note> and <term>Abraham</term> <note>Likely Abraham Ibn Ezra, a famous 12th-century scholar</note>, say: If the bearer of the urine is a servant, the tenth house should be assigned to the lord of the urine, and the house following the ascendant (which is the fifth from the tenth) to the liver. You should test both and hold onto whichever you find to be truer, though the first method is more rational.

4. Second, it must be noted that once these things are known, one must seek the <term>almuten</term> <note>original: "almutes" or "almuten"; the planet that holds the most power or "dignity" over a specific point in a horoscope</note>. This is the planet that is strongest according to its <term>essential dignities</term> <note>The inherent strength a planet gains by being in a specific sign of the zodiac</note> in the positions of the sun, the moon, the ascendant, the <term>part of fortune</term>, the place of the <term>prevention</term> <note>original: "praeventionis"; refers to the most recent New or Full Moon</note>, and also in the houses of heaven. A planet, by reason of its house, has five dignities or strengths; by reason of its <term>exaltation</term>, four; by reason of its <term>triplicity</term>, three; by reason of its <term>term</term>, two; and by reason of its <term>face</term>, one—as was stated in the first short treatise. You will find the strengths of the planets in the eighth chapter of the first treatise.

An **example** of this: a urine sample was brought by the brother of Lord Charles of Monte Felici at the hour when (as seen below) the firmament was moving with the stars. I wished to know the *almuten*—that is, the lord and strongest planet. At this hour, I observed the strength in the location of the Sun, which was at 15 degrees of **Taurus**; and in the location of the Moon, at 27 degrees of **Capricorn**; and in the east (which I took here as the third house, because it was the brother bringing the urine), namely 25 degrees of **Cancer**. And in the part of fortune, which was at 28 degrees of **Aquarius**; and in the place of the prevention, which was 9 degrees of **Taurus**; as well as the strongest in the houses of heaven. I found that **Saturn** had 18 dignities in all these aforementioned places, **Jupiter** 22, **Mars** 11, the **Sun** 3, **Venus** 21, **Mercury** 5, and finally the **Moon** 27. Therefore, in this case, I declared the **Moon** the *almuten*, because it held the greatest dignities or strengths.

5. Third, it must be noted: once the *almuten* is obtained, one must see from which planet it is separating, or which planet has separated from it. For according to its state shall be the health or sickness of the lord of the urine; and according to the <term>sextile</term> <note>An astrological aspect of 60 degrees</note> which prevails in it, the sickness of that same lord is determined. 6. For if the planet from which the *almuten* separates is masculine, the patient is male; if feminine, the patient is female. 7. And the planet corrupting the *almuten* reveals the cause of the disease according to its own house (which it regards most closely). Furthermore, the location of the *almuten*—the house of heaven in which the *almuten* of the disease is placed—reveals the foundation of the illness. For if it is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The first house, representing the head</note>, the patient suffers in the head. If in the second, they suffer in the neck and throat; and so on for the other houses.

<p align="center">**Example of this.**</p>

I observed the <term>almuten</term> <note>the planet with the most mathematical power in a specific sign or house</note>, the Moon, approaching Mars through a <term>square aspect</term> <note>an astrological angle of 90 degrees, typically indicating tension or conflict</note> while located in Aries and in the twelfth house. Because Mars was well-disposed in its own house <note>Mars rules Aries, making it stronger there</note>, illnesses will trouble the <term>lord of the urine</term> <note>original: "dominum urinae"; the patient</note> very little as far as Mars is concerned. However, because Mars regards the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the inquiry</note> of the lord of the urine—specifically the third house—and Saturn infects this house with its rays, it is foretold that the person born will be quite sickly. They will perhaps suffer from coldness and humidity <note>Referring to the "humors," the bodily fluids thought to govern health</note>. And because Saturn corrupts the almuten (the Moon) with an <term>opposite aspect</term> <note>an angle of 180 degrees</note> from its own sign of Capricorn—which is a better placement for Saturn than Aquarius—it indicates a sickness in the legs around the knees caused by cold and humid humors. 

But because Saturn is found in the second house, which signifies the neck, throat, <term>fistulas</term> <note>narrow, infected passages in the flesh</note>, and glands, I stated that he also suffers in these members. And because Saturn has the power to signify paralysis, <term>dropsy</term> <note>original: "idropisim"; swelling caused by excess fluid</note>, diarrhea, and gout, I said that the lord of the urine suffers from one of these ailments. Furthermore, because of the almuten’s presence in the ninth house, the lord of the urine will suffer an <term>obstruction</term> <note>original: "opilationem"</note> in the <term>chyme of the liver</term> <note>the semi-fluid mass of partly digested food</note> due to coldness and humidity.

**Fourthly, it should be noted.** The house of Saturn signifies that the thing feared will be caused by coldness and humidity, such as diarrhea or <term>consumption</term> <note>original: "ptisis"; a wasting disease of the lungs</note>, especially if it is in Capricorn. If it is in Aquarius, it will be due to coldness and "winds" <note>internal gases or vapors</note>. But the house of Jupiter—namely Sagittarius—indicates causes of heat and winds, such as <term>abscesses</term> <note>original: "apostemata"</note> and the like.

The house of Mars, such as Aries, will manifest more in the head; Scorpio will signify heat with humidity, and there will be suffering in the lower parts of the body.

The house of the Sun signifies causes of heat and dryness, and this is even stronger if the Sun is <term>afflicted</term> <note>original: "infortunatus"; weakened by a bad relationship with another planet</note> by Mars.

The house of Venus signifies causes related to medicines and poisons, and the outcome will be celebratory <note>original: "festiuum"; possibly meaning a successful recovery or an indulgence</note>. If it is in Taurus, the cause will be coldness and dryness, or caused by beasts. If it is in Libra, it is through heat and humidity, specifically regarding pains of the throat, especially if Venus is in Aries.

The house of Mercury, such as Gemini, signifies heat, humidity, liver pain, <term>delirium</term> <note>original: "frenesis"</note>, and loss of the senses. If it is in Virgo, it is due to the destruction of the liver, bile, and bowels.

If it is the house of the Moon, it is due to coldness and humidity; combine the planets that are associated with the Moon and judge accordingly. For if the associated planets agree with the aforementioned points, the judgment will be more certain, provided these aspects are also observed.

### BOOK THREE

...it is established: the place of Jupiter, Mars, and Venus, and the place of the <term>Lot of the Liver</term> <note>original: "locus partis hepatis"; an astrological point calculated by the distance between specific planets</note>, which is taken by day and night from Jupiter to Mars and projected from Venus. Once this is found, observe from which planet it is separated or which planet separates from it. For according to its state, so is the state and condition of the liver; similarly, according to its strength, so is the condition of the stomach. But if the <term>almuten</term> <note>the most mathematically powerful planet in a specific zodiacal location</note> of the liver stands alone, such that it separates from no one and no one from it, then judge the consistency of the entire body according to its own nature and the portion of its place, as shown by the almuten of the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>. If you have well understood the selection of the almuten of the ascendant, or the lord of the entire figure, you will understand these matters without need of an example.

And if you carefully examine the strength of the planets, or their <term>dignities</term> <note>the power a planet gains from its position in the zodiac</note> in the places of the liver, you will find:

And Venus is found separated from Jupiter by a <term>sextile</term> <note>a harmonious 60-degree angle</note> aspect along with the <term>Tail of the Dragon</term> <note>original: "cauda Draconis"; the South Node of the Moon, often associated with depletion or ill fortune</note>; thus, it portends some measure of indisposition of the liver by reason of heat and humidity. The lord of the place of the liver in a "hot and humid" sign indicates the same. Yet this indisposition will hardly be dangerous, owing to the kindness of the sextile aspect, as well as the naturally beneficial natures of Jupiter and Venus.

->**Sixth Point to be Noted: Concerning the contents of the urine.**<-

<margin>9</margin> The contents found in urine are judged according to the consistency of the liver. For if the <term>retentive faculty</term> <note>the body's ability to hold onto nutrients</note> is faltering, and the <term>expulsive faculty</term> <note>the body's ability to eliminate waste</note> is overpowering it, the contents of the <term>humors</term> <note>the four primary bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note> fall into the urine, and it appears excessively "cooked" (digested). Conversely, however, if the retentive faculty is strong and the expulsive faculty is faltering or weak, the urine is thinner and lacks sediment. If the <term>digestive faculty</term> <note>the body's ability to process food and heat</note> exceeds its natural heat, and the <term>separative faculty</term> <note>the ability to distinguish waste from nutrients</note> falters, the urine will be bluish-gray and turbid. But when the opposite happens, the urine will be temperate in color and clear in substance. We have already stated in the second treatise how these "faculties" are attributed to the planets. Whichever of these planets mixes itself most strongly in the place of the liver, its power shall prevail: if it is naturally <term>fortunate</term> <note>a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it acts according to nature; if it is <term>unfortunate</term> <note>a "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars</note> and corrupted, it acts unnaturally. But if none of these planets aspect the house of the liver, the power of the lord of the <term>term</term> <note>a specific sub-division of a zodiac sign</note> shall prevail. Thus, a comparison should be made between the almuten of the ascendant and the almuten of the fifth house, and between their powers, so that a discerning judgment may proceed through all things. However, this meticulous inquiry is published more for the healthy than for the sick.

<margin>10</margin> For in the case of the sick, the place of the liver—together with the mixture of the almuten, or the place of the liver alone if it lacks an almuten or planet—fully reveals the heat and substance of the urine according to the nature of that place.

### BOOK THREE

*Seventhly, it must be noted concerning the color and substance of urine more specifically.*

11 A further investigation occurs regarding the sequence of the color and <term>substance</term> <note>original: "substantia"; referring to the consistency or thickness of the urine</note> of urine according to the natures of the four <term>triplicities</term> <note>groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element: Fire, Air, Water, or Earth</note>, which naturally correspond to the <term>four humors</term> <note>the bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—believed to control health</note>. This is because, insofar as it is in the nature of the signs, the indication of the humors' essence remains naturally unchanged. For the actual mixing of these humors with one another, or the intensity of their qualities, will come from the planet that is in the "place of the liver" or which aspects it. I say "mixing" if it participates in the location in practice, or if it lacks testimony. Of the triplicities, the **fiery** corresponds to **cholera** <note>yellow bile</note>. The **airy** to **blood**. The **watery** to **phlegm**. The **earthy** to **melancholy** <note>black bile</note>. And according to this essence of the signs, the natural essence of the humors remains unchanged, as has been said.

Similarly, **Saturn** holds leadership over **melancholy**. **Jupiter** over **blood**, **Mars** with the **Sun** over **cholera**, the **Moon** with **Venus** over **phlegm**, and **Mercury** is mixed, according to its <term>application or separation</term> <note>astrological terms for when planets are moving toward or away from an aspect with each other</note> with others.

Here also, to weigh the color and substance of the urine, the present disposition of the body must be observed according to the natures of the signs and stars, as has been said, since the variation of color occurs primarily according to this. For example: 

12 If **Aries** is the place of the liver, and **Mars** is existing there or looking upon it <note>original: "aspiciens"; forming an astrological aspect</note>, the disposition of the body is a fever. The substance of the urine is moderate, due to the weakness of the <term>sequestrating</term> <note>filtering or separating</note> or segregating power in the liver; in color it is livid, or approaching blackness from **choleric combustion** <note>original: "adustione cholerica"; a condition where yellow bile is "burnt" by excessive heat, turning it dark and toxic</note>. If, however, the disposition of the body is healthy, the urine will be thin throughout, and reddish, or an intense lemon-yellow with a tendency toward fever.

13 If the place of the liver is **Capricorn**, and **Saturn** is existing there or looking upon it, the body is feverish, and the urine is livid with blackness from <term>mortification</term> <note>the "death" or decay of the humor's vitality due to extreme cold</note>, with a moderate substance from the mixing of thick humors, due to the weakness of the segregating power in the liver. But if the body is healthy, the urine will be thin, with a leaden color.

14 If the place of the liver is **Pisces**, and **Jupiter** is looking upon it from **Capricorn**, the disposition of the body will be a fever; that is, a mixing of cold blood (because of Capricorn) and phlegm (because of Pisces), which cause "sweet phlegm." In this case, the urine is moderately thick with a red color. If, however, the body is healthy, the urine will be somewhat yellow, or golden in color, with a moderate substance. If **Mars** were in that same place, "salty phlegm" would be produced through the mixing.

15 If it is the **Sun**, because of infection the color of the urine is reddish with a moderate substance. If it is the disposition of a sick person, it is yellowish approaching paleness; if healthy, it is in this manner according to the present disposition of the body and the natures of the signs and stars. One must search for which humor abounds, and the intensity or relaxation of its disposition, and then a comparison of all these factors against one another is required.

### Example regarding the color and substance of urine

The Moon is the <term>almuten</term> <note>original: "almutes"; the planet which holds the most astrological strength or "dignity" over a specific point in a horoscope</note>, as has been said. ## EXPLANATIONS.

**1** By conjectural foresight, and therefore not by necessity. <note>The author distinguishes between a probable prediction based on signs and a "necessary" or certain outcome.</note>
**2** You should cast the chart at the hour of the request; concerning this casting, it was spoken of above.
**3** You ask [this], but to understand this matter thoroughly, you must keep in your memory what the author taught in Chapter 8 of Book 1 regarding the <term>significance of the houses</term> <note>The twelve divisions of the sky in an astrological chart, each representing a different area of life such as health, wealth, or family</note>. And so you do not always have to look them up, commit to memory these verses written by <note>Valentino Naibod (1523–1593) was a German mathematician and astrologer</note> Valentin Naibod in his commentary on <note>Alcabitius was a famous 10th-century Arab astrologer whose work was a standard textbook in Europe</note> Alcabitius:

->*Life, wealth, brothers, father, children, and health.*<-
->*Spouse, death, and religion, kingdom, and benefactor.*<-
->*But the last house is to be feared, the house of prison.*<-

*The first house, therefore, signifies life and those things that happen by one's own nature. For this reason, if someone has brought their own urine, you should consider the first house for the person who carries the urine. However, if it was a brother or a relative, give him the third house; if a father, the fourth; if a son, the fifth; if a servant, the sixth; if either a spouse, a business partner, or the person who manages the sick person's trade, the seventh; if a client, the eighth; if a religious man or a wise man, the ninth; if a mother, or grandmother, or someone established in authority, the tenth; if a king's advisor or a great benefactor of the sick person, the eleventh; if a lowly person or a prostitute, give them the twelfth. For these persons are signified by the twelve houses, as in the first treatise. Furthermore, the fifth house from the house of the carrier of the urine will be the "house of the liver," from which—together with the house of the carrier—you will draw the judgment, as will become clear in what follows.*

**4** Secondly, <term>Almuten</term> <note>original: "Almutes"; a term derived from Arabic meaning the "winner" or "prevailer." It refers to the planet that holds the most influence over a specific degree of the zodiac</note> is interpreted as "conquering": for he is the one who has the most <term>dignities</term> <note>The "strength" a planet gains based on its specific position in the zodiac</note> in certain places, as the matter you seek requires. In this context, it is that planet which has the most of the five <term>essential dignities</term> <note>Five specific ways a planet can be "strong": House, Exaltation, Triplicity, Term, and Face</note> in the position of the Sun (☉), the Moon (☽), the <term>Horoscope</term> <note>The Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, and in the place of the <term>syzygy</term> <note>original: "præuentionis"; the point of the New or Full Moon that most recently preceded the day the urine was brought</note>—namely, the Sun and Moon—and in the houses of heaven. These things require much interpretation so that the matter becomes clearer and the reader may have a certain method by which to find the almuten of the urine's figure, since the heart of the matter depends almost entirely on this one thing. Therefore, as was said, first cast the chart. For example, a servant of a certain sick person brings urine on June 24th at three o'clock in the afternoon; the positions of the heavens for this hour from the <term>ephemeris</term> <note>A table showing the daily positions of celestial bodies</note> of <note>Giovanni Antonio Magini (1555–1617) was an Italian astronomer and cartographer</note> Magini is as follows:

Next, look in the first treatise for the <term>dignities</term> <note>Dignities are a scoring system in astrology where planets gain points for being in specific parts of the zodiac that they "rule"</note> of each planet in this manner: first, Saturn at 3° Cancer has no dignity, so I have written 0 in the shared column for Saturn and 3° Cancer. At 19° Capricorn, Saturn has its <term>domicile</term> <note>The sign where a planet is "at home," providing the highest score of 5 points</note>, which gives five dignities; therefore, I have recorded them. At 2° Scorpio, which is the <term>horoscopus</term> <note>The Ascendant or rising sign</note>, it has no dignity, so I wrote 0. At 18° Taurus, where the <term>Part of Fortune</term> is located, it has no dignity. At 2° Cancer, which is the place of the preceding <term>syzygy</term> <note>The most recent conjunction or opposition of the Sun and Moon</note>, it likewise has none. However, since it is in the fifth house, it has 7 dignities, as can be seen in chapter 8 of the first treatise in the table concerning the dignities of the houses. Therefore, Saturn has 12 dignities across all these places. The same must be done for the rest of the planets; if you do this diligently, you will find that Mars is the <term>Almuten</term> <note>The "winner" or most influential planet of the entire chart, also called the *Almutes*</note> of this figure.

<margin>5</margin> Thirdly, it should be noted that since Mars is the Almuten in this figure, one must see from what he is <term>separating</term>, or who is separating from him. Regarding the <term>separation</term> <note>When a planet moves away from an aspect or conjunction with another planet</note> of planets, the author spoke quite obscurely in chapter 7 of the first treatise, and even more obscurely in this place. For in our figure, no planet is separating from Mars, and he himself is separating from none; therefore, the rule is not universal. It seems our author here is speaking only of separation by body <note>Physical conjunction</note>, and not separation by <term>aspect</term> <note>Geometrical angles between planets, like a square or trine</note>. For if <term>application</term> <note>The movement of a planet toward an aspect</note> occurs both by body and by aspect, then separation—which is its opposite—must also be considered to occur by both body and aspect. Nevertheless, separation that occurs by body is always to be preferred over separation by aspect. 

However, so that you can perceive this separation, and indeed all the aspects of the planets, with your own eyes, it will be worthwhile to include here what <term>Valentin Naboth</term> <note>Valentinus Naibod (1523–1593), a German mathematician and astronomer</note> writes on this subject in his commentary on <term>Alcabitius</term> <note>Al-Qabisi, a famous 10th-century Arab astrologer</note>: draw about thirteen longitudinal lines, and in the spaces at the top, beginning with Aries, describe the twelve signs of the <term>zodiac</term> <note>original: *signiferi*, the "sign-bearer" or zodiac belt</note>. Afterward, draw seven transverse lines across the first ones, comprising seven spaces for the number of the seven planets. Finally, in the first and highest space, draw the symbol of that planet which has completed the fewest degrees of its sign, placing it under that sign in which the planet...

<margin>1</margin> The planet corrupting the <term>almuten</term>.
<margin>2</margin> The house of that same planet that is most clearly seen <note>aspected</note>.
<margin>3</margin> The house of the heavens in which the <term>almuten</term> resides.

The First House, in which the <term>almuten</term> Mars is located, declares the **foundation** of the disease—that is, the place in our body where the sickness resides.

One must also see if there is anything that badly affects the house of the urine-bearer <note>the person who brought the sample to the physician, often associated with the 6th house in medical astrology</note>, as in this figure it is Saturn <note>original: ♄</note>, who harms the 6th house with his rays. <margin>9. Contents in the urine</margin> The indicators of the urine are the location of the liver and the planets either joining that location bodily <note>conjunction</note> or looking at that location <note>aspecting</note>. If no such planet is present, the indicator is the "lord of the term" <note>the planet that rules the specific degree of the zodiac</note> in which the location of the liver is found. In our figure, Saturn and Venus <note>original: ♄ ♀</note> look upon the location of the liver by a trine <note>original: △; an aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered harmonious</note> aspect, platically <note>original: platicè; an aspect that is not exact by degree but within a functional range</note>. Venus <note>original: ♀</note>, however, since she is the lady of the term in which the liver is located, and she herself is weak (both by her dignity and her position in the figure, being in the eighth house), and since Venus is cold and moist, she will be a companion to the Moon <note>original: ☽</note>. The Moon presides over the expulsive power <note>the body's ability to eliminate waste</note>, and this part will also be weak. Mars <note>original: ♂</note> also perhaps looks too "platically" at the location of the liver; however, along with the Sun, by reason of dryness and heat, he can preside over the attractive power <note>the body's ability to draw in nourishment</note>. Since Mars is stronger than the others by reason of his position (being in the seventh house), the attractive power seems stronger than the expulsive and retentive powers. Therefore, the urine will be thinner and lacking in contents. For, as the author says:

> If the retentive power is weak,
> And the expulsive power is strong:
-> It causes there to be much of the humors in the urine, and it appears overly "cooked" <note>well-digested</note>. <-
> If the expulsive power is weak,
> And the retentive power is strong:
-> The urine is thinner and lacking in contents. <-
> If the digestive power exceeds by unnatural heat,
> And the separative power is weak:
-> The urine will be livid <note>bluish-gray</note> and turbid. <-
> If the separative power is strong,
> And the digestive power is weak:
-> The urine will be temperate in color and substance. <-

Because the location of the liver is stronger by its position in the tenth house of the figure (which is a stronger location for the liver than the ninth house, where the almuten of the liver is), the attractive power is therefore stronger. Thus, the urine in this manner will be thin and lacking in contents. And Mars <note>original: ♂</note>, the almuten of the ascendant, since he is in the seventh house...

# THE JUDGMENT OF THE URINE
->*once seen, you shall understand through the following things.*<-

The Second part begins regarding the judgment of the inspected urine, in which eight things to be considered occur. The first thing that occurs in the inspection of urine is the color; there are commonly twenty colors numbered according to the authors. Among these, the first is white, like the purest spring water. Black [is a sign] of mortification <note>tissue death or gangrene</note>, like a very black horn.

*   Black from adustion <note>original: adustione; the "scorching" or overheating of humors</note>, like ink. Milky, like the whey of milk. Glaucous <note>original: Glaucus; a pale blue-gray or sea-green</note>, like a clear white horn. Charopus <note>a grayish-amber or tawny color</note>, like the whitish fleece of a camel, and it is compared to the cloth called *camelot* in French [camlet], which is made partly of white and black, but more of white; it is also compared to the onyx stone.
*   Sub-pale <note>slightly pale</note>, like the broth of half-raw meat. Pale, having a little more bile. Reddish-gold <note>original: Ruffus</note>, like the purest gold. Sub-reddish-gold, like gold that has been cast and is a little impure.
*   Red, like Oriental saffron. Sub-red, like garden saffron. Ruddy <note>original: Rubicundus</note>, like an intense flame of fire; others call this color *Erythron* <note>Greek: ἐρυθρόν, meaning red</note>.

### BOOK

<meta>archival pencil mark 001 at top left; catchword: le</meta>

Slightly reddish, or *hyperytron* <note>original: hyperytron; a Greek-derived term for a reddish-orange hue</note>, like a low flame, or like the color of a date fruit. *Wine-dark* <note>original: Inopos</note>, like dark wine. *Deep blue* <note>original: Kyanos</note>, like the color of the liver, or like putrefied blood; others describe it as a purple color.

Green or *pale green* <note>original: chloron</note>, like a green cabbage stalk, or the juice of a leek.

Livid, or *leaden-gray* <note>original: pelidnon</note>, like lead, but appearing livid due to "burning" <note>an excess of internal heat scorching the humors</note> or mortification <note>tissue death</note>, resembling a dark, bruised horn; this is a fatal sign. *Citrine* <note>lemon-yellow</note> like the color of a citron fruit. *Sub-citrine* is the same, but a lighter shade.

Second, when judging urine, new students <note>original: tyrones; recruits or beginners</note> of the medical art should carefully observe whether it is the urine of a human or of another animal; for physicians are very often tested on this point <note>it was a common trick for patients to bring animal urine to a doctor to see if he could tell the difference</note>. Indeed, the closer human urine is brought to the eyes, the thicker it appears, and the further it is moved away, the clearer it becomes—this is not the case with other urines. For the urine of a donkey in a flask is like liquid butter, with a cloudiness and thickness appearing on the outside, leaning toward white. The urine of draft animals—beasts of burden that carry yokes, such as mules, horses, pack animals, and the like—resemble donkey urine in substance but tend toward a yellow color; in these urines, the top half of the flask appears clear, while the bottom half is cloudy. However, the urines of sheep are white, leaning toward yellow, and are similar to human urine, but they are always watery and thin, and their sediment is like oil or the dregs of pressed olives <note>original: amurca</note>.

Third, they should see whether the urine belongs to a man or a woman. For women's urines are thicker and whiter, and less "beautiful" <note>less clear or less ideally colored</note> than those of men. When men's urines are moved, they become cloudy, and this cloudiness rises to the top; they are usually quite turbulent. But women's urines are hardly clouded by motion, and they usually have a round foam upon their surface, and if they are cloudy, the turbulence will be slight.

There is a difference between the urines of women and of the elderly. Women's urines are clearer and more luminous than those of the elderly. The urine of the elderly is cruder and more leaden, because their natural heat is near extinction. When women reach old age, their natural heat is even weaker than that of elderly men, and their urines are less luminous and more leaden. But the urine of pregnant women from the first, second, and third months up to the sixth month (exclusive), is a pale yellow <note>original: citrina pallearis</note> leaning toward off-white; it is clear on the surface but has a "cloud" <note>original: nebulam; a suspended mass in the upper part of the flask</note> and in the middle a "tuft of carded wool" <note>original: cotum carminatum; a traditional uroscopic term for a specific cloudy sediment</note>, in which granules appear to rise and fall. But in the middle of pregnancy, around the sixth or seventh month, it will be like the water in which unskinned calf's feet <note>original: pedes vituli non excoriati</note> have been boiled. For when the menstrual blood is retained and the nature of the womb <note>original: matricis</note> is strong, it expels some of that retained blood through the pores; this mixes with the urine, causing such a color. But at the end of pregnancy, a redness appears in the flasks, especially when the flask is shaken.

### Fifth: How the complexion may be known by the inspection of urine.

<image-desc>A classification list mapping urine characteristics to humors and complexions. A large left-facing bracket groups five descriptions under the heading "Urine".</image-desc>

( **Temperate** in substance and color—that is, clear citrine, midway between citrine and a fiery color, and between a thick and heavy substance—indicates a temperate complexion <note>the 'complexion' was the specific mix of the four humors—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—that determined a person's health</note> in which none of the qualities exceeds the others.
( **Red** in color and **thick** in substance indicates a hot and moist complexion: **Sanguine**.
( **Red and thin** indicates a hot and dry complexion: **Choleric**.
( **White and thick** indicates a cold and moist complexion: **Phlegmatic**.
( **White and clear** indicates a cold and dry complexion: **Melancholic**.

And only the active qualities provide color to the urine, not the passive ones. For heat, by its presence, colors the urine. Coldness, however, when it is present, diminishes the color; heat provides redness, and cold provides whiteness. Similarly, moisture thickens the urine, while dryness makes it clear.

### Sixth: Following are the rules concerning the colors of urine, and first
->concerning the white color.<-

White urine that is clear and thin signifies an obstruction <term>oppilatio: a blockage in the body's channels</term>, particularly of the spleen; it also indicates a discoloration of the face, sleepiness, a sluggishness throughout the whole body, as well as heaviness and pain in the left side <note>The spleen is located on the left side of the abdomen; medieval doctors believed its blockage caused many of the symptoms listed here</note>.

White urine with a lead-colored circle in the upper part signifies an obstruction in the brain and epilepsy, arising from thick phlegmatic or melancholic matter <note>phlegm and melancholy were two of the four bodily humors</note>.

White and mucous-like urine indicates an abundance of humors that are cold, phlegmatic, thick, and raw <note>original: "crudorum," referring to humors that the body has not yet "cooked" or digested properly</note>.

White, semi-clear, and purulent urine <term>saniosa: containing "sanies," a thin, greenish-bloody discharge from a wound</term>, similar to the color of a mushroom, indicates ulceration in the kidneys and in the urinary tracts. Indeed, any purulent urine demonstrates either the bursting of an abscess <term>apostematis: an internal swelling or pocket of infection</term> or ulceration in the urinary tracts.

White and thin urine, somewhat livid <note>bluish or discolored</note> without pus, having the color of a mushroom, indicates a stone in the kidneys or bladder. White, thick, and oily urine throughout signifies a "hectic" fever <note>ethica: a wasting fever often associated with consumption or tuberculosis</note>. Oily urine in any illness is a bad sign; it signifies the dissolving and melting away of a stone.

White urine appearing in fevers after the urine has been lemon-yellow or deeply colored indicates the changing of the fever into a quartan fever <note>a fever that returns every fourth day, traditionally associated with the humor of black bile</note>. White urine that is lead-colored in some parts and has no sediment <term>hypostasis: the cloud of matter that settles at the bottom of a urine glass</term> signifies death.

White and thin urine with white, round particles like tiny specks signifies arthritis <note>original: "artheticam," referring to gout or joint pain</note>.

White and thick urine, livid on the surface with ashy particles settling with much stickiness, indicates a prolapse of the womb <note>original: "descensum matricis"</note> caused by phlegm that is slippery and heavy. White urine like milk in a diabetic patient signifies death.

White, thin urine passed in great quantities and frequently signifies diabetes.
White and fine urine in a patient with jaundice indicates future dropsy <note>hydropisim: an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</note>. White and fine urine in a "bad" fever <note>likely an acute or malignant fever</note>. White and fine urine with pain in the hips indicates an obstruction in the urinary tracts caused by thick phlegm; in a fever, it signifies an obstruction caused by thick bile. White urine accompanied by itching of the body and in the lower belly indicates that "sand" <note>gravel or tiny mineral deposits</note> will form in the bladder.

White and thick urine in mild fevers indicates distress and fear. White and thick urine without sediment is a cause for fear and is a bad sign. White and thick urine that is almost oily signifies death. White, thick, and cloudy urine like foam is the worst sign.

White urine having a cloud like snow signifies pain in the kidneys and a long duration of the disease. Foul-smelling white urine in fevers indicates a wandering of the mind <note>delirium</note>. White, thick urine that does not change over a long period indicates a future kidney stone. White, thin urine passed in small amounts signifies that something in the stomach cannot be digested.

Thick white urine signifies pain in the back of the head caused by phlegm, and a fever.

### BOOK FOUR

...fever, specifically a continuous fever arising from phlegm. White, thin, and abundant urine indicates the end of a fever. White with a certain bluish tint <note>original: "liuiditate"</note> indicates dropsy <term>hydropisim: a swelling caused by excess fluid in the body's tissues</term>.

White and subtle urine with sandy deposits <note>original: "arenosis resolutionibus"</note> signifies pain in the kidneys. Abundant white urine with fleshy deposits signifies diabetes <term>dyabeten: in the medieval view, a condition where the body's flesh "melts" and is passed through urine</term>. White and thin urine with black deposits signifies affections of the womb <note>original: "passionibus matricis"</note>. White urine at the beginning of an acute fever signifies the rawness of the matter, a weakness of the body's heat, and a long-lasting illness. In children, very white urine is a bad sign; if it is watery, it is the worst sign; in the elderly, it signifies a long-drawn-out sickness.

White and thin urine in a case of dropsy signifies recovery; however, in a burning fever <term>causonide: a high, "acute" fever</term>, it signifies a headache in the front of the head caused by heat, and sometimes a loss of reason or a nosebleed.

White and thin urine with small grains distinct in the upper circle <note>the "circle" or "crown" refers to the top layer of the urine in the flask</note> signifies arthritis or a "catarrh" <term>catarrum: a downward flow of humors, often from the head</term>. White, thin, and seemingly greenish urine with a lead-colored upper circle signifies epilepsy. White and moderately thin urine during a fever denotes lethargy <term>litargiam: a state of "sleepy" forgetfulness or coma</term>. White and moderately thick urine with a certain undigested lump signifies a daily fever caused by "glassy" phlegm <note>original: "phlegmate vitreo," a thick, clear type of phlegm resembling molten glass</note>.

In healthy people, white and thin urine signifies the drinking of much liquid with a large amount of food, especially if it was a weak wine. In the elderly, however, such urine signifies a weakness of the digestive power.

White and thin urine in a three-day fever <note>original: "tertiana"</note>, a burning fever, or similar scorching fevers signifies that a "frenzy" <note>a state of delirium or mental agitation</note> is coming.

White, milky, and thin urine at the start of fevers is a bad sign, as it signifies the long duration of the fever or illness. However, during the decline of the illness, if the urine is abundant, it signifies a resolution of the disease.

White and oily <note>original: "pinguis"</note> urine in acute illnesses relieves abscesses <term>apostemata: internal swellings or pockets of infection</term> that have formed in the joints; this applies to those who were in pain, those who were in a state of laborious sickness, or those who for a long time possessed an abundance of oily humors.

Milky and oily urine, if it appears at the end of an illness, signifies the formation of stones <term>litiasim: lithiasis</term> in the bladder or kidneys.

White urine, clear like water, signifies a failure of digestion and a weakness of the nutritional power, or an obstruction <term>opilationẽ: a blockage of the body's internal channels</term>, or both; it also signifies diabetes.

White urine that resembles semen signifies an abundance of cold, raw, phlegmatic humors; it usually predicts apoplexy <note>a sudden loss of consciousness or "stroke"</note> or a similar illness. Children have this urine when they are becoming epileptic, and it is most often a predictive sign.

White and subtle urine, or white and turbid urine, signifies the opposite of good digestion.

Milky urine in acute illnesses is deadly.

White urine in acute fevers—appearing after the urine had already been colored at the start of the fever—signifies that bile <note>original: "choloræ"</note> has been snatched away to some limb where an abscess is being generated, or it indicates a flux of the belly <note>diarrhea</note>, or it signifies that the bile has been snatched away to the head.

White, milky, thin, and scanty urine signifies a stone in the bladder.

### BOOK FOUR

Clear white urine indicates ulcers of the lungs, especially if it is abundant.

Thick, granular, and turbid white urine, occurring in small amounts, signifies a flux of the belly <term>fluxum ventris: a general term for diarrhea or dysentery</term>.

Turbid white urine, like that of beasts of burden <note>original: "subiugalium," referring to draft animals like oxen or horses</note>, signifies a piercing pain in the left side.

Urine similar to sour milk in an acute fever portends either a swift death or a sudden calming of the febrile heat and its intensity; however, if the urine becomes lighter, it signifies that the sick person will succumb to a "hectic" fever <term>ethicam: a chronic, wasting fever</term> or to phthisis <term>ptisim: a progressive wasting of the body, often tuberculosis</term>.

Foamy white urine signifies pain in the left side.

Milky, thick urine in small amounts—if it has thick scales at the bottom—signifies a stone; without scales, it signifies a flux of the belly.

->On black urine.<-

Abundant thin black urine in a quartan fever <term>quartana: a malarial fever where paroxysms occur every fourth day</term> resolves the fever.

A small amount of black urine surrounded by a certain mist, with a leaden color <note>original: "liuido"</note> appearing first, signifies the extinction of natural heat and death.

A small amount of shining black urine, appearing like horn and preceded by a greenish tint, signifies the ultimate "adustion" <term>adustionem: the "scorching" or over-cooking of bodily humors due to excessive heat</term>.

Abundant, thick black urine with black sediment at the bottom signifies the release of suppressed menstruation.

A small amount of foul-smelling, oily, or greasy black urine—if the kidneys and bladder are otherwise healthy—occurring during a continuous fever, signifies death.

Thick black urine in small amounts with sanious sediment <term>sedimine sanioso: a discharge containing a mix of blood and pus</term> signifies a ruptured abscess <term>apostematis: an internal swelling or pocket of infection</term> of the kidneys.

Thick, fatty black urine, very small in quantity with red sanious sediment, signifies a ruptured abscess of the bladder.

Abundant black urine on a "critical day" <note>the day a disease was expected to change for better or worse</note> having a hanging cloud or mist on the surface, or an enormous amount of sediment, signifies deafness of the ears or a future nosebleed. If good signs appear—such as the patient sleeping or eating—they will be recovered; if the signs are bad, they will die.

Black urine having yellow foam on the surface, mixed with leaden and black tones, signifies internal jaundice <term>icteritiam: a yellowing of the skin and eyes, here interpreted as being deep within the body</term>.

Black and thin urine in very acute fevers is a very bad sign, especially if there is little of it.

If black urine appears at the beginning of an illness alongside trembling symptoms and remains until the seventh day, but is then followed by healthy urine with white sediment <term>hypostasi: the deposit that settles at the bottom of a urine flask</term>, it indicates the decline of the disease and a return to health. But if it is not followed by a favorable sign, but rather by shortness of breath, sweating on the upper limbs, mental confusion <note>original: "alienatio mentis"</note>, and a loss of appetite, it signifies destruction and death.

In cases of suppressed menstruation, black urine without fever or other substances coloring the urine indicates the woman will soon be cured.

### BOOK FOUR

Black urine in a fever signifies a spasm caused by dryness. Black urine in very acute fevers, when accompanied by intense sweating of the head, neck, and back, and with sighing, signifies death.

Black urine in a large quantity that stains cloth signifies a "critical expulsion" <note>This refers to the body successfully purging harmful humors during a "crisis" or turning point in the illness</note> and is a very good sign.

Abundant black urine with black sediment <term>hypostasi: the medical term for sediment that settles at the bottom of a urine sample</term>, occurring on a critical day during an acute fever with a sharp odor and fine sediment, signifies a headache, a confusion of reason <note>original: "permixtionem rationis," referring to delirium or mental fog</note>, and a nosebleed on that critical day.

Black urine with a strong odor signifies inflammation in the "spiritual" organs <term>membris spiritualibus: the heart and lungs, which medieval doctors believed managed the body’s "vital spirit"</term>; in an acute fever, this sometimes signifies death.

Black urine preceded by a lemon-yellow color <note>original: "citrinitas"</note>, or mixed with yellow, signifies jaundice <term>ictericiam: a yellowing of the skin and eyes, here linked to bile</term>.

Black urine preceded by a dusky or tawny color <note>original: "fustedo"</note> signifies "black jaundice" or a condition of the spleen.

Black urine preceded by green, or leaning toward a greenish tint, denotes death.

Black urine in a woman, with dreggy matter resting at the bottom, signifies the actual flow of her menstrual period.

Abundant black urine that lacks any green tint, appearing during a "quartan" fever <term>quartana: a fever where the paroxysms return every fourth day, often associated with melancholy or the spleen</term> and accompanied by pains in the back and womb, is a sign of a return to health.

Thick black urine with round sediment, occurring with tension in the upper abdomen <term>hypocundriorum: the "hypochondria," the regions under the ribs</term>, or with persistent sweating, or an abscess in some part of the body, is a sign of death.

Thick, abundant black urine in women who have missed their periods signifies the flow of the menses, or that the sick woman is being purged through the urine.

Granular black urine that is thick at the bottom and clear at the top signifies the purging of the menses.

Blackness in the upper part of the urine during acute fevers, accompanied by deafness <note>original: "surditate capitis," literally "deafness of the head," a common symptom in severe medieval fever cases</term>, signifies a "crisis" or turning point marked by a nosebleed.

Black urine like dark blood in cases of pleurisy <term>pleuresi: an inflammation of the membranes surrounding the lungs</term> signifies death.

Black and thick urine in acute fevers signifies a spasm; if delirium is also present along with a loss of appetite, it signifies death.

Black and foul-smelling urine without pain in the bladder is fatal. Black urine is a good sign in cases of stones or kidney ailments arising from thick humors <note>In this context, it suggests the body is successfully passing the heavy matter causing the blockage</note>.

Black urine is also a bad sign in ailments of the kidneys and bladder when there is an intense burning sensation; for this signifies a cancer in those organs or malignant ulcers.

Black urine is not a good sign in the elderly of either sex.

Watery black urine signifies ruin <note>death or total loss of strength</note> in patients of all ages.

Very black urine in women, if it shows a slight redness when shaken, signifies the release of suppressed menstruation.

Black urine in very violent fevers containing small pieces of matter signifies death, especially if the quantity of urine is small.

And in summary: Black urine—that is, urine that is perfectly black—signifies either intense internal burning, or perhaps extreme cold, or death, or the [extinction] of natural heat...

## *Concerning the livid or lead-colored urine.*

Livid urine throughout the entire sample, in any illness, is a sign of death.

Urine that is somewhat livid and tending toward black, which was preceded by green urine, signifies death.

Urine in which there is a leaden or livid ring on the surface declares epilepsy.

Urine that is partially livid while there is swelling of the belly demonstrates a great dropsy <term>hydropisim: an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid accumulation, often related to heart or liver failure</term>.

Livid urine in a case of dropsy signifies a difficult cure.

It is possible for livid urine to appear in a "stomach fever" <note>likely referring to a fever accompanied by severe gastric distress or inflammation</note>.

Urine that is livid in the upper or middle part, with tiny, distinct, and separate granules, signifies either pleurisy <term>pleuresim: inflammation of the membranes surrounding the lungs</term> or pneumonia <term>peripleumoniam: a severe lung infection</term> in the "spiritual" organs <term>membris spiritualibus: the heart and lungs, which managed the body’s "vital spirit"</term>.

But if the granules are joined together, it argues for a condition of the kidneys and the liver.

And lest the physician be deceived if he sees this urine with tiny, separate granules, he ought to predict an abscess <term>apostema: an internal swelling or gathering of pus</term> of the chest, without limiting it specifically to pleurisy or pneumonia.

Livid urine persisting in pleurisy or pneumonia is a very bad and fatal sign.

A small amount of livid urine that is partially oily designates death in any illness.

A small amount of livid urine, frequently passed, signifies strangury <term>stranguiream: a condition where passing urine is painful, slow, and occurs in drops</term>.

Partially livid urine in a great or small "hemitritaeus" fever <term>emitriteo: a type of semitertian fever, historically associated with malaria</term> is dangerous.

Livid urine in "phthisis" <term>ptisi: a term for a wasting disease, usually pulmonary tuberculosis</term> is a fatal sign near to death.

Livid urine commonly appears in arthritic pains, especially in one whose rheum <term>reuma: a discharge or flow of "bad humors" believed to cause inflammation</term> descends from the upper part through the spinal marrow to the hip <note>original: "stiam," likely referring to the ischium or sciatic region</note> or to the knee.

Livid urine in which dissolved pieces appear signifies arthritic pain.

Livid urine occurs from a catarrhal flow <note>original: "fluxu catarrali," a discharge of fluid or mucus</note> to various parts of the body.

Livid urine arises from the restriction and blockage of the menses.

Livid urine in a "hectic" fever <term>febre ethica: a persistent, wasting fever often associated with consumption</term> signifies death.

Livid urine in palpitations of the heart <note>original: "tremore cordis," literally a trembling of the heart</note> argues that the condition is incurable.

Livid urine in "phrensy" <term>frenesi: a state of delirium or mental agitation believed to be caused by inflammation of the brain</term> is a sign of death.

Urine that is livid as far as the middle region, and then reddish or somewhat reddish, indicates...

...regarding abscesses of the lungs, sometimes a *karops* <note>original: "Karops"; a technical term in medieval uroscopy describing a specific turbid or variegated appearance</note> appears internally, especially in cases of pleurisy and pneumonia. In pleurisy, however, the urine appears red or reddish, and it is thick; if the hand is placed behind the vessel, the surface appears livid from the blood.

A small amount of livid urine with certain long "resolutions" <note>particles or streaks suspended in the liquid</note> signifies a minor semitertian fever <term>emitriteum: a fever that combines characteristics of both continuous and intermittent fevers</term>.

Livid urine with a granular ring indicates a defect of the lungs.

Thick livid urine signifies pain in the liver, provided that the pain is felt in the right side.

Intensely turbulent livid urine signifies a "flux of the belly" <note>diarrhea or dysentery</note>.

Thick livid urine with white, long resolutions signifies an abundance of phlegm, and pain is felt around the intestines.

Faint and thick livid urine, containing small livid bodies diffused throughout, signifies the retention of the menses.

Livid urine with bran-like scales <note>original: "furfuribus"</note> indicates pain in the bladder and around the pubic bone <note>original: "pectinem"</note>.

A small amount of livid urine, passed with great difficulty, signifies death.

->**Concerning red, sub-red, and reddish urine, etc.**<-

Reddish urine <note>original: "russa"</note>, like pure gold, which is moderately thin and uniform, signifies a healthy person. However, if such urine appears in a child, or in a phlegmatic old man or a woman, it signifies fever. In a child, it indicates a continuous fever; in the elderly or in a woman, a tertian fever <note>a fever that peaks every three days</note>. In the autumn, it indicates a quartan fever and injury to the liver.

Red urine during an acute fever is a good sign.

Red urine with a very white sediment <term>hypostasi: the "hypostasis" or sediment that settles at the bottom of a urine flask</term> signifies the breaking or resolution of the fever.

A small amount of thin red urine is a very bad sign.

A small amount of red urine with black, turbid sediment is mortal.

Pure red urine, in small quantities, signifies death in cases of dropsy.

Red urine that looks like blood in acute fevers signifies sudden death.

Reddish urine that is white in the upper third signifies headache and alienation of the mind <note>delirium or loss of mental faculty</note>.

Red urine accompanied by greenish <note>original: "eriginosa"</note> vomit, a rough tongue, and red color signifies death.

A small amount of reddish urine in a case of jaundice <term>icteritia: yellowing of the skin and eyes, which physicians diagnosed via the urine's depth of color</term> signifies the resolution of the disease.

Urine that is reddish throughout its substance, thick, and has a livid, granular ring, signifies an abscess in the groin or the genital members.

Urine that is reddish both at the top and the bottom, thick, and which appears livid and oily on the surface when a hand is placed behind it, and contains hair-like filaments <note>original: "crinoidibus"</note>, signifies "hectic" fever <term>ethicam: a wasting disease or consumption, often associated with tuberculosis</term>.

Thin red urine that appears oily signifies arthritic pain and alienation of the mind.

Foul-smelling red urine with a black and turbid sediment, or containing hair-like particles or oiliness, is very bad and mortal.

Red urine in a case of ileus <note>original: "hylcon"; a painful intestinal obstruction</note> or the "iliac passion" is very bad.

Red urine without any sediment is a bad sign.
