# BOOK

<meta>catchword: Reddish-</meta>

Thick red urine in an acute fever signifies a headache, as well as heaviness in the hypochondria <note>the upper abdomen, below the ribs</note> and the <margin>neck</margin>.

Urine that is red like blood, or like dark wine, without headache, is a sign of a laborious condition; if it remains in that quality, a stone will form in the bladder.

Red urine, resembling the color of blood but small in quantity and thin, is a bad sign, especially in cases of sciatica.

Red urine like the color of blood in an acute fever, accompanied by tremors of the body and pain in the right hypochondrium, is fatal.

If someone passes much blood suddenly, they have a ruptured vein in the kidneys, or in the liver, or it is due to the menses.

Red urine having the appearance of wine but tending toward black indicates a release from illness in the elderly; however, if such urine is produced at the end of a sickness, it indicates that the humors are being converted into stones <note>original: "calculosos humores"; the formation of kidney or bladder stones</note>.

A sub-reddish color similar to blood, having a thick substance, indicates a long duration of illness.

Rose-colored urine signifies "white bile" <note>an interpretation of a specific humoral imbalance</note>; if it has a black cloud in the middle, it is a lethal sign; but if the cloud is not black, it indicates "toasted" <note>original: "tostam"; scorched or overly heated</note> bile in the body.

Thick red urine signifies a synochal fever <term>synocham: a continuous, non-intermitting fever</term> and a tertian fever <note>a fever that peaks every third day</note>; if it is livid, it signifies a quotidian fever <note>a fever that peaks every day</note>.

Clear red urine in large amounts signifies heat in the lungs.

Thick and turbid red urine indicates the onset of a stinging pain in the right side.

Red urine that stains a cloth dipped into it signifies jaundice <note>original: "ictericiam"</note>; the redder and more staining it is—to the point that the stain can hardly be removed from the cloth—the healthier the patient is in their jaundice, for it indicates the sickness is leaving them. But when the urine is white with little redness during jaundice, it indicates future dropsy <note>edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</note>.

Reddish urine <note>original: "ruffa"</note> resembling the foam of wine indicates an alienation of the mind <note>delirium or mental confusion</note>.

Reddish urine with a black sediment <note>original: "hypostasi"</note> is a bad sign in those with splenic disorders.

Red urine in kidney ailments that remains red signifies a "hot abscess" <note>original: "apostema calidum"</note>.

Red urine like a rose signifies an ephemeral <note>one-day</note> fever; but if it is passed continuously, it signifies a quotidian fever.

Reddish or sub-reddish urine having round, white "resolutions" <note>suspended particles</note> at the bottom and appearing somewhat oily on the surface signifies a hectic fever <term>ethicam febrem: a wasting fever often associated with consumption</term>.

Clear sub-red urine that is foamy signifies a greater pain in the right side than in the left.

Reddish or sub-reddish urine that is thick throughout and appears livid when a hand is placed behind the vessel indicates—if occurring shortly before—pneumonia or pleurisy; or a quotidian fever caused by "sweet phlegm" with rheum; or gout from a hot cause; or dropsy <note>original: "astliten," likely a corruption of "asciten"</note>.

Red or sub-red urine, distinctly livid when the hand is applied, indicates pleurisy.

# BOOK FOUR

Reddish or somewhat reddish urine, thin in its substance throughout and liquid like fire, and accompanied by foam, signifies a burning fever <term>causon: a high, inflammatory fever often associated with severe dehydration</term>. If such urine is thick throughout and not lead-colored, it signifies a continuous fever <term>synocha: a non-intermittent fever believed to be caused by an excess of blood</term>; but if it is moderately thin, it signifies a burning fever, and if it is moderately thick, it signifies a continuous fever.

Reddish urine appearing with a haze <note>original: "nebula"; a cloud-like suspension in the fluid</note> signifies mental alienation <note>delirium or loss of reason</note>.

Red urine, like purple or the color of liver, thick and more turbulent at the bottom and full of dregs with certain black bodies, signifies a flow of hemorrhoids or of the menses.

Red urine persisting in acute illnesses, which produces no sediment <note>original: "residentiam"; the material that settles at the bottom of the flask</note>, signifies the death of the sick person or a hot abscess <term>apostema: an internal swelling or pocket of infection</term>.

Red urine in cases of headache signifies delirium.

Thick, turbid red urine signifies an abscess in the liver or its weakness.

Red urine in:
- Spasm
- Apoplexy
- Epilepsy
- Paralysis or Phthisis <note>a wasting disease, usually tuberculosis</note>
- Pneumonia
- Dysentery
- Colic
...signifies, for the most part, death.

The color:
- Rose-red, or rosy, is a color mixed with a little redness like a rose.
- Dark red is similar to venous blood.
- Dusty red, which on the surface seems to have a certain blackness.
...all three of these colors signify a dominance of blood.

### On citron and sub-citron urine.

Sub-citron <note>a pale, lemon-yellow color</note> urine, close to paleness and thin throughout, signifies that natural melancholy <note>one of the four humors, associated with the earth element</note> is abundant.

Sub-citron thin urine, and slightly "inflamed" <note>original: "incensa"; referring to a deeper, more intense heat in the color</note>, signifies that bile is abundant.

Sub-citron urine, thick throughout, signifies a daily fever caused by phlegm.

Sub-citron urine, moderately thin but tending toward a medium consistency, signifies a daily fever from acidic and undigested phlegm.

Sub-citron urine, moderately thin but tending more toward thinness, signifies that "vitelline" bile <note>original: "choleram vitellinam"; bile resembling the color of egg yolks</note> is abundant. If it is intensely "inflamed," it indicates a tertian fever <note>a fever that peaks every third day</note> arising from vitelline bile. In children, this signifies a double or minor semitertian fever <term>hemitritæus: a complex fever combining characteristics of both continuous and intermittent types</term>. In a woman, an old man, or those of a melancholic or phlegmatic temperament, it signifies a simple daily fever.

Somewhat citron with saffron-colored foam signifies saffron-colored jaundice <term>icteritia: a yellowing of the skin or eyes, known today as jaundice</term>.

Thin citron with a dark substance signifies fainting in women.

Citron with a citron circle, and similarly somewhat citron, is a healthy sign.

Thin citron, and even thinner in the upper part, especially with bubbles and grains, signifies a defect of the chest, tightness of the breast, and a certain progression toward a wasting disease <term>phthisis: a progressive wasting of the body, historically associated with tuberculosis</term>.

Citron or somewhat citron, very clear, streaked, and patchy <note>original: "fenestrata" (windowed); likely referring to areas of transparency within the fluid</note> signifies a disorder of the spleen, joint pain, or growths <term>condylomas: wart-like growths or swellings</term> and hemorrhoids. And if it is large in quantity along with thirst, wasting of the body, and constipation of the bowels, it signifies a hot imbalance of the liver.

Thin citron appearing at the start of an acute fever signifies the rawness of the matter <note>medical theory suggests "raw" humors have not yet been "cooked" or processed by the body’s heat</note>, a long duration of the disease, and a lack of strength; if such urine appears in the middle of a disease, or at the end following red or reddish urine, it signifies delirium <term>phrenitis: an acute inflammation of the brain or its membranes</term>. But if a "critical purging" <note>a sudden, beneficial discharge of fluids believed to signal the turning point of an illness</note> preceded it, it indicates recovery and the decline of the disease.

Subtle citron in healthy bodies is a good sign, but in the sick, it is a poor sign.

Thin citron and very clear notes pain in the spleen.

Thin and abundant citron indicates constipation and pain in the liver.

Clear citron urine, undigested, signifies illness, and a failure of the patient's strength is to be feared.

### *On pale and somewhat pale urine.*

Pale urine signifies a defect of the stomach and an obstruction of the "second digestion" <note>In medieval medicine, the first digestion occurred in the stomach and the second in the liver</note>.

Thin and clear pale urine signifies acidic phlegm.

Urine that is pale at the bottom signifies kidney pain in men, and in women, a defect of the womb.

Pale or somewhat pale and thick throughout signifies an abundance of phlegm, but if it is thin, it signifies melancholy without fever.

Moderately thick pale urine signifies "digested" acidic phlegm.

Thin pale urine, however, signifies the indigestion of acidic phlegm.

Pale and thick throughout during an acute fever signifies lethargy <note>a state of comatose sleepiness</note>. 

But if it appears over a long time without fever, it precedes dropsy <term>hydrops: an accumulation of fluid in the body's tissues or cavities</term> caused by phlegm.

Pale or somewhat pale with other good signs in an acute fever signifies an abscess beneath the diaphragm.

Pale or somewhat citron, foamy at the top, with a certain oily-blue, leaden, or ashen color and small in quantity, signifies a looseness of the bowels; if localized, it signifies a wasting disease. If a flow of the bowels <note>severe diarrhea</note> follows, it signifies death.

### On milky urine, and urine of a thick substance.

Milky, thick urine that is passed in small amounts signifies a stone <term>calculus: a hard mineral deposit, such as a kidney or bladder stone</term> in the bladder or kidneys.

Milky urine appearing at the onset of an acute fever indicates either death or life; if good signs appear, such as restful sleep and good respiration, it signifies life; if the opposite, death.

Milky or amber-colored <term>caropos: a Greek-derived term (charopos) used in uroscopy to describe a pale yellow or sea-gray color</term> urine with a thick substance, if it has been turbid for a long time and appears bluish when a hand is placed behind the vessel, signifies dropsy <term>hydropisis: an old term for edema, or the swelling of soft tissues due to the accumulation of excess water</term>.

Milky or amber-colored thick urine without small grains of "sand" signifies colic <term>cholica: severe abdominal pain</term> and intestinal obstruction <term>iliaca passio: a painful blockage of the intestines, often called ileus</term> arising from raw and viscous phlegmatic humors, from which a twisting sensation is felt around the intestines.

Milky thick urine, if there are small grains of sand at the bottom, indicates a stone.

Milky thick urine signifies a headache caused by phlegmatic humors ascending into the brain.

Amber-colored urine signifies a multitude of corrupt humors, as occurs in those who are phlegmatic, dropsical, gouty, or suffering from similar conditions.

### On wine-colored and dark-blue urine.

The color "wine-colored" <note>original: "inops"; a Latinization of the Greek "oinops," meaning wine-colored or wine-dark</note> is a color like wine that verges toward blackness, such as Italian wine or that which is brought from Calabria. "Dark-blue" <note>original: "Kyanos"; the Greek word for a deep blue or black</note>, however, has a deeper blackness and even multiple colors, as it appears reddish in one part, black in another, and livid or green in another. Wine-colored urine—like wine that is dark and turbid at the bottom, and appears red or reddish with a certain yellowish lividity at the top—signifies a dark abscess of the liver or kidneys.

Wine-colored urine in acute fevers, especially in burning fevers <term>causonide: from the Greek "causos," a high, parching fever</term>, signifies great internal burning and sometimes approaching death.

Dark-blue urine appearing after lemon-colored urine signifies a rupture of a vein in the kidneys or the liver, in both men and women.

Dark-blue urine in healthy men indicates that the labor of travel or much running has been performed. If, however, it appears in an elderly person and persists for a long time, it signifies the formation of stones <term>lithiasis: the clinical term for the formation of stony concretions in the body</term>. If the urine first appears reddish and then becomes wine-colored or dark-blue, it is a very bad sign and an indicator of death. Such urine is also prone to appear in women without fever due to the onset of menstruation, and then it is thicker, fatty, and dreggy at the bottom.

These urines usually appear during a rupture of the "hollow vein" <term>vena chilis: the vena cava, the large vein carrying deoxygenated blood into the heart</term>, which causes the greatest pain to be felt in the seventh vertebra <note>original: "spondili"</note> due to a change occurring in the lower part, and then the urine appears more turbulent at the bottom.

# BOOK [FOURTH]

Wine-colored <note>original: "Inops," from the Greek *oinoops*, meaning wine-colored.</note> and dark blue <note>original: "Kyanos," meaning a deep, leaden blue.</note> urine, if it appears thicker in the middle region, signifies dropsy <term>hydropisis: swelling caused by excess fluid</term>. If it is red and bloody, it signifies "under-flesh" dropsy <term>hyposarcha: a type of edema where fluid accumulates under the skin</term>; if it is more leaden in color, it signifies "white-phlegm" swelling <term>leucophlegmasia: a pale, flabby swelling associated with an excess of phlegm</term>.

Wine-colored and dark blue urine also indicates an abscess of the liver, pleurisy, pneumonia, and an abscess of the kidneys.

Wine-colored urine having excessive saffron-colored foam signifies an over-heating of the liver, or jaundice. If this occurs before the seventh day during an acute fever, it is a very bad sign; but if it appears after the seventh day, it indicates a resolution of the disease.

Wine-colored urine in a burning fever <term>causone: a high, inflammatory fever</term> indicates a crisis <note>The "crisis" was the turning point in an illness where the patient would either begin to recover or succumb.</note> occurring through a nosebleed accompanied by a headache.

->On the color green.<-

Green urine mixed with red, appearing after red urine, signifies "adustion" <term>adustio: the "scorching" or overheating of humors, thought to make them toxic</term> and is fatal.
Green urine in an infant announces paralysis or a spasm.
Green urine throughout the course of an acute fever indicates death.
Green urine similar to the color of those with wasting disease <term>phthisis: a term usually referring to tuberculosis or similar pulmonary consumption</term> signifies the mortification of the body's natural heat and indicates excessive coldness.
Green urine similar to leek juice is a very bad sign: for it signifies an "ignition" <note>an internal burning or inflammation</note> in the vital organs <term>membris spiritualibus: the heart and lungs, which medieval doctors believed managed the "spirit" or breath of life</term>.
Green urine similar to the rust of copper <note>verdigris</note> is worse than the others and indicates ruin.
Green urine similar to the color of an iris flower, preceded by other green urine, signifies a violent cooling that suffocates the natural heat, and is consequently an evil sign.
Green urine, when accompanied by persistent pain and distress in the stomach without any sediment <term>hypostasi: the material that settles at the bottom of a urine sample</term>, signifies that the person has taken poison in a drink, and consequently indicates death.
Green urine with a green circle in a case of "phrensy" <term>frenesi: an inflammation of the brain or its membranes causing delirium</term> is a most desperate sign of death.
Green urine appearing on a "critical day," if the patient suffers from a headache, announces the resolution of the pain.
Green or bran-like <note>original: "furfurea," meaning containing scaly particles like bran</note> urine during the heat of a fever—if the patient has become thin, has sweated on the upper parts of the body, and has grown cold in the extremities—signifies a terrible spasm and exhaustion.
Thick green urine signifies strangury <term>stranguirea: painful, drop-by-drop urination</term>. A small amount of green urine notes death.
Copious green urine, heavy and foul-smelling, signifies the rupture of an abscess, perhaps in the liver.
Smelly green urine signifies jaundice arising from leek-green bile.

# BOOK [FOURTH]

The second circle is red, representing the sanguine humor <note>blood</note>. The third is lemon-yellow <note>original: *citrinus*</note>, representing the choleric humor <note>yellow bile</note>. The fourth, the upper one, represents the phlegmatic humor. If these circles have a different position or order, or if they have changed colors, it signifies various and long-lasting illnesses. This circle in the upper region of the urine signifies the condition of the head. Sometimes a circle appears in the middle region of the urine, though rarely, and this signifies the condition of the "spiritual members" <term>membra spiritualia: the organs of the chest, such as the heart and lungs, responsible for the vital spirits</term>.

A thick, dilated, and watery circle foretells pain in the back of the head caused by phlegm.

A reddish and thick circle indicates pain in the front of the head from a sanguineous constitution.

A thin white circle indicates pain in the left side of the head from a melancholic constitution, that is, from coldness and dryness.

A red and slender circle indicates pain in the right side of the head from a choleric constitution.

A lead-colored circle, heavy in substance, denotes epilepsy or apoplexy <term>apoplexia: a sudden loss of consciousness, often a stroke</term>.

A livid <note>bluish or leaden-gray</note> circle signifies that the brain is damaged; and if, during an illness, this lividity changes to redness and clarity, it designates recovery <note>original: *convalescentiam*</note> and a change from death to life.

A green and thin circle in an acute fever signifies "adustion" <term>adustio: the "scorching" or overheating of the humors, making them toxic</term> and frenzy.

A trembling circle, when shaken by physicians, signals pain in the spine and paralysis, or a catarrhal discharge <term>catarrh: a flow of humors from the head into the body</term>.

A black circle signifies death <note>original: *mortificationem*</note> or adustion; it signifies death if lividity preceded it, and adustion when greenness preceded it.

Circle {
*   **Thick white:** designates that phlegm dominates the back of the head, along with coldness of the head.
*   **Red and thick:** signifies that blood dominates the front of the head.
*   **Lemon-yellow or red, and thin:** signifies a fault of red bile <note>red choler</note> in the right side of the head.
*   **Black or pale, with thinness and light substance:** portends pain in the left side of the head.
}

->### On bubbles and foam.<-

A bubble <note>original: *ampulla*</note> that persists for a long time indicates "windiness" <term>ventositas: gas or vapors trapped in the body</term>, indigestion, a "crudity" of matter, the long duration of a disease, kidney affliction <term>nephreticam passionem</term>, and headache due to windiness.

Continuous foam signifies a mastery of windiness, violent heat, and an inflammation <note>original: *incensionem*</note> of the liver.

# BOOK [FOURTH]

Black, broken foam indicates black jaundice caused by the melancholic humor.
Black foam that is not broken indicates scorched melancholy <term>melancholiam adustam: a pathological state where the humors are overheated or "burnt," leading to severe illness or depression</term>.
Broken foam with tiny grains signifies an abundance of rheum <term>rheuma: a flow of excess watery humors, often associated with inflammation or catarrh</term>.
Broken foam that is green or similar to the color of saffron indicates the heating and scorching of the liver.
Black foam signifies severe jaundice arising from melancholy.
Saffron-colored foam indicates jaundice from red choler <note>yellow bile</note>.
Green foam indicates an inflammation of the liver.
By "ampules" <note>original: *ampullas*</note> are understood large bubbles. And "grains" <note>original: *granula*</note> are medium-sized bubbles.
Bubbles floating on top of the urine signify kidney disease and a long-lasting illness.
A large bubble signifies that rumbling and heaviness of the stomach, vomiting, or a flux of the belly <note>diarrhea</note> has preceded.
A large bubble signifies heaviness of the stomach, pain, ileus <term>ileos: a painful blockage of the intestines</term>, or a condition of the kidneys caused by a thick and viscous phlegmatic humor.

### *On grains or medium-sized bubbles.*

Grains, in whatever region of the urine they may be found, always indicate that rheumatic matter is flowing from the brain, especially if they persist in the urine for a long time. These grains are like broken foam, separated and divided into various particles within the circle <note>the ring at the top of the urine sample</note>.
Grains in the upper region of the urine signify a headache caused by rheum, particularly if the urine is moved and the grains descend, but after the movement they rise again to the upper or highest region without spreading out.
Grains in the middle region signify the descent of rheum to the nerves, the feet, and the joints, though this rarely occurs.

Small grains indicate a rheumatic condition.
Grains at the bottom of the urine in a woman's urine indicate conception <note>pregnancy</note>: if they are red, it is a male; if white, a female; however, if they are rough and the urine is cloudy, they indicate rheum.

### *On the cloudiness of the urine*

A "little cloud" <note>original: *nubecula*</note> is a certain foamy and vaporous excess, appearing dark in the urine like a spider’s web or like dust scattered through the liquid.
A lead-colored cloud appearing in the lower region like scattered dust signifies the beginning of "hectic" consumption <term>ethica: a wasting disease or persistent fever, often associated with tuberculosis</term>.

->[BOOK] FOURTH<-

A shadowy little cloud <note>original: *nubecula*</note> accompanied by a certain saffron or green foam signifies overheating of the liver and an abundance of bile <note>original: *cholerae*</note>.
A little cloud always signifies a lack of balance <term>distemperantia: a disruption of the body's healthy "temperament" or balance of humors</term> in the respiratory organs <note>original: *membrorum spiritualium*, the organs of the "vital spirit" like the heart and lungs</note>.
A mist <note>original: *nebula*</note> hanging in the urine, if white, is a good sign; if black, it is bad.
A thickness, like a spider’s web floating on top of the urine, is an evil sign.

### *On pus in the urine.*

A small amount of pus <note>original: *sanies*</note> in the urine, while pain exists around the kidneys, signifies an abscess <term>apostema: an internal swelling or collection of pus</term> of the kidneys or an ulceration.
Much pus with a heavy and strong stench, while there is pain in the chest <note>likely referring here to the lower torso or pelvic cavity given the context of the bladder</note>, signifies an abscess or ulceration of the bladder.
Much purulent matter with pain in the pubic region <note>original: *pectine*</note> signifies an abscess in the womb.
Purulent urine with pain and throbbing in the right side below the ribs <note>original: *hypocundrio dextro*</note> signifies that an abscess of the liver has ruptured.
Purulent matter in a patient with pleurisy or empyema <term>empima: a collection of pus in the space between the lung and the chest wall</term>, when foam has decreased and bad symptoms have lessened, signifies that the pleurisy or empyema is being resolved through the urinary passages.
Pus mixed with moisture in the urine along with red contents, when the urine passes without difficulty, indicates an ulcer in the kidneys.
Pus separated from the urine, settling at the bottom with white contents, when the urine passes with difficulty, signifies an ulcer of the bladder.

### *On fatty and oily urine.*

By "fatness" is understood a certain fatty and oily matter dissolved from the organs, which is discharged with the urine.
Fatty and oily urine during fevers signifies the wasting away <note>original: *dissolutionem*</note> of the entire body; but without fever, it signifies the breaking down of the kidneys, the bladder, and the loins.
Fatty urine that is broken up and distinct in parts on the surface, looking like the fat on meat broth that is not very thick and has no sediment, indicates the first stage of hectic fever <term>ethicae febris: a chronic, wasting fever often associated with consumption or tuberculosis</term>.
Fat covering the entire surface of the urine, like a spider’s web with moderate sediment, notes the second stage of hectic fever. If the fat is spread out and sounds like oil when poured onto stone, it signifies the third stage of hectic fever; this urine is the worst of all.
Oily urine that is small in quantity and foul-smelling signifies death.
Oily urine appearing throughout acute illnesses on the fourth day signifies the patient will die on the seventh day.
A small amount of oily urine, in which there is something resembling the washings of fresh meat, is a most evil sign.
Oily urine in cases of colic and dropsy <term>hydropisi: an old term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid</term> signifies that death is near.

->*On raw humor in the urine.*<-

Raw humor <note>original: *humor crudus*, referring to undigested or improperly processed bodily fluids</note> in the urine is recognized in this way: it commonly presents the appearance of a sediment <term>hypostasis: the solid matter that settles at the bottom of a urine sample</term> located in the lowest part of the urine.

If the urine is shaken and breaks down into certain fine, atom-like particles <note>original: *athomofas resolutiones*</note>, and the raw humor is dispersed, its presence is then confirmed.

If such humor occupies the upper region of the urine, it indicates a defect of the chest and a compression of the respiratory organs <note>original: *spiritualium membrorum*, the organs of the "vital spirit," primarily the heart and lungs</note> by the diaphragm; from this, asthma and difficulty breathing <term>dyspnia: shortness of breath</term>, the coughing up of blood <term>emoptoica: hemoptysis</term>, and arthritic suffering <note>original: *arthetica passio*</note> or orthopnea <term>orthopnæa: a condition where a person must sit upright to breathe comfortably</term> are revealed.

If it occupies the middle region, it reveals a defect of the stomach caused by a fullness of excess humors, as well as vomiting, bloating of the belly, and the rumbling of the intestines.

If the humor occupies the lowest region, it signifies pain in the kidneys, the loins, and the generative organs, as well as straining <term>tenesmum: a distressing but ineffectual urge to evacuate the bowels or bladder</term>, kidney inflammation <term>nephritim</term>, painful urination <term>stranguram: strangury, where urine is passed painfully and in drops</term>, and pain in the shins and knees.

->*On blood in the urine.*<-

If pure blood appears in the urine and pain is felt around the right side under the ribs <note>original: *hypocondrium*</note>, it comes from the liver. If it comes from the bladder, the blood is clotted <note>original: *trumbosus*</note>, has a heavy odor, and pain is felt around the pubic region <note>original: *pectinem*</note>.

If it proceeds from the large vein <note>original: *chili*, referring to the vena cava</note> and is pure and abundant, pain is felt in the seventh vertebra, counting from the bottom.

Thick, clotted blood in the urine that sinks to the bottom indicates the actual flow of the menses in a woman, provided no other part of the body is in pain.

Black blood at the bottom, accompanied by a reduction of pain in the kidneys, indicates that the blood is flowing from the kidneys themselves.

Blood appearing in the urine for a long time is a very bad sign, as it signifies "deceitful" <note>likely meaning persistent or malignant</note> ulcers in the body.

Urine that resembles blood, or urine with much sediment and dregs <note>original: *fece*</note> appearing during the decline of a disease of the spleen, is a good sign.

Not every urine containing blood is to be called bad, for sometimes such urine occurs by way of a crisis <term>crisis: a sudden change in the course of a disease, leading to recovery or death</term>.

Whoever urinates blood voluntarily <note>i.e., without external injury</note>, for these a rupture of a vein in the kidneys is indicated.

Blood mixed [in urine] without the opening of veins during acute blood-related diseases, such as in continuous fevers <term>synochis: a fever that remains constant without relief</term>, signifies a superfluous excess of blood.

->*On small grains of sand in the urine.*<-

Red, hard grains of sand appearing without fever and with pain in the back denote a stone in the kidneys, either fully formed or currently forming.

Red, hard grains with relief of the kidneys or loins [signify] the dissolution

White and hard grains <note>original: *arenulæ*, small sand-like particles</note> settling at the bottom, accompanied by pain in the pubic region <note>original: *pectine*</note>, indicate a stone in the bladder.

Red and soft sand comes from the kidneys. White sand comes from the bladder. In the kidneys, they say this produces nephritis <term>nephritim: inflammation of the kidney</term>, and in the bladder, lithiasis <term>lithiasim: the medical condition of forming stones</term>.

Red, soft grains appearing with a fever, and especially at the end of a fever, signify the scorching <note>original: *adustionem*, a state where humors were thought to be "burnt" or thickened by excess internal heat</note> of the humors.

Red grains appearing without pain or a sense of heaviness in the kidneys indicate heat in the liver and the kidneys.

Grains at the end of choleric fevers <term>febris cholerica: a fever attributed to an excess of yellow bile</term> signify a transition or mixing of the choleric fever into a quartan fever <term>quartanam: a fever that recurs every fourth day, often associated with "black bile"</term>.

Do not always be terrified when you see small grains, nor should you immediately judge it to be a stone, because sometimes grains are caused by arthritis <note>original: *arthetica*</note>, or by a long-lasting quartan fever, or by medicine that is too sharp; in such cases, the grains should be soft and not hard. This also occurs in double or simple tertian fevers <note>recurring every third day</note>, where red grains are sometimes accustomed to appear because of a disorder <term>distrasiam: dyscrasia, an imbalance of the bodily humors</term> of the feverish heat.

### On Hairs in the Urine.

It should be noted that hairs <note>original: *pili*, referring to hair-like filaments or "shreds" found in a urine sample</note> are not made from the actual substance of the kidneys, but are caused by thick, viscous, and cold humors; some, however, are caused by extreme heat acting upon the body's moisture.

Red or yellow hairs in any region of the urine, when no fever is present, signify heat in the kidneys.

Oily hairs of a solid substance appearing without fever denote a breaking down <note>original: *dissolutionem*</note> of the kidneys and the loins.

Hairs that are thick in substance, but which vanish if squeezed or dissolve when the urine is shaken, indicate a blockage <term>opilationem: an internal obstruction or clogging of the "vessels"</term> caused by thick and viscous humors.

Solid hairs appearing in urine that looks oily during a fever signify a total breakdown of the body and consumption <term>ethicam: hectic fever, a wasting condition often associated with tuberculosis</term>, as well as a long-lasting and chronic suffering.

### On Scales, Bran, and Barley-like Sediments.

Scales <note>original: *squamæ*</note> are broad and round fragments that are torn away and uprooted from the surface of the organs by the action of heat. They become like bran <note>original: *furfur*, or chaff from wheat</note> and resemble the scales of fish; hence they are called "leaf-like" <note>original: *petaloides*</note> or scales.

Bran <note>original: *furfur*</note>, however, consists of certain fragments arranged like bran that are shed from the organs by the violence of heat; they are white and thicker than scales.

Scales in the urine without fever signify dry mange <term>scabiem: a skin irritation or "itch," here believed to affect the internal linings</term>.

Scales appearing with a fever signify consumption and wasting; bran-like fragments [shedding...]

### *Concerning Specks.*

Specks <note>original: *atomi*, referring to tiny, indivisible particles or "atoms" of sediment</note> are small, round granules like dots, sometimes white and sometimes reddish; they signify gout <term>guttam: literally 'a drop,' the medieval term for joint pain believed to be caused by a drop of morbid humor</term> in both men and women.

Specks appearing at the bottom of the urinal and settling there indicate pain in the reproductive organs, the feet, and the knees, and consequently podagra <term>podagram: gout specifically affecting the feet</term>.

Specks in the middle region [of the urine] signify pain and gout in the spiritual organs <term>membris spiritualibus: the heart and lungs, which were believed to process the 'vital spirits'</term>, and from the reproductive region up to the diaphragm.

Specks in the highest region signify gout of the upper parts. Specks throughout the entire urine declare gout in all the limbs. Clear urine that is pure in substance, in which there appears something thick like a cloud, and within which there are specks descending and ascending in clusters below, signifies pregnancy and conception.

Fatty specks in the lower part, resembling dregs <note>original: *loturæ*, literally 'wash-water' from meat, indicating a cloudy or sediment-heavy appearance</note>, if they settle at the bottom and congeal after a short time, signify that the woman has conceived; if they are reddish or brownish and round in shape, it signifies she has conceived a male. If they appear lead-colored <note>original: *lividæ*, a bluish-grey or bruised color</note> and broad in shape, it signifies she has conceived a female. However, if the woman has not conceived and such signs appear, it signifies gout in the woman.

### *Concerning Sperm in the Urine.*

Sperm in the urine tending toward the bottom, or settling at the bottom, signifies that sexual intercourse preceded it, or a nocturnal illusion <note>original: *nocturnam illusionem*, a medieval term for a dream leading to involuntary ejaculation</note>, or the effect of venereal acts.

Globular or lumpy sperm mixed with the urine in thick pieces signifies abstinence from intercourse or nocturnal pollution <note>involuntary ejaculation</note>.

Sperm appearing frequently on many occasions indicates gonorrhea <term>gonorrhœam: in this period, understood generally as an involuntary 'flow of seed'</term> or...

->**On Ash-colored Deposits.**<-

Ash-colored deposits <term>reſolutiones cineritiæ: fine, greyish sediments resembling wood ash</term> that are subtle in color, clinging together in clumps, or gathered together while residing at the bottom, signify the retention of the menses.

Ash-colored deposits of a blackish color scattered through the urine signify an active menstrual flow.

Ash-colored deposits, blackish and thick, clinging to the substance of the urine at the bottom, signify a splenic passion <note>a disease or "suffering" of the spleen</note> and an abscess of the spleen.

Ash-colored deposits occurring at the end of phlegmatic fevers signify that the phlegmatic fever is changing into melancholy <term>melancholia: an excess of "black bile," often associated with chronic or cold, dry illnesses</term>.

Ash appearing in the urine signifies pains in the lower parts such as the womb, the retention of the menses, the flow of hemorrhoids, and pain in the spleen; it also signifies condylomata <note>original: *condylomata*</note>, that is, hard and solid deposits around the anus, round and shaped like acorns.

Strictly speaking, however, condylomata are abscesses caused by melancholic blood congealed at the heads of the veins.

It also signifies "figs" <note>original: *ficos*, a historical term for hemorrhoidal growths or anal warts</note> in the anus, which are distinct collections formed around the anus from melancholic blood, inducing a lumpy swelling.

->**Eighthly, Concerning the Hypostasis and the Sediment.**<-

The hypostasis <term>hypoſtaſis: from the Greek, meaning "that which stands under"; the general term for any sediment in the urine</term> is the foundation and the waste product of the third digestion <term>third digestion: the metabolic process occurring within the solid organs and tissues themselves</term> sent out with the urine; it has three distinctions according to its location. For if the hypostasis settles and remains at the bottom, it is called the sediment <note>original: *sedimen*</note>.

If, however, it is driven into the middle region of the urine, it is called an eneorema <term>eneorima: from the Greek for "something suspended"; a cloud-like sediment floating in the center of the vial</term>, as if hanging there. But if it should be pushed all the way to the surface of the urine, it is called a nephilis <term>nephilis: from the Greek "nephele" for cloud</term>, that is, a "cloud," using a metaphor taken from the clouds in the sky. A natural hypostasis should be white and sitting at the bottom of the vessel; it should be of a middle consistency between thin and thick, of a round and pine-cone shape, continuous without any interruption of its parts, and light in motion. Thus, if the vessel is moved, the sediment should rise quickly without making the liquid turbid; when the vessel is at rest, it should suddenly return to the bottom in the shape of a pine-cone or a pyramid. According to various authors, several rules are given concerning the hypostasis.

**First rule.** A cloudy hypostasis signifies windiness <note>internal gas or "flatulence" in the humors</note> and a thick rawness, which carry the matter of the disease upward; it shows that nature is beginning to digest or "cook" the matter, and to dissolve and refine the windiness of the humors.

**Second rule.** A cloudy hypostasis at the bottom during any disease is a very bad sign, because it signifies that nature is fleeing from its governance of the disease because... <note>original: *pro-*</note>

**The Third Rule.** A cloudy sediment <term>hypostasis: the sediment or deposit that settles at the bottom of a urine sample</term> that remains suspended announces a mediocre state of digestion; it indicates flatulence and a "rawness" <term>cruditas: in Galenic medicine, the state of humors that have not been properly "cooked" or processed by the body's heat</term> that has been lifted upward but is soon to be dissolved.

### On the colors of the sediment.

A white color, light and joined, etc., signifies a praiseworthy disposition of the body. Red signifies a long illness and the rawness of the matter; however, it indicates an illness that is likely to end well.

A reddish color is worse than a pure red: for it is created from watery blood, wherefore it threatens a prolongation of the illness due to the rawness of the humors.

A black color in the sediment is the worst of all and is the most immediate sign of death, occurring either because of excessive "burning" <note>original: *incensionem*, referring to extreme feverish heat</note> or extreme coldness. This is especially true if a livid or leaden color <note>original: *liuiditas*</note> preceded the blackness. If, however, the sediment is first purple and then becomes black, death from internal burning [fever] is to be expected.

A black color in the sediment signifies destruction <note>original: *perditionem*, meaning a fatal outcome</note>, even if the urine itself is a color other than black.

Black sediment combined with black urine—especially if it is grainy—signifies certain destruction.

A rose-colored or arsenic-colored <note>original: *arsenica*, likely referring to the bright orange-yellow color of the mineral orpiment</note> sediment that is subtle within the liquid indicates a long duration of the disease.

A bluish-grey <note>original: *glaucus*</note> color is consistent with a tempered liquid and indicates an excess of yellow bile <term>cholera: one of the four humors, associated with a hot and dry temperament</term>.

A lemon-yellow <note>original: *citrinus*</note> color during a fever shows choleric matter and suggests a return to health only after a long time; it shows humors that are naturally raw and "un-cooked." This color can signify both good and evil: if it appears as a cloud, it signifies hope that the "cooking" <term>coctio: the metabolic process where the body's heat matures the humors</term> will be completed.

If it is floating, we have less hope that the process will be completed. If it remains at the bottom, it signifies the rawness of the humors and a heaviness combined with thickness.

A livid sediment signifies mortification <note>the death of the body's "vital spark" or tissue</note>.

Sediment that changes into a reddish or bluish-grey color notes a return to health.

...sharp, or solid, and continuous. If [the sediment] appears with a sharp fever, it signifies phlegmatic humors <note>In Galenic medicine, phlegm was a cold, moist humor; "burned" phlegm was considered particularly toxic</note> ignited by the heat of the fever. If it occurs with a continuous fever and is scaly, like the scales of fish, it signifies the wasting away of the external, hard, and subtle members of the body. But if it is bran-like <note>furfurea: appearing like dandruff or grain husks</note>, it signifies the dissolution of moisture and the scraping of the bladder.

**Galen** states: Scaly sediment <term>hypostasis: the solid matter that settles at the bottom of a urine sample</term> signifies the consumption of the hard members of the body. Bran-like sediment indicates a more intense heat during the "perforation" <note>likely referring to the breakdown or ulceration</note> of a bodily member. Sediment resembling coarse meal is a sign of consumption in the hard parts of the limbs and announces death after a long period of time. Sediment like coarse meal appearing during fevers notes a long-lasting disease, and death occurring before that long duration is finished. Lentil-like sediment, resembling crushed lentils, indicates a suffering of the liver. Vetch-like sediment <note>orbina: resembling the bitter vetch or "orobus" bean</note>, like crushed vetch, commonly occurs in those of a sanguine temperament; these signs signify the wasting of the liver and kidneys, and indeed of the whole body, though in different ways.

Sandy sediment denotes a stone in the kidneys and bladder, depending on the variety of the grains, as has been said.

Ash-colored sediment, if it is thinner than it should be during fevers, announces an impending rigor <note>a sudden chill or shivering fit</note>; if it appears without a fever, it signifies choleric humors and phlegm that has not been properly "cooked" <note>original: coctum; referring to 'coction,' the process by which the body's natural heat digests or processes the humors</note>. If the sediment is thicker than it should be and is accompanied by fever, it announces a thickness and viscosity of the waste matter and a long-lasting illness; if there is no fever, it signifies these things more mildly.

Briefly, according to the mind of **Isaac** <term>Isaac: Isaac Judaeus (c. 832–932), a foundational author on the science of urines</term> regarding the judgment of urine: A black or very black sediment denotes absolute evil, especially if it is grainy and rough, and most of all if the urine itself is black.

Red, citron-colored, and green sediments are mediocre—falling between good and bad. However, red is the best among them and closer to a good health; green is worse and closer to fear, because it indicates the burning of the humors and the consumption of the blood's moisture. A citron color in the sediment can signify both good and evil.

**Averroes** <term>Averroes: Ibn Rushd (1126–1198), the influential Andalusian physician and philosopher</term> says in his book *The Colliget* <term>Colliget: from 'Kitab al-Kullyat', his comprehensive medical encyclopedia</term> that the substances of unnatural sediments come from many materials. Some resemble broken wheat and some resemble vetch, and these note the liquefaction of the body's members or the scorching of the humors. In acute illnesses, these are bad signs. If they are red, they indicate a viscous, bloody humor, or a scorching of either the liver or the loins. A citron color is more specific to the loins, but a slimy sediment is the worst, because it denotes the liquefaction and breakdown of the "radical" <note>foundational or essential</note> members. However, a bran-like sediment sometimes occurs because of "scabies" <note>roughness or irritation</note> of the bladder and sometimes because of the liquefaction of the members; the way to distinguish whether it comes from the bladder or elsewhere is that in the case of the bladder, an itching is felt in the parts of the penis <note>original: virgæ; literally "rod," the standard medical term for the penis</note>.

| { There is no sediment | the one who urinates is following a regimen <note>lifestyle, especially diet</note> of extreme refinement. |
| { There is much sediment | the one who urinates is following a heavy or coarse regimen. |
| { There is little sediment | the one who urinates is following a balanced regimen. |

A large amount of <term>hypostasis: the solid matter that settles at the bottom of a urine sample</term> in healthy people is a good sign; it notes that the body is well-nourished and that the limbs are strong enough to expel their superfluities <note>waste products or excess humors</note> through the sediment. It indicates that the body is neither too thin nor too fat. However, in entirely healthy people who govern themselves in a proper and orderly way, there is no sediment in their urine. Plentiful, white sediment—refined in the liquid, moderately round, and smooth in its movement—shows health and the strength of the limbs reaching the completion of digestion <note>original: "coctionis," the "cooking" or processing of food into humors</note>; yet its great quantity also denotes an abundance of humors.

Plentiful sediment in sick bodies—if it is white, round, cohesive, and light—announces that the nature of the disease is descending from the upper to the lower parts of the body, and this is most visible on a critical day <note>the "crisis" or turning point of a disease</note>. If such sediment appears during fevers along with delirium <note>original: "alienatione"</note> and the hair falls out, it shows the disease is quieting. But if it is not round, etc., it notes many humors gathered in the body of the type of thick or thin <term>phlegm: one of the four bodily humors, associated with cold and moisture</term>. Plentiful and bran-like <note>furfurea: appearing like dandruff or grain husks</note> sediment during a fever, when the kidneys and bladder are otherwise healthy, announces the shivering-fit <note>original: "rigorem"</note> of a coming fever.

Plentiful sediment, when the fever is neither softening nor decreasing, marks the body being consumed <note>wasting away</note>. A small amount of sediment in the healthy signifies dryness, thinness, and refinement. A small amount of sediment in the sick marks the corruption of the blood's moisture and the proximity of consumption <note>physical wasting/decline</note>; for this reason, it is a very bad sign if it occurs with an acute fever.

A balance <note>original: "temperamentum"</note> of sediment between much and little signifies a balanced constitution and the strength of the limbs.

<summary>This page details how the consistency and quantity of urinary sediment (hypostasis) reflect a patient's diet, the presence of kidney stones, and the severity of wasting diseases. It synthesizes Galenic principles with the authoritative medical observations of Averroes.</summary>

### *Variation of urine according to thickness and thinness.*

Urine that is thin when it first leaves the body, and thickens after standing in the vessel for a little while, signifies that nature <note>The "nature" of the body refers to its innate healing power or vital force</note> has begun the process of "cooking" <term>coction: the medieval medical concept of the body "ripening" or processing harmful humors into a form that can be expelled</term> and has mixed the humors and dissolved the gassiness of those humors. Nature has refined a good portion of them because of the speed and lightness of its own movements. Urine that is thin when passed and remains thin indicates a "raw" <note>original: "crudum," meaning unprocessed or in the early stages where the body has not yet begun to fight the illness</note> disease. If healthy signs follow, it indicates the end of the disease will involve an abscess <term>aposteme: a localized collection of pus or a swelling</term> beneath the ribcage <term>hypochondrium: the upper abdominal regions on either side of the body, just below the ribs</term>. And if this urine appears during an acute and burning fever, it is a very bad sign, because it signifies that the fever is growing hotter and more inflamed, and is ascending to the upper parts of the body and into the head.

Urine that is thick and remains thick signifies a massive struggle <note>original: "conturbationem," a state of disorder or turmoil</note> between the substance of the disease and nature. However, in this case, nature has been overcome by the disease, because although it has disturbed and mixed the humors and shown a certain degree of refinement or processing, it has not completed the "cooking." If this urine appears at the beginning of an illness, it marks the destruction of the sick person. If this urine is globular or resembles that of a beast of burden <note>original: "iumentura," referring to the murky, thick urine typical of pack animals like horses or mules</note>, it signifies a headache that is past, present, and future.

Urine that is thick but then clears while in the vessel signifies that nature has completed the "cooking" of the dregs <note>original: "fęcis," meaning the waste or sediment</note> and has refined it. Nature has not let up until the matter is divided and each part is placed where it naturally belongs. This is a better sign than urine that starts thick and stays thick. This is also a better sign than urine that is thin and later thickens.

Likewise, urine that is thin when passed and later thickens is better than urine that is thin and remains in its thinness and clarity. The latter signifies that nature has not yet begun to "cook" those humors which are the material of the diseases. Praise be to God.

*Let these things be sufficient so that you may more easily understand the author’s teaching. Let whoever desires to pursue this art perfectly also read other authors who have written on this matter—but not before you have thoroughly mastered these teachings. This is so that the memory and intellect, distracted by many and various opinions, do not fail to cling to any of them. If anything good is found here, let it be credited to God, from whom all good things proceed. But if there is something you do not approve of, ascribe it to the weakness of my own intellect. Know, however, that I have undertaken all this for the sake of being helpful. Even if I have failed in some matter or have not grasped the author's meaning, perhaps I will be the reason for someone more skilled to make this matter clearer. If that should happen, I will consider myself to have gathered the fruit of my labor. Farewell, reader, and enjoy this little book, or rather, use it with good fortune.*

-># THE AUTHOR TO THE READER<-

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'V' featuring a figure, possibly a scholar or a saint, seated and gesturing towards an open book or desk.</image-desc>Just as one who builds in public is forced to endure many critics, it does not escape me that once I have published this little work to the common people, there will be no shortage of mockers who will not be pleased by my labor and diligence.

To some, I will seem—either for some reason, or I know not how, or perhaps just from their own disposition—as though I should have written nothing at all. But who is there who can satisfy the minds of everyone, when no host can satisfy three guests equally, according to the Poet? <note>A reference to the Roman poet Horace</note>

> *Three guests seem to me to disagree nearly entirely,*
> *Asking for many different things with varying palates.*
> <note>original: "Tres mihi conuiuæ propè dissentire videntur. Poscetes vario multum diuersa palato." - Horace, Epistles 2.2.61-62</note>

Furthermore, the manners of men are now so corrupted that each person picks out and amplifies from the words and writings of others only what seems to be faulty. No one brings forth what is good and properly approved; so sharply does the envious eye see the faults of others. But I, friendly reader, do not care what detractors think or say about me. I have strived to be useful to you to the best of my ability; if I have achieved this, as I hope, I will not regret my labor, my sleepless nights, and my late-night studies <term>lucubration: work or study produced by late-night effort, literally "by candlelight"</term>. 

If, however, there is anyone who thinks they can gain no utility from this, let them know that they should read other things; for these writings are only for beginners <term>tyrones: novices or junior students, originally referring to young soldiers in training</term> and those unrefined in the medical art, as a sort of entrance and introduction to this study. If anyone wishes to rebuke me for this, let him write something better himself; I do not stand in the way. But I think it is fair that each person helps others according to their own capacity and learning. Therefore, if not in elegant words, I believe I have written in plain ones. 

In this matter, you will easily grant me pardon, kind reader, for you should seek a more elaborate style from the young men of this time, and not from me or those like me. Finally, if I have inserted any paradoxes <note>original: "paradoxa" - ideas that challenge common opinion or traditional medical consensus</note> according to the opinion of the common people, I pray that no one judges things unknown before they have understood them. They are unskilled who believe or approve of nothing except what they themselves know or have experienced.

Nor do I say this because I wish anyone to be bound to my words; rather, let each person read other authors—both older and more skilled than I—and then let them judge and approve what seems most correct. You, whoever you may be, most excellent reader, think well of our work, such as it is, and may you long enjoy good health in safety. 

From Heidelberg, in the Year of the Virgin's birth <note>A common Renaissance way of dating a text to the year of our Lord, Anno Domini</note> 1532.

# HERMES TRISMEGISTUS’
### MEDICAL ASTROLOGY

...the second is which diseases the Moon, when combined with malefic planets <note>original: "maleficis," usually referring to Saturn or Mars</note> in the zodiac signs, may provoke; the other is which medications should be used to provide relief.

<margin>1</margin>
**The rays** emitted from the seven planets are multiplied and mingled into the individual limbs of a human being while the conception begins to take shape within the mother’s womb. Nor indeed does it happen differently when the child comes forth into this light <note>is born</note>, according to the positioning of the twelve signs, such that the head is dedicated to Aries. The sensory parts are assigned to the seven planets in the following manner:

<margin>2</margin>
To the **Sun**, the right eye; to the **Moon**, the left.
To **Saturn**, hearing and the ears; to **Jupiter**, the brain.
To **Mars**, the gore and the blood; to **Venus**, the sense of smell and taste.
To **Mercury**, the tongue and the throat <note>original: "gurgulio," referring to the windpipe or gullet</note>.

3 Therefore, that limb is mutilated or impaired over which an afflicted <term>afflicted: in astrology, a planet is "afflicted" when it is in a physically or symbolically weak position or receiving harsh "aspects" from malefic planets</term> planet holds dominion at the moment of conception or birth <term>birth: original "genitura," the astrological chart of one's birth</term>.

4 There are also four principal and more general parts in a human: the head, chest, hands, and feet. If the star which presided over these individual parts was poorly positioned at the time of conception or birth, it likewise afflicted the parts attributed to it, or the specific components of those parts.

For instance, either one eye or both are affected when the Sun or Moon are poorly disposed; the hearing, the ears, or the teeth are affected when Saturn is afflicted.

An oppressed Mercury takes away the use of the tongue or speech, as if the rays emitted from a malefic planet from some other position have bruised, impaired, or mutilated them. We find the same in the chest, discovering an impaired lung, or the liver, spleen, heart, or some corruption of the intestines.

In the consideration of the hands and feet, we shall observe whether the fingers, the nails, or any of these small parts are poorly affected according to the kinship or affinity of the ruling planet.

5 Therefore, for those injuries which can be corrected by treatment, it will be necessary to apply suitable aids and resist the disease through planets having contrary powers and natures.

To Saturn are assigned things that are cooling, and those that thin through aridity and dryness.

# THE LITTLE BOOK

To **Mercury**, things that are congealing and flatulent <note>original: "congelantia, & flatuosa," referring to the production of gas or the thickening of bodily fluids</note> are naturally attributed.

To **Mars**, things that are heating and filling are assigned, as he is the most piercing, burning, and the generator of blood.

To **Jupiter** and **Venus** belong those things that are softening, binding, and those that restrain and heal all ulcers.

As for the **Moon**, whether that star be favorable or harmful <note>original: "siue benefica illa, siue malefica fuerit," referring to the Moon's functional role in a specific chart</note>, she will support whichever planet she joins herself to.

<margin>6</margin>
Therefore, the positioning of the heavens must be diligently explored by one intending to heal, and the hour of <term>decubitus: the exact moment a patient takes to their bed at the onset of an illness</term> or of the encroaching disease must be learned with precision. The stars and their mutual relationships to one another must be considered. For without their meeting or influence, nothing in human affairs is either diseased or healthy. Recurring or acute diseases do not arise, nor is anyone relieved by the doctor’s diligence, unless—regardless of the care and skill applied—the patient either perishes or is saved through the conspiracy <note>original: "conspiratio," here meaning a harmonious alignment or agreement of celestial influences</note> of these stars.

<margin>7</margin>
But if the hour of taking to bed cannot be sufficiently scrutinized, that hour in which the illness was first announced must be observed, and the chart of the heavens' position must be diligently contemplated.

One must also observe which planet the Moon approaches after her separation <note>original: "defluxum," the Moon's movement away from an astrological aspect</note>, or from whom she has separated and toward whom she flows. If she is disconnected, notice by whose opposition <note>original: "diametro," a 180-degree aspect</note> or square <note>original: "quadrangulo," a 90-degree aspect</note> she is afflicted; if she is joined, notice whose meeting she supports. Configured with malefic planets <note>traditionally Saturn or Mars</note>, she intensifies the disease toward a despair of life; joined by aspect or meeting with beneficial planets <note>traditionally Jupiter or Venus</note>, she then brings help more immediately and effectively.

<margin>8</margin>
This consideration will also be necessary: whether the Moon, while increasing her speed, decreases in light, or if the opposite happens; whether she increases in light while slowed in her course, or if both occur at once, or neither.

<margin>9</margin>
For if the Moon, after her <term>conjunction with the Sun: the New Moon</term>, when she begins to swell with the increase of light and moves with a faster motion, is at the same time afflicted by a square from **Mars**, or strikes against Mars before she reaches her opposition, and no beneficial planet intervenes, she will provoke lethal and destructive diseases. If, however, she joins or is mixed with one of the beneficial planets, even if the patient is laid low by a desperate and ruined state of health, they will nonetheless recover from the illness.

But with the Moon decreasing in both motion and light, and especially if tainted by an opposition or square with **Saturn**, the illness will be insurmountable and lethal unless the disease remits after the Moon has reached her opposition. If the Moon meets beneficial planets, the patient will be freed from the disease in a short time.

Furthermore, it should be remembered that the disease will intensify as long as the Moon proceeds with a swifter course; likewise, the disease turns for the better when she is slowed in her course, provided the <term>node: the points where the Moon's orbit crosses the sun's path</term> has been passed. Let this be...

### HERMES TRISMEGISTUS ON IATROMATHEMATICS

...the consideration is established at the first onset of any disease.

Whoever lies afflicted with disease, oppressed by **Saturn** or **Mercury**, will be slow and sluggish, dragging their sick limbs with difficulty. These limbs are numb and obstructed because of the cold and the downward flow of fluids <note>original: "defluxione," referring to the movement of humors like phlegm</note>; as the disease reveals itself gradually, they are difficult to wake even when prodded. They are quiet and fearful, seeking the warmth of blankets; they delight in the dark, sigh continually, and draw their breath slowly. The pulse is short and anxious. They find great relief from hot things. Their pulses are also weak and faint, while the entire surface of the body is dry and cold, signaling that in treating these patients, there is a need for heat as well as softening and binding agents.

But those who fall ill by the assault of **Mars** or the **Sun** will be turbulent, restless, and disturbed in mind, with the entire surface of the body inflamed by a fiery heat. They are prone to anger and noisy shouting; they stare fiercely and are thirsty, with a dry, rough tongue. They are demanding of wine and cold drinks and are seized by a longing for baths. No food sharpens their appetite, and they are constantly wagging their tongues with impudence. These are known by a short and low pulse, yet an irregular one; they are burdened by a flushed face and a fullness of the body. For these, <term>bloodletting: the surgical removal of blood to balance the humors</term> is beneficial up to the fifth day, as are those things which can either evacuate or purge the body's fullness, and whatever aids the necessity of nature finds and discovers as remedies for these diseases.

<margin>10</margin> Indeed, things suitable for **Mars** are contrary to **Saturn**, such as those that heat, soften, and dissolve obstructions.

Things consistent with **Saturn** depart from the nature of **Mars**—that is, whatever cools, binds, and repels.

Whatever passions of the heart and those arising in the mouth of the stomach, as well as arterial, arthritic, and similar conditions, are stirred up by the **Sun** and **Mars**.

<margin>11</margin> On the other hand, true fevers, pleurisy <note>original: "pleuritides," an inflammation of the membranes around the lungs</note>, and lung ulcers or inflammations and the like take their origin from **Saturn** and **Mercury**. Against these diseases, cooling agents are used, such as: *Nightshade, Coriander, Endive, Poppy juice, bark of the Winter Cherry root <note>original: "Halicacabi"</note>, Knotgrass, Houseleek, Fleawort, Duckweed, Vine leaves, White lead, Litharge <note>original: "argenti spuma," a byproduct of silver refining used in ointments</note>, Hematite stone, Purslane, Egg white, Linseed, Reed, Mallow leaves, Pomegranate, Hypocistis <note>a parasitic plant found on rockroses</note>, Cypress, Bramble, Acacia, Quinces, Wild pears, Alum, Wild vine flower, dates of the male and female Palm, Myrtle, Sumac, fresh Rose, Rush, Ladanum, Saffron, and Pondweed.*

Both the **Sun** and **Mars** rule over heating things: namely, among many other things, *Oil of Privet <note>original: "Cyprinum oleum"</note>*, and all fragrant-smelling things, as well as *Iris ointment, Cinnamon, Marjoram, Narcissus, and Fenugreek*...

12 Whoever falls ill while the **Moon** is passing through **Aries** (especially if she is slow in motion and waning in light) and is corrupted by a square <note>a 90-degree aspect</note>, an opposition <note>a 180-degree aspect</note>, or a conjunction with **Saturn**, the origin of the disease for this person will be from cold. Naturally, with the head heavy with congestion and the eyes weighed down by weariness, the throat and airway are then seized by catarrh <note>a buildup of mucus</note>. Because of the dripping of these humors into the chest, the pulses are weak and irregular. At night, the severity of the disease intensifies: the internal organs are all burning, while the surface of the body is chilled and the extremities of the limbs grow numb with cold. Fainting, a loathing of the stomach, and untimely sweats are present. For these cases, heating, softening, and bowel-loosening agents are appropriate. <term>Bloodletting: the surgical removal of blood to balance the body's humors</term> is useless here. If the **Moon** does not apply herself to a beneficial planet, nor looks upon one through a square or opposition, the patient will not survive but will die. But if she moves toward a beneficial planet in the manner we have described, the patient should recover comfortably, or certainly, they will fall back from one disease into another, descending into nightly disturbances.

<margin>The Moon in Aries afflicted by Mars.</margin>
If, however, **Mars** also awaits the incoming **Moon** in the configuration we have described, the disease will not be recurring, but when the **Moon** reaches the point of opposition, the patient will die.

For anyone who falls ill when the **Moon** is in the same configuration, or is carried toward **Mars** or the **Sun**, the disease arises for them from the head—specifically from the membranes of the brain being afflicted. There will also be continuous fevers, wakefulness, and insomnia; the mouth will be burning, the thirst intolerable, and the tongue agitated and dry. There is heat in the chest, inflammation of the liver, and the pulses are high, raised, and irregular. For these people, the pursuit of health must begin with bloodletting, and both cooling and soothing agents must be applied. There will also be alienation of the mind and <term>phrenesis: a state of delirium or brain fever</term>. ### *The Moon in Taurus Afflicted by Saturn*

If, at the time a disease sets in, the Moon is passing through **Taurus** and is afflicted by an opposition <note>original: "diametro"</note>, a square <note>original: "quadrangulo"</note>, or a conjunction with **Saturn**—especially if she is moving slowly and her light is waning—the disease will be provoked by surfeit <note>original: "ex crapula," meaning excessive consumption or a hangover</note> and a fullness of the humors. Fevers will arise from blockages; pains in the diaphragm <note>original: "præcordiorum"</note> and joints will cause distress; the pulse will be raised, high, and then irregular. There will be inflammation of the entire body and ulceration of the lungs. For these patients, bloodletting <note>original: "sanguinis minutio," literally a lessening of the blood</note> will be beneficial, as will everything that suppresses such a condition. ### *The Moon Overwhelmed by Mars in Taurus*

If the Moon is configured with **Mars** by conjunction, opposition, or square while in **Taurus**, she will produce a disease in the bedridden patient arising from a plethora <note>original: "plenitudine," an excess</note> of blood. Continuous fevers will be present, as well as a blockage of the entire body, inflammation of the neck and throat, and torment in the bones. There will be excessive wakefulness and insomnia, and a craving for wine and cold water. These patients will be greatly relieved by the cutting of a vein <note>original: "venæ sectione," phlebotomy</note>; everything that thins and soothes the humors will be helpful. If **Mars** rages in this way and no ray from a benefic planet helps the Moon, the disease will extinguish the weak patient on the ninth day. However, if his power is repressed by a configuration of a benefic with the Moon, the patient will be relieved after the critical day.

### *The Moon in Gemini Overwhelmed by Saturn*

When the Moon is in **Gemini**, afflicted by the rays of **Saturn** or joined with him—especially as her light is decreasing—the cause of the illness will be wakefulness, insomnia, or the exhaustion of travel. The joints will seem as if loosened and will hardly hold together. The disease reveals itself quickly, or certainly begins to increase after the third day and lasts until the thirtieth. Slight fevers will set in, and a wasting <note>original: "consumptio"</note> of the entire body will press more heavily at night with the violence of the sickness. The pulse is rare and small; there is a troublesome sweat and pain in the spleen. If **Mars** affects the Moon from somewhere else with ill-omened rays, the sick person will be released from life after the tenth day. But if benefics are also present and aiding the Moon with their support, the patient will recover health after a long-lasting sickness.

### *The Moon by Saturn in Pisces.*

### *The Moon by Mars in Pisces.*

When the Moon is oppressed by Mars in Pisces, being fast in motion and increasing in light, she will stir up the causes of disease from over-fullness <note>plethora</note> and the gluttonous swallowing of wine. Because of this, the suffering will be increased by nightly intensifications; there will be delirium, frenzy, headaches, burning fevers, intense thirst, and a craving for wine. For these patients, the beginning of health must be sought through bloodletting <note>original: "venæ sectione"</note>, and those things must be applied which can drive away this evil state of the body. If benefic planets do not help the Moon, the patient will die at the next square aspect <note>original: "quadrato," a 90-degree astrological alignment</note> of Mars. But if the Moon is in any aspect with Jupiter or Venus—that is, in a square, opposition, or conjunction—regardless of which sign she is in at the time the patient takes to their bed, the afflicted person will be restored after the next square or opposition.

It will also be of great importance to observe at what hour the first onset of the disease is detected, and whether at that time the benefic planets are rising or occupy the Midheaven <note>original: "medium cœli," the highest point of the sky in a horoscope, representing success and strength</note>. For when positioned thus, they will provide more help to strength that has otherwise collapsed than even the most excellent Physician could. Therefore, it is necessary to scrutinize exactly both the day and hour of falling ill <note>term: decubitus; the moment a patient is forced to take to their bed by sickness</note> and to examine the position of the heavens. For nothing happens to a human being that does not arise and take its origin from celestial consensus and sympathy.

<note>original: "LIBELLVS"</note>

They have such a correspondence <note>original: "conuenientiam"</note> between themselves that the position of the Moon at conception is the ascending degree <note>the sign of the Zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note> at birth, as Ptolemy—or rather the same Hermes—reports in most clear words in his *Book of Aphorisms*, Aphorism 51. However, since nothing is more difficult than to know the hour of the conception of children from either the father or the mother, and since this is the most powerful moment—given that it is the natural beginning, while the hour of birth is accidental, according to Ptolemy in Book 3 of *On Judgments* <note>Tetrabiblos</note>, Chapter 1—astrologers provide two ways by which this may be known. I believe physicians should learn these from the ephemerides <note>astronomical tables showing the positions of celestial bodies</note> which report them, as Gioseffo Moleti and Valentin Naboth <note>original: "Iosephus Moletus, & Valentinus Naibod"</note> do quite clearly in their commentaries on Alcabitius <note>A 10th-century Arab astrologer whose work was a standard medieval textbook</note>. We have deemed it sufficient to advise on these matters in this place, but not to teach them fully, for here we strive for brevity.

2. To see what others think of this matter, see page 6.

3. Regarding what constitutes an afflicted planet, see page 31, verso, number 3.

4. The whole is nothing other than the gathering together of its parts; thus, when a planet shows—whether at conception, birth, or even the hour of the onset of a disease—that some limb is injured, it is not always the entire limb that is harmed, but some specific small part of that limb.

5. Detriments of the body which are caused by the celestial bodies are divided into two kinds: for they are either impediments or diseases, according to Ptolemy in Book 3 of *On Judgments*, Chapter 12. He teaches the difference between these with these words: [impediments happen only once and will not last long, but infirmities will either last forever or happen repeatedly]. Therefore, "infirmities" here are those detriments which do not require the physician’s work; indeed, if anyone applies care to them, he not only achieves nothing, but leads the patient into the most ruinous calamities. I have experienced this very thing myself: a skilled physician must therefore be knowledgeable in this matter. For this reason, the author said "those things which can be corrected by treatment," meaning the "impediments" described by Ptolemy, which wise physicians can resist with contrary things. This is according to the principle: *Contraries are cured by contraries* <note>original: "Contraria contrarijs curantur," the foundational principle of Galenic medicine</note>. What things are subject to the rule of individual planets you will find (in addition to those written by this author) in Marsilio Ficino’s book *On Life, Arranging it Celestially*, and also by Joannes Hasfurt on pages 2 and 3.

6. We taught the method of erecting a celestial theme <note>casting a horoscope</note> on page 29. However, if anyone wants this matter treated more exquisitely, let him read either Alcabitius with the commentaries of Valentin Naboth, or the ephemerides of Magini <note>Giovanni Antonio Magini, an Italian astronomer</note>, or others if he prefers. If you explore the celestial theme diligently, you will have the causes of illnesses, since the causes of all human affairs exist in the heavens—excepting those (as we said above) which are in the free will of God or man. If this is so, it follows that in the hour of taking to bed <note>original: "hora decubitus," the moment one falls ill</note>, or rather when the sick person is greatly afflicted by the distress of the disease, there is a cause present in heaven which may be discerned from the position of the sky and the specific minute <note>original: "scrupuli"</note> of that hour.

7. It very often happens that we are ignorant of the hour the disease struck; in that case, you should erect a celestial figure for the hour of the question—namely, when the urine is brought to the physician. Even if this has less power, Joannes Hasfurt and Galen believe it still holds some weight, and...

Thus, for the work to be complete and perfected, it is necessary to frequently cast a celestial figure <note>an astrological chart or horoscope</note> and to judge with the help of some interpreter, so that you may attain a perfect habit and right judgment in this matter. Nothing is more admirable in a physician than this, and it is the one thing above all by which good physicians differ from the bad.

### FROM MATHEMATICAL SCIENCE,

#### Chapter I.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial letter 'A'. Within the square frame of the letter, there is a pastoral scene featuring a reclining human figure in a landscape with a bovine animal (a goat or ox) visible on the left side.</image-desc>

**T**o prove that <term>Mathematical science</term><note>Meaning Astrology and Astronomy</note> is indeed essential, even the authority of the Stoic philosophers was sufficient; they both labored over books on the subject and demonstrated by their lives what its nature is. Nevertheless, since our present discussion concerns those things which the medical art promises, it is necessary to bring forward the testimonies of those who were most highly approved in that field. This is so that it may become known to everyone that even the physicians themselves—whom one ought to admit as the "foreseeing" part of their art—have, if not all, then certainly most of them, accepted that <term>Mathematical science</term>.

Before all things, one must consider the Moon, whether it moves by adding to or subtracting from its numbers <note>This refers to the Moon's mathematical velocity—whether it is speeding up or slowing down in its orbit—rather than just its visual brightness.</note>, not its light, as some have been deceived into thinking.
