### ON LIFE FROM THE HEAVENS. COMP.

...gold, and the scent of cinnamon and roses. Moreover, just as food properly taken into us—which is not alive in itself—is reduced through our own **spirit** to the form of our life, so also our bodies, when properly accommodated to the body and spirit of the world (namely through worldly things and through our own spirit), draw as much as possible from that worldly life. If you wish for food to take on the form of the brain, the liver, or the stomach more than other parts, you should consume food as similar to those as possible—that is, the brain, liver, and stomach of animals that are not far removed from human nature. 

If you desire your body and spirit to receive power <note>original: "virtutem," referring to the inherent medicinal or magical efficacy of a thing.</note> from some member of the cosmos—namely from the **Sun**—you must seek those things which are **Solar** above all others: among metals and stones, but even more so among plants. You should seek them even more among animals, and especially among humans, for things more similar to yourself undoubtedly confer more benefit. These things are to be applied externally and, as much as your strength allows, taken internally—especially on the day and hour of the Sun, and while the Sun is ruling in the configuration of the heavens. 

Indeed, **Solar things** <term>Solar: things governed by the Sun, associated with light, heat, authority, and the heart</term> include all those stones and flowers called *heliotropes*, because they turn toward the Sun. Likewise gold and orpiment <note>a deep yellow arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment</note>, gold colors, chrysolite, carbuncle, myrrh, frankincense, musk, ambergris, balsam, yellow honey, aromatic calamus, saffron, spikenard, cinnamon, aloe-wood, and other spices. Among animals, these include the hawk <note>original: "Astur" (or "Arieastur" in the OCR), a bird of prey associated with solar clarity</note>, the rooster, the swan, the lion, the beetle, the crocodile, and people who are blonde, curly-haired, fervent, and magnanimous. These things can be adapted for use partly as food, partly as ointments and fumigations <note>herbal incense or vapors</note>, and partly for general utility. These things must be felt, frequently thought upon, and above all, loved; and much light must be sought out.

If you suspect your stomach is deprived of the liver's warmth, draw the power of the liver from the stomach, both by rubbing and by compresses made of things agreeable to the liver—such as chicory, endive, *spodios* <note>original: "fodium," likely metallic ash used in ancient pharmacy</note>, eupatorium, liverwort, and the livers of animals. Similarly, so that the body is not deprived of **Jupiter** <term>Jovial: things governed by Jupiter, representing a temperate, balanced, and "sanguine" influence</term>, move the body on the day and hour under the reign of Jupiter. In the meantime, use **Jovial things**: silver, hyacinth, topaz, coral, crystal, beryl, *spodios*, sapphires, green and airy colors, wine, white sugar, honey, and thoughts and affections that are primarily Jovial—that is, constant, equitable, religious, and law-abiding. You should also associate with people of this kind: those who are of a sanguine temperament, handsome, and venerable. 

But remember that into those cold things mentioned first, one must introduce gold, wine, mint, saffron, cinnamon, and leopard's bane. The Jovial animals are the lamb, the peacock, the eagle, and the bullock. However, my sense of modesty does not allow me to show how the power of **Venus** is attracted by turtledoves, pigeons, wagtails, and the rest.

### On the harmony of the world, and the nature of man according to the stars, and how an attraction is made from each star. Chapter 11.

Nor indeed should anyone doubt that we, and all things around us, can claim celestial gifts for ourselves through certain preparations. For these things were made from heaven, are constantly governed by it, and were prepared from the very beginning to receive those influences. Most importantly, the world itself is a single living being <note>original: "animal." Ficino follows the Neoplatonic view that the universe possesses a soul (Anima Mundi) and a body.</note> more unified than any other animal, provided it is the most perfect animal. Therefore, just as in us the quality and movement of any single member—especially a principal one—affects the others, so the actions of the principal members in the world <note>the celestial bodies/planets</note> set all things in motion; and the lower members easily receive from the highest ones, which are ready to give of their own accord. For the more powerful a cause is, the more ready it is to increase others, and thus the more inclined it is to give. Therefore, a small preparation applied to us is sufficient for receiving the gifts of the heavens, provided that each person accommodates themselves especially to that planet to which they are primarily subject.

But before considering the individual property of each of us, we must consider the property of the human species as a whole. The Arabian astrologers <note>Referring to medieval thinkers like Albumasar or Al-Kindi, who influenced Renaissance magic.</note> agreed that this species is **Solar**. I conjecture this to be true from man's upright and beautiful stature, the subtlety of his humors <term>humors: the four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) that determined health and temperament</term>, the clarity of his spirit, the perspicuity of his imagination, and his pursuit of truth and glory. Furthermore, I add to this a **Mercurial** property, because of the vigorous movement of man's versatile intellect. And since the human race is born naked, unarmed, and in need of everything, yet acquires all these things through its own industry—which is characteristic of **Mercury**—I also add a **Jovial** property <note>referring to Jupiter (Jove)</note>, because of the temperate complexion of the body and the establishment of laws. 

Moreover, because we receive life in the second month after conception, over which **Jupiter** rules, and we are born in the ninth month, when he again receives dominion, the human species can therefore claim even more ample gifts from these three planets if it accommodates itself more and more daily to them through Solar, Mercurial, and Jovial things. 

As for the others: **Saturn** does not easily signify the common quality or lot of the human race, but rather a man separated from others—one who is either divine, or a happy brute, or one weighed down by extreme misery. **Mars**, the **Moon**, and **Venus** signify affections and actions that are shared equally with other living creatures. Let us therefore return to the **Sun**, **Jupiter**, and **Mercury**. 

We have already mentioned some Solar and Jovial things, but somehow we overlooked **Mercurial** things. They are of this kind: tin, silver—especially **quicksilver** <term>quicksilver: mercury (the element)</term>—silver marcasite, the agate stone, glass, porphyry, and things that mix saffron-yellow with green, emerald, and lac <note>a resinous secretion used for dyes and medicine</note>. Also, animals that are wise and clever yet vigorous: monkeys, dogs, and eloquent, sharp, versatile humans with oblong

From the Moon, one seeks through things that are white, moist, and green, through silver, crystal, pearls* <note>original: "vniones." *Now, if someone should argue that Saturn and Mars are harmful by nature—a thing which I myself would never believe—nevertheless, even these are to be used, just as physicians sometimes use poisons, which Ptolemy proves in the Centiloquy* <note>The "Centiloquium," a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms attributed to the astronomer Claudius Ptolemy.</note>. *Therefore, the power of Saturn will sometimes be beneficial if taken cautiously, just as physicians use things that are astringent and binding, or even things that numb the senses, such as opium and mandrake; and Mars likewise, like euphorbia and hellebore. Very often, therefore, we are subjected to Saturn by turning our reason away from human affairs through leisure, solitude, and steadiness; through theology, secret philosophy, superstition, magic, and agriculture. Through sorrow we are also subjected to Saturn; but we are subjected to Jupiter through civil and ambitious business, and through natural philosophy,*

That this world is animated—just like any other animal, but much more effectively—is proven not only by Platonic arguments but also by the testimony of the <note>original: "astrologorum Arabum." This happens on one hand through our own spirit, which acts as a medium within us and is then strengthened by the world-spirit; and on the other hand, through the rays of the stars acting favorably upon our spirit, which is similar in nature to those rays and then adapts itself to the heavenly things.

### *Between the soul of the world and its body, its spirit is manifest, in whose power are the four elements; we, however, are able to draw this in through our own spirit. Chapter III.* <note>Though labeled as Chapter III here, this is Chapter 12 in most standard editions of Book III.</note>

Ficino refers to the "Gymnosophists" or ancient Indian sages often cited in Hermetic and Platonic traditions.</note> Indian philosophers prove this by the fact that the world generates living things from itself everywhere. Therefore, it lives through a soul that is present everywhere and perfectly suited to it. Thus, between the world's tangible and partially decaying body and its soul—the nature of which is too far removed from such a body—there exists everywhere a spirit, just as there is between the soul and the body within us, provided that life is everywhere and always communicated by the soul to the thicker body. For such a spirit is necessarily required as a medium, so that the divine soul may both be present to the thicker body and bestow life deeply upon it. # ON THE COMPARISON OF THE HEAVENLY LIFE

<header>ON THE COMPARISON OF THE HEAVENLY LIFE. COMPLETED.</header>

...falling far away from the most divine things, it <note>Referring to the World Soul, which requires a medium to act upon the physical world.</note> therefore requires the assistance of a more excellent body that is, as it were, not a body at all. Accordingly, we know that all living things, plants as well as animals, live and generate through a certain spirit similar to this. Furthermore, among the elements, that which is most spiritual <note>Likely referring to Fire or Air, which were considered more "active" and "spiritual" than Water or Earth.</note> generates most quickly and is moved perpetually, as if it were alive. 

But one might ask in the meantime: if the elements and living creatures generate something similar to themselves under the influence of a certain spirit, why do stones and metals not generate? These are intermediate between elements and living beings. The reason is clearly that the spirit within them is restrained by a thicker matter. Yet, if this spirit is at any time properly separated and preserved in its isolation, it will be able to generate something similar to itself like a <term>seminal power</term> <note>original: "seminaria virtus," the inherent capability of a substance to reproduce its own kind.</note>. This is possible if it is applied to a certain matter of the same kind—the sort of spirit that diligent natural philosophers <note>original: "physici," meaning those who study nature.</note> separate from gold by a certain sublimation with fire. When they apply this to other metals, they produce gold. Such a spirit, drawn properly from gold or another source and preserved, is what the Arabic astrologers call the **elixir**. 

But let us return to the spirit of the world, through which the world generates all things, since it generates all things through its own spirit. We can call this spirit either "the heavens" or the **quintessence** <note>original: "quintam essentiam," the "fifth element" or ether that makes up the celestial bodies, distinct from the four earthly elements.</note>. It is roughly the same thing in the body of the world as our own spirit is in our bodies. There is this primary exception: the soul of the world does not draw this spirit from the four elements as if from its own humors, as our soul draws ours from our own. Rather, to speak in the manner of the <term>Platonists</term> or <term>Plotinians</term>, the world soul procreates this spirit directly from her own generative power, as if swelling with it, and creates the stars along with it. Immediately through this spirit, she gives birth to the four elements, as if all things are contained within the power of that spirit. 

Indeed, the spirit itself is a most thin body, almost as if it were not a body, and almost already a soul; likewise, it is almost not a soul, and almost already a body. Within its power, there is surely something of an earthly nature, but more of a watery nature, and even more of an airy nature. Again, it contains a great deal of the fiery and stellar nature. Toward the measures of these degrees, the stars themselves have brought forth the quantities of the elements. Indeed, this spirit flourishes everywhere in everything: it is the immediate author of all generation and movement, concerning which it is said that "the spirit nourishes from within." <note>A reference to Virgil, Aeneid VI.726: "Spiritus intus alit."</note> 

By its very nature, it is entirely bright, hot, moist, and life-giving, having obtained these gifts from the higher qualities of the soul. The leader of the sages <note>original: "hierarchas," referring to Iarchas, the Indian sage mentioned in the life of Apollonius of Tyana.</note> testified that **Apollonius of Tyana** drank deeply of this spirit, saying: "No one should wonder, O Apollonius <note>original: "ò apollonite"</note>, that you have achieved the science of divination, since you carry so much ether in your soul."

->*Our spirit draws in the spirit of the world through the rays of the Sun and Jupiter, insofar as it is itself*<-
->*Solar and Jovial. Chapter IV.*<-

For the spirit itself is the middle between the thick body of the world and its soul, and the stars are contained within it.

### BOOK III
#### PAGE 164

...demons, and through the Spirit itself. For whether the body of the world and worldly things proceed directly from the **Soul of the World**, as **Plotinus** and **Porphyry** <note>Neoplatonic philosophers who believed the universe was permeated by a divine, animating soul.</note> believe, or whether the worldly body and the soul both proceed directly from God—as our own thinkers believe, and perhaps **Timaeus the Pythagorean** <note>A character in Plato’s dialogues; here representing the view that the world is a created living being.</note>—the world entirely lives and breathes, and we are permitted to draw in its spirit. 

This spirit is drawn in properly by a person through their own spirit, which is by its own nature conformable to that of the world, especially if it is made even more closely related by art—that is, if it becomes as **celestial** as possible. It becomes celestial, indeed, if it is purged of filth and of everything that clings to it that is unlike heaven. Such "filth" infects the spirit not only if it is inside the internal organs, but also if it is in the mind, on the skin, in one’s clothing, in the home, or in the air. 

It is finally made celestial if, according to the circular motion of the mind and body, it also describes its own orbits; <note>Ficino refers to the idea that human thoughts and physical health should mimic the perfect, circular movements of the stars.</note> if it refines itself through more frequent gazing upon and contemplation of light; and if things similar to heaven are applied to it with the same diligence with which **Avicenna** <note>The Latinized name of Ibn Sina, a Persian physician whose medical texts were standard in the Middle Ages and Renaissance.</note> cares for the spirit in his book *On the Powers of the Heart*, and which we ourselves strive to provide in our book *On Caring for the Health of Scholars*. 

In those works, first, the clouding vapors are separated from the spirit by medicines that purge it; second, it is illuminated by shining things; and third, it is cultivated so that it is both refined and strengthened at the same time. Finally, it will become most celestial—as far as the present reasoning dictates—if the rays and influences of the **Sun** (which dominates among the heavenly bodies) are applied to it above all. 

And so, through this spirit—acting as a medium within us—celestial benefits, which are primarily implanted in the spirit itself, will overflow into both our body and our mind. All celestial goods, I say, for all things are contained in the Sun. The Sun will contribute to making the spirit **Solar** <term>Solar spirit</term> <note>A state of the human spirit that is bright, clear, and vital, mirroring the qualities of the Sun.</note> in the proper sense when it is in the signs of **Aries** or **Leo**, while being "looked upon" by the **Moon**. This is especially true in Leo, where the Sun so enlivens our spirit that it fortifies it to repel the poison of an **epidemic**. This is clearly seen in Babylonia, Egypt, and regions pertaining to the sign of Leo, where the Sun entering Leo calms an epidemic for the very reason we have stated.

Therefore, you should also compose exquisite "solar" things everywhere; then begin to use solar things, yet with the caution that you carefully avoid dehydration under the intense heat. A solar spirit cannot easily emerge, however, unless it is very abundant. For abundance belongs especially to the Sun. This abundance is created both by diligence in fostering the heart with "cordial" <note>Medicines or substances that stimulate the heart and spirits.</note> things inside and out, and also by a diet of subtle foods that are nevertheless very nourishing, easy to digest, and healthy. 

Also required is frequent and gentle movement, timely rest, air that is thin and serene (removed from extreme heat and frost), and above all, a **joyful mind**. Again, the spirit will not be solar unless it is warm, refined, and clear. You will make it refined and clear if you avoid sad, thick, and dark things. You should use bright and joyful things, both inside and out, with much light...

### ON THE LIFE OF THE HEAVENS

...degenerating so far from the divine, it therefore needs the support of a more excellent body, which is almost as if it were not a body at all. <note>Ficino is describing the "Spirit" (spiritus), a fine, vaporous substance that mediates between the immaterial soul and the heavy, physical body.</note> Furthermore, we know that all living things, both plants and animals, live and generate through a certain spirit similar to this. Among the elements, those that are most "spiritual" <note>In this context, "spiritual" means light and airy, like fire or air, rather than the heavy elements of earth or water.</note> generate most swiftly and are in perpetual motion, as if they were alive. But you may ask meanwhile: if the elements and living creatures generate something similar to themselves through their own spirit, why do stones and metals not generate? It is because they are positioned in the middle of the elements and living things, and the spirit within them is imprisoned by thicker matter. If this spirit should ever be correctly separated and preserved, it would be able to generate its own kind just like a **seminal power**. If it is applied to a certain matter of the same kind—just as diligent physicists <note>original: "physici"; here referring to natural philosophers or alchemists.</note> separate a certain spirit from gold by a process of **sublimation** <term>Sublimation: An alchemical process of heating a substance until it becomes a vapor, then collecting the purified result as it cools.</term> using fire, and then apply it to other metals to create gold—Arabic astrologers call such a spirit, drawn properly from gold or another source and preserved, the **elixir**. 

But let us return to the **Spirit of the World**, through which the world generates all things, since it generates all things through its own spirit. We can call this spirit either "the heavens" or the **fifth essence** <term>Fifth Essence (Quintessence): A celestial substance distinct from the four earthly elements (earth, water, air, fire), thought to be the material of the stars.</term>, which is nearly the same in the body of the world as our own spirit is in ours. There is this primary exception: the **Soul of the World** does not draw this spirit from the four elements as if they were its humors (as our soul draws from ours); rather, it procreates this spirit directly (to speak in the manner of **Plato** or **Plotinus**) from its own generative power as if it were swelling with life. Along with this spirit, the soul procreates the stars, and through the spirit, it immediately gives birth to the four elements. It is as if all things exist within the power of that spirit. The spirit itself is a most thin body—almost not a body, and almost already a soul; likewise, it is almost not a soul, and almost already a body. Within its power there is certainly something of the nature of earth, but more of water, even more of air, and a great deal of the nature of fire and the stars. Ancient authorities have handed down the measures of these degrees and the quantities of the stars and elements; the spirit itself flourishes everywhere and in all things as the immediate author and motion of all generation, of which it is said: "the spirit nourishes from within." <note>A reference to Virgil’s *Aeneid* (6.726): "spiritus intus alit," describing the divine breath animating the world.</note> It is entirely bright, hot, moist, and life-giving by its own nature, having obtained these gifts from the higher qualities of the soul. **Iarchas** <note>A legendary Indian sage and king.</note> testified that **Apollonius of Tyana** <note>A famous 1st-century Greek philosopher and reputed miracle-worker.</note> had drawn deeply from this spirit, saying to us: "No one should wonder, O Apollonius, that you have obtained the science of divination, since you carry so much **ether** in your soul."

### BOOK III.

...demons, and through the spirit itself. For whether the body of the world and all worldly things arise directly from the **World Soul** <term>World Soul: The *Anima Mundi*, a Neoplatonic concept of a cosmic soul that gives life and order to the physical universe.</term>, as **Plotinus** and **Porphyry** <note>Plotinus (c. 204–270 AD) was the founder of Neoplatonism; Porphyry was his student and editor.</note> believe, or whether the worldly body and the soul both arise directly from God—as our own thinkers believe and perhaps **Timaeus the Pythagorean** <note>A character in Plato's dialogue who describes the creation of the cosmos.</note> suggests—the world is entirely alive and breathing, and we are permitted to drink in its **spirit** <term>Spirit: In Ficino's medical philosophy, "spiritus" is a fine, vaporous substance in the human body that acts as a bridge between the physical flesh and the immaterial soul.</term>. 

This spirit is properly drawn in by a person through their own spirit, which is naturally suited to it, especially if it is made even more "kin" to the heavens by art—that is, if it becomes as **celestial** as possible. It becomes celestial if it is purged of all "filth" and everything that is unlike the heavens. This "filth" refers to things that frequently infect the spirit: not just what is inside the organs, but also what is in the mind, on the skin, in one’s clothes, in the home, and in the air. 

The spirit is finally made celestial if it aligns itself with the circular motions of the mind and body; <note>Ficino believed that circular or regular movements imitated the perfect, eternal motion of the stars and planets.</note> if it refines itself through frequent contemplation of light; and if things similar to the heavens are applied to it with the same diligence that **Avicenna** <note>Avicenna (Ibn Sina, c. 980–1037) was a Persian physician whose medical works were foundational for Renaissance science.</note> used in his book *On the Powers of the Heart*, and which I myself have strived to use in my book *On Caring for the Health of Scholars*. In such a practice, first, shadowing vapors are separated from the spirit by purifying medicines; second, it is brightened by shining objects; and third, it is cultivated so that it is both refined and strengthened at the same time.

Ultimately, the spirit becomes most celestial—as far as our current reasoning dictates—if it is exposed primarily to the rays and influence of the **Sun**, which rules over all heavenly things. Thus, through this spirit (acting as the "middle ground" within us), heavenly blessings first plant themselves there and then overflow into both our body and our soul. I say all celestial blessings, for all things are contained within the Sun. 

The Sun contributes specifically to creating a **solar spirit** when it is in the signs of **Aries** or **Leo**, and when the Moon is "looking" upon it <note>This refers to an astrological "aspect," where planets are positioned at specific angles to one another.</note>. This is especially true in Leo, where the Sun nourishes our spirit so much that it guards us against the poison of the plague. This is clearly seen in Babylon and Egypt, and regions looking toward Leo, where the Sun entering Leo calms the epidemic for the reason we have stated. 

Therefore, you too should prepare exquisite "solar" items at that time, and begin to use them—though with the caution that you carefully avoid becoming dried out by the summer heat. A solar spirit cannot easily emerge unless it is abundant. Generosity and amplitude belong to the Sun. You can foster this abundance by caring for the heart with heart-strengthening things (both inside and out), and by a diet of light but highly nutritious and healthy foods. Also helpful are frequent, light movement, timely rest, thin and clear air, and—staying away from heat and frost—above all, a **joyful mind**. Furthermore, a spirit will not be "solar" unless it is warm, refined, and clear. You will make it refined and clear if you avoid sad, thick, and dark things. Use bright and joyful things, both inside and out, with much light...

# ON THE CELESTIAL LIFE. COMPENDIUM.

<meta>catchword: and those (original: easque)</meta>

Then, day and night, you shall receive this **spirit**, expel filth, and avoid idleness, sluggishness, and especially darkness. When bringing the **spirit** <term>Spirit: In Ficino’s thought, this is the "spiritus," a thin vapor that connects the physical body to the soul.</term> to the natural heat of the Sun, beware that you do not lead it to the third degree of heat or to dryness. For the heat of the Sun itself does not naturally dry things out; <note>original: "non exsiccat"</note> otherwise, it would not be the Sun of life, the lord of generation, and the author of growth. Rather, drying occurs by its rays only when they are trapped within the hollows of dry matter. 

Therefore, you shall apply a subtle moisture to this heat—the kind of moisture belonging to the Sun, and especially to Jupiter—and you will preserve it in the spirit by using such things. If you are intending to create a "solar" effect, take care that you do not accidentally lead the spirit toward a "Martial" <note>Martial: Relating to the planet Mars, which Ficino associated with excessive, destructive heat and anger.</note> state rather than a Solar one. They say that Mars is like the Sun in only a few, obvious, and not very excellent ways, and is meanwhile considered its enemy. But we know that **Jupiter** is like the Sun in many excellent (though more hidden) gifts, and is its dearest friend. 

Hence **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the most influential astronomer and astrologer of antiquity.</note>, when discussing harmony <note>original: "consonantia"</note>, says that Jupiter harmonizes most perfectly with the Sun above all others, and **Venus** with the **Moon**. All astrologers attribute a "universal beneficence" to the Sun, just as they do to Jupiter, although the Sun acts more effectively. Jupiter works under the power of the Sun. In both, heat flourishes and overcomes moisture; but in Jupiter it overcomes it only moderately, while in the Sun it overcomes it excellently—and in both cases, it is beneficial. 

Since they harmonize so well, you will easily be able to make your spirit solar just as you make it Jovian <note>Jovian: Relating to the planet Jupiter, associated with health, justice, and balanced growth.</note>, and you can rightly mix solar and Jovian things together. This is especially true if you combine them and apply them to the spirit when Jupiter looks toward the Sun in a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <term>Aspect: The geometric angle between two planets in the sky, believed to influence their power.</term>, or at least when the Moon moves from an aspect with one to an aspect with the other—most of all when it moves from an aspect with the Sun toward a **conjunction** <term>Conjunction: When two celestial bodies appear in the same part of the sky.</term> with Jupiter. 

Separately, you will specifically create a solar or Jovian spirit when you observe the Moon’s aspect to the Sun or to Jupiter; however, once you have attained the nature of one, you will soon easily attain the nature of the other. Understand a **sextile aspect** to be when two planets are separated by the space of two zodiac signs, and a **trine aspect** when they are separated by an interval of four signs. We measure a conjunction or the Moon’s aspect to others within twelve degrees before or after the exact point.

-> *There are three Graces: Jupiter, the Sun, and Venus. Jupiter is the middle grace between the two, and the one most suited to us.* <margin>Chapter V.</margin> <-

You will find Jovian compositions and cures, as well as solar ones, in our book *On Long Life* and in the book *On the Care of the Learned*. In those works, we also mixed in many things of **Venus**; for we fear a "drying out" in those who are studious, which Venus resists. This same Venus is a very dear friend to Jupiter, just as she is to the Sun. Jupiter is, as it were, the three Graces concordant and joined among themselves. From these three "graces of heaven," and from stars of the same kind, astrologers both hope for and diligently seek out favors <gloss>original: "gratias," meaning both astronomical influences and divine favors/graces</gloss>.

and they believe those things are transmitted through Mercury and the Moon as if by messengers, and they manage this easily and commonly through the Moon. We will therefore use the influence of **Jupiter** when both he and the **Moon** possess both natural and accidental dignity <term>Dignity: A planet's strength or influence based on its position in a particular zodiac sign or its relationship to other planets.</term>, and when they are together or looking upon each other happily. ### *On the natural, vital, and animal virtue within us, and through which planets they are aided, and how through the aspect of the Moon to the Sun and Venus, but especially to Jupiter. Chapter VI.*

But the primary discipline is to correctly understand which spirit, what power, and what matter these planets especially signify. The **Moon** and **Venus**, therefore, signify the natural and generative power and spirit, and those things that increase it. **Jupiter** signifies the same, but more effectively, as well as the liver and stomach; he also has no small part in the heart, the spirit, and the **vital virtue** <term>Vital virtue: The power responsible for life-sustaining functions like breathing and the heartbeat.</term>, insofar as he agrees with the **Sun** by his very nature, or rather through himself. Otherwise, the heart would not properly receive the vital spirit in the "month of Jupiter." <note>This refers to the stages of fetal development or planetary hours where Jupiter governs life-giving force.</note> Hence the Greeks call **Jupiter** "life," and "he through whom life exists." <note>original: "Iouem græci appellant uitam" — a reference to the Greek name Zeus, which was etymologically linked to 'zēn' (to live).</note>

# ON THE CELESTIAL LIFE. SUMMARY.

<meta>catchword: gari</meta>

Such is the mind of men as the father of gods and men <note>original: "pater hominum atque deorum"; a reference to Jupiter or the Sun, often quoting a sentiment from Homer’s Odyssey.</note> brings with each day. In no place truly is any other divinity so named except for **Jupiter**. The **Sun** signifies primarily the <term>vital spirit</term> <note>Spiritus vitalis: In Renaissance medicine, a subtle substance that carries life-force from the heart through the arteries.</note> and the heart; it also possesses no small influence in the head on account of sense and motion, of which it is the master, nor does it desert its natural power. **Mercury** governs the brain and the instruments of the senses, and therefore the <term>animal spirit</term> <note>Spiritus animalis: A refined vapor thought to reside in the brain and travel through the nerves to facilitate thought and movement.</note>; consequently, the safest path will be to do nothing without the favor of the **Moon**. This is because she commonly, frequently, and easily transmits celestial things to the lower realms. 

They call her a "second Sun," as she creates the four seasons of the year within every single month. For in her first quarter, the Peripatetics <note>Peripatetics: Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note> believe her to be hot and moist; in the second, hot and dry; in the third, cold and dry; and in the fourth, cold and moist. Her light is beyond doubt the light of the **Sun**, governing the <term>humors</term> <note>Humors: The four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) that determined health and temperament.</note> and generation. She measures all the changes of the fetus in the womb by her own cycles, and whenever she is joined to the **Sun**, she receives a life-giving virtue from him, which she pours into the humors. At that same point, she receives from **Mercury** a power that mixes the humors. **Mercury** brings this power through his transformations and his many-layered orbits; then she soon receives from **Venus** a power that leads toward the forms suitable for procreation.

It will be worthwhile to remember that the daily course of the **Moon** is also distributed into four quarters. In the first, she rises from the East to the mid-heaven, and meanwhile increases the humor and the <term>natural spirit</term>. In the second, she seeks the setting from the mid-heaven, and produces the opposite effect in us. In the third, she goes from the setting to the point below the mid-heaven <note>The "Imum Coeli" or the lowest point of the sky below the horizon.</note>, and again increases that spirit and humor. In the fourth, she falls from there back toward the rising, and decreases them in turn. This is most apparent on the shores of the ocean, where the sea visibly advances and recedes according to this course, and the vigor in the sick follows the same order. 

It is also probable that the **Sun** increases or diminishes natural heat and the vital spirit through these same quarters of its own, and the animal spirit as well, insofar as it has **Mercury** as a companion. Having learned these things, the physician will be able to observe the more opportune times for restoring the humors, natural heat, and any spirit. 

But enough about the **Moon** for now. Nor is it right to pass over **Jupiter**, in whose second month we received life, and in whose other month we were commonly and more happily born <note>Ficino refers to the traditional astrological belief that Jupiter governs the second and ninth months of fetal development.</note>; and because he is the middle in quality and effect between the **Sun** and **Venus**, as well as between the **Sun** and the **Moon**, he therefore embraces all things. We consider it impious and dangerous to overlook the **Sun** itself, the lord of the heavens, unless perhaps one says that he who has **Jupiter** already has the **Sun** within him—for in **Jupiter**, the **Sun** is most perfectly tempered for human beings. Not only Iamblichus and Julian <note>Iamblichus and Julian the Apostate: Neoplatonic philosophers who emphasized the central, divine role of the Sun.</note> but everyone affirms that all the virtues of the celestial beings are certainly in the **Sun**. And **Proclus** says that at the sight of the **Sun**, all the virtues of all the celestial beings assemble...

# BOOK III.

...to be gathered together in one and collected. No one will deny that **Jupiter** is a kind of **Sun** tempered for our benefit. You should also not neglect the **Moon**, when she is tempered toward **Venus**. She helps greatly toward a strong and prosperous life, since **Venus** makes a man fertile and joyful; therefore, you shall observe her. Though if you properly mix the **Moon**—which is similar to **Venus**, equal in moisture, and scarcely less warm—with **Jupiter**, or if you mix her with the **Sun** when you already have **Venus** nearby, you have performed the rite correctly. 

What then? To walk the safest and most convenient path of all, observe the **Moon** when she looks toward the **Sun** and joins with **Jupiter**, or at least looks toward both **Jupiter** and the **Sun** at once. Or certainly, observe when, after looking at the **Sun**, she soon proceeds to a conjunction or aspect with **Jupiter**. At that very time, combine or apply to yourself solar, Jovial, and Venerean things all together. 

If necessity urges you to take refuge in only one of the great planets, or if your business is with **Jupiter** himself, take refuge in the **Moon** and **Jupiter** together. For no star fosters and strengthens our natural powers—indeed, all of them—more than **Jupiter**. Furthermore, no star promises more prosperous or more numerous things, and it is auspicious to receive his influence everywhere. To receive the **Sun**, however, is perhaps not safe in every case; for while the former <note>referring to Jupiter</note> always helps, the latter <note>referring to the Sun</note> often seems to cause harm <note>The Sun's heat can be too intense or "combust," whereas Jupiter's heat is considered perfectly balanced for human life.</note>. **Venus** is, as it were, weak; therefore, he alone <note>Jupiter</note> is called the "Helping Father" <note>original: "iuuans pater"; this is the classical etymology for the name "Iupiter" (Iovis + Pater).</note>. 

Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century mathematician and astronomer whose 'Tetrabiblos' was the foundational text for Western astrology.</note> confirms this when he says that a medicine <term>pharmacum</term> <note>original: "pharmacum"; in this context, it refers specifically to a purgative or a drug intended to move the humors.</note> scarcely moves nature at all when the **Moon** joins with **Jupiter**, because he thinks that the entire nature of the whole body is so thoroughly strengthened from that source. I have also found through experience that when the **Moon** is joined with **Venus**, medicine scarcely moves the body. 

Now, when we greatly fear <term>phlegm</term> <note>original: "pituitam"; the cold, moist humor associated with lethargy and respiratory issues.</note>, we should especially observe the **Moon** in relation to the **Sun**; but where we fear <term>bile</term> <note>original: "bilem"; specifically yellow bile, which is hot and dry.</note> and similar drying effects, we look to **Venus**. Nevertheless, the **Moon's** direction toward **Jupiter** helps in all these matters in some way, and especially for expelling <term>black bile</term> <note>original: "atram bilem"; also known as melancholy, the cold and dry humor.</note>, as well as for restoring and strengthening the common <term>complexion</term> <note>Complexion: Not just skin tone, but the specific balance of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) that determines a person's health and temperament.</note> of men. 

For just as liquorice <note>original: "glyzirhiza".</note> and oil of roses warm things that are too cold and cool things that are too hot, and wine does the same—and moreover, as it moistens dry things and dries overly moist ones—so **Jupiter** is agreeable to human heat, like wine, rose oil, chamomile, and liquorice. 

So when you hear Albumasar <note>Albumasar: Ja'far ibn Muhammad Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886), a highly influential Persian astrologer and astronomer.</note> saying there is no life for living things except through God, and through the **Sun** and **Moon**, understand this as far as it concerns the common <term>influence</term> <note>original: "influxum"; the "pouring in" of celestial power from the stars to the terrestrial world.</note> for everyone. However, the influence from **Jupiter** is more specific and most suited to man. There are in the nature of the body the powers of attracting, retaining, <term>digesting</term> <note>original: "coquendi"; literally 'cooking,' the physiological process by which the body's innate heat transforms food into humors.</note>, and expelling; **Jupiter** himself helps all of these, but especially the power of digesting, as well as those of generating, nourishing, and growing. This is because of his airy and abundant moisture and his ample heat, which holds a moderate dominance over the moisture. Truly, through the rays of **Jupiter**, [they] are always spread everywhere...

### ON THE LIFE OF THE HEAVENS. COMPENDIUM.
<meta>catchword: especially</meta>

...poured out the **Sun's** <note>original: "Solis"</note> own light, which is especially tempered for the health of men, while the rays of **Venus** <note>original: "Veneris"</note> diligently contribute to the same end. And in a similar way, when the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note> transfers these influences, the rays of **Venus** and the **Moon**, being somewhat wetter, require a tempering agent, just as the rays of the **Sun**, being hotter, demand the tempering of something wetter. The rays of **Jupiter** <note>original: "Iouis"</note>, however, require no such tempering. For what else is **Jupiter** <note>original: "Iuppiter"</note> but a kind of **Sun**, tempered from the beginning for the health of things, especially human ones? What else is he again, if not the **Moon** and **Venus**, though made warmer and more powerful? Therefore, astrologers begin a fertile, serene, and healthy year with **Jupiter**, and from him they hope for remedies for impending diseases. And **Empedocles** <note>A Greek Pre-Socratic philosopher who theorized that the universe was composed of four elements</note>, when assigning specific duties to each of the planets, names **Jupiter** alone as the prince of generation, following the tradition of **Orpheus**.

Besides **Jupiter**, they instruct that the **Moon** must be carefully preserved <note>Meaning kept in a favorable state or "fortified"</note> in all works as a suitable medium between celestial and earthly things. Therefore, let the **Moon** be in the degree, position, and aspect appropriate for the desired work; she should not be on the ecliptic <note>original: "eclyptica"; here referring to the path where eclipses occur, which was considered unlucky</note>, nor under the rays of the **Sun** within twelve degrees before or after <note>This refers to the Moon being "combust," or overwhelmed by the Sun's light</note>, unless by chance she is in the same minute as the **Sun**. Indeed, most scholars hold that all planets will be strong when they exist in "unity" with the **Sun**. They measure this unity as thirty-two minutes, such that sixteen are counted before and sixteen after <note>This specific position is called "Cazimi," meaning "in the heart of the Sun," where a planet's power is thought to be purified and boosted rather than burned.</note>. She should not be hindered by **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturno"</note> or **Mars** <note>original: "Marte"</note>, nor should she descend into southern latitude when she departs from those twelve degrees. She should not be opposite the **Sun**, nor waning in light, nor slow in her course—that is, when she does not complete twelve degrees in a single day. She should not be in the "burned path" <note>original: "combuſta gradu"; the *via combusta*, a section of the zodiac considered malefic</note> from the 28th degree of **Libra** <note>original: "libræ"</note> to the 3rd of **Scorpio** <note>original: "Scorpionis"</note>, nor in the eighth house, nor in the ascendant, nor in the "terms" <note>Subdivisions of zodiac signs</note> of **Mars** or **Saturn**. Some also do not want the **Moon** in the sixth, twelfth, ninth, or fourth houses, but they approve of her in the other regions of the sky.

Where you cannot satisfy all these conditions, at least wait for **Jupiter** or **Venus** to be in the ascendant or the tenth house; for in this way, they come to the aid of the **Moon’s** detriments. Nor would it be out of place to remember that as the **Moon** increases in light, so too are our moisture, spirit, and virtue increased, and these expand toward the periphery, especially in her second quarter. But when she wanes, the opposite happens, especially in the last quarter; her first trine aspect to the **Sun** is better than the second, and the first sextile better than the second; as the **Moon** is filled with light, she is likewise filled with heat. It seems, therefore, that some do not observe how the **Moon** "looks" at the **Sun**—for she always looks at him—so much as they observe that she should have her first light, especially while she is increasing. Meanwhile, let her look upon **Jupiter** or **Venus** with a trine or sextile aspect; accordingly, fiery things aid the <term>attractive power</term> <note>original: "virtutem attractiuam"; the faculty of the body that draws in nutrients</note>, earthy things the <term>retentive power</term> <note>original: "retentiuam"; the faculty that holds nutrients in place</note>, airy things the <term>digestive power</term> <note>original: "digestiuam"</note>, and watery things the <term>expulsive power</term> <note>original: "expulſiuam"; the faculty that eliminates waste</note>. If you wish to aid all these within yourself, use the attractive power through fire...

### BOOK III.

...you will most greatly strengthen <note>Referring to the attractive or appetitive faculty mentioned on the previous page</note>, when the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note> is positioned in the fiery signs or stations and looks upon **Jupiter** <note>original: "Iouem"</note>; specifically, in **Aries**, **Leo**, or **Sagittarius**. You will strengthen the **retentive** faculty <note>original: "Retentiuam"</note> through the earth signs, especially when she gazes upon him while she is located in the signs or stations of earth: **Taurus**, **Virgo**, and **Capricorn**. You will strengthen the **digestive** and **generative** faculties through the air signs, **Gemini**, **Libra**, and **Aquarius**, whenever she receives or enters **Jupiter** under those airy signs. You will strengthen the **expulsive** <note>original: "Expulſiuam"</note> faculty through the water signs, **Cancer**, **Pisces**, and **Scorpio**, when she herself is placed under the water signs and is illuminated by the rays of **Jupiter**. You will most greatly achieve your desired results in all these matters if **Jupiter** occupies the same signs, or similar ones, or at least those that are not too dissimilar.

To move the bowels with solid medicines, choose **Pisces**; with liquid ones, **Scorpio**; and for moderate ones, **Cancer**. To purge through the lower parts, choose **Pisces** and **Scorpio**; through the upper parts, **Cancer**. You shall avoid the harmful aspect of **Saturn** or **Mars** toward the **Moon**; for the former vexes the stomach, while the latter dissolves the intestines. You should avoid **Capricorn** and **Taurus**, for they bring about nausea. You know that a limb should not be irritated <note>Through surgery or harsh treatment</note> when the **Moon** occupies the sign governing that limb, for she moves the humors; rather, the limb should be soothed. Let these words suffice regarding the power and the **natural spirit** <note>The spirit responsible for basic biological functions like nutrition and growth</note> which dominates chiefly in the liver, and which is divided into the four offices we have described.

But what do we advise regarding the **vital power** and **spirit** <note>The spirit responsible for heat and life-force</note> flourishing in the heart? This has already been sufficiently indicated. For these are aided primarily by fiery things and, in a certain way, by airy things at the same time, when the **Moon** in similar houses or stations looks up to **Jupiter**, especially if she embraces both **Jupiter** and the **Sun**. You can also confirm the **animal power** <note>The power of the "anima" or soul, governing the brain, senses, and movement</note> which dominates in the head through sense and motion, primarily through airy signs with fiery ones joined to them, and when the **Moon** looks up to **Jupiter** in similar houses or seats, especially if she embraces **Jupiter** and **Mercury** almost together.

Here, however, I warn you not to think that **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercuriũ"</note> is watery or earthy—something I also once suspected—otherwise he would not contribute to the movements and speed of the intellect; rather, you should know that he is in some way airy. For this same reason he is so mobile, so easily changeable, and contributes so much to talent, especially when he is positioned in **Aquarius**, which is most airy. Indeed, the moisture in him is tempered, his heat is slight; when placed under the **Sun** he is said to dry out, but when moved further from the **Sun** he is thought to moisten, though there he certainly heats up much from the nature of the **Sun**. Here, however <note>meaning when further away</note>, he heats very little and moistens more by his own nature; in heat, perhaps, he does not yield to **Venus**, and he surpasses the **Moon**, but in moisture he yields to both. Others prove that **Mercury** mixes the qualities of the heavens because he is very easily changed, both into the quality of the boundary he enters and into the nature of the star he gazes upon. I, therefore, think he is so easily changed because he has neither the excellent power that **Jupiter** has, nor the exceeding quality that most celestial bodies possess, by which he might resist alteration. Finally, it is probable that **Mercury**, as the constant companion of the **Sun**...

# BOOK III.

### ON THE COMPARISON OF THE CELESTIAL LIFE

...you will strengthen [the attractive power] most greatly when the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note>, positioned in fiery signs or stations, looks upon **Jupiter** <note>original: "Iouem"</note>—namely in **Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius**. You will strengthen the retentive power primarily through earthy signs, when she gazes upon the same [Jupiter] while placed in earthy signs or stations: **Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn**. The digestive and generative powers are strengthened through the airy signs—**Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius**—whenever she looks up at or enters Jupiter's influence under airy signs. The expulsive power is strengthened through the watery signs—**Cancer, Pisces, and Scorpio**—when she is herself placed in watery signs and illuminated by the rays of Jupiter. You will most especially achieve your desired results in all these matters if Jupiter himself occupies these same signs, or similar ones, or at least signs that are not entirely dissimilar.

If you are about to move the bowels with solid medicines, choose **Pisces**; with liquid ones, **Scorpio**; and for moderate ones, **Cancer**. To purge through the lower parts <note>referring to laxatives</note>, choose Pisces and Scorpio; to purge through the upper parts <note>referring to emetics</note>, choose Cancer. You shall avoid an evil aspect of **Saturn** or **Mars** to the Moon; for the former [Saturn] vexes the stomach, while the latter [Mars] dissolves the intestines. You shall avoid **Capricorn** and **Taurus**, for they bring about nausea. You know that a limb should not be provoked <note>such as through surgery or harsh treatment</note> when the Moon occupies the sign governing that limb—for she moves the humors there—but rather that limb should be cherished. Let these things said concerning the **natural virtue** <note>original: "virtute... naturali"; the faculty governing nutrition and growth</note> and the spirit which dominates chiefly in the **liver**—which are divided into the four functions we have described—be sufficient.

But what do we advise regarding the **vital virtue** and the spirit flourishing in the **heart**? This has been fairly well indicated: for these are aided primarily through fiery and, in a way, simultaneously airy things, when the Moon in similar houses or mansions looks up at Jupiter, especially if she embraces both Jupiter and the **Sun**. You can also confirm the **animal virtue** <note>original: "virtutem... animalem"; the faculty of the "anima" or soul, governing sensation and thought in the brain</note> ruling through sense and motion in the **head**, primarily through airy signs with fiery ones joined, and when the Moon in similar houses or seats looks up at Jupiter, especially if she closely embraces Jupiter and **Mercury**.

Here I warn you: do not think Mercury is watery or earthy (as I once suspected), otherwise he would not contribute to the movements and speed of the intellect; rather, know that he is in some way airy. For this same reason he is so mobile, so easily changeable, and contributes so much to the intellect, especially when positioned in **Aquarius**, which is a most airy sign. His humor is indeed tempered and his heat is meager; when placed under the Sun he is said to dry things out, but when he is further from the Sun he is thought to moisten—there [near the Sun] heating much from the nature of the Sun, but here [far from the Sun] heating very little and moistening more by his own nature. In heat perhaps he does not yield to **Venus** and surpasses the Moon, but in humor he yields to both. Others prove that Mercury mingles the qualities of the celestials because he is very easily changed, both into the quality of the "term" <note>an astrological subdivision of a sign</note> he enters and the nature of the star he beholds. I therefore think he is so easily changed because he has neither an excellent power (such as Jupiter has) nor an exceeding quality (which many other celestials have) through which he might resist alteration. Finally, it is probable that Mercury, as the constant [companion] of the Sun...

# ON THE CELESTIAL LIFE. COMPARISON.

...the Sun's <note>original: "Solis"</note> own light, poured out, is most greatly tempered for human health, with the rays of **Venus** meanwhile constantly contributing to the same effect. And likewise, when the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note> transmits the light, the rays of Venus and the Moon, being somewhat more humid, require a tempering agent; just as the Sun's rays, being hotter, require the tempering of something more humid. But the rays of **Jupiter** <note>original: "Iouis"</note> require no tempering; for what else is Jupiter except a kind of Sun, tempered from the very beginning for the welfare of things, especially human ones? What else is he, again, but a Moon and a Venus made warmer and more powerful? Therefore, astrologers take their favorable start from Jupiter for a fertile, serene, and healthy year, and from him they hope for remedies for imminent diseases. 

And **Empedocles**, when he assigns the proper roles to each of the planets, names Jupiter alone as the "prince of generation," following the teachings of **Orpheus**. In addition to Jupiter, they instruct that the **Moon** must be diligently observed in all works as a suitable intermediary between celestial and earthly things. 

Let the Moon, therefore, be in a degree, position, and aspect appropriate for the desired work; let her not be on the ecliptic <note>the path where eclipses occur, considered unstable</note>, nor under the rays of the Sun within twelve degrees before or after, unless by chance she is in the same minute as the Sun. Most people, however, maintain that all planets will be at their strongest when they exist in "unity" <note>often called 'cazimi', or being in the heart of the Sun</note> with the Sun. They measure this unity as thirty-two minutes: sixteen counted before the center of the Sun and sixteen after. 

Let her not be hindered by **Saturn** or **Mars**, nor descend into southern latitude when she departs from those twelve degrees mentioned. Let her not be opposite the Sun, nor diminished in light, nor slow in her course—that is, when she does not travel twelve degrees in a single day. Let her not be in the <term>Via Combusta: "The Burned Path," a section of the zodiac traditionally considered unlucky or debilitating for the Moon</term> from the 28th degree of **Libra** to the 3rd of **Scorpio**, nor in the eighth house, nor in the Ascendant <note>the first house of a chart</note>, nor in the "terms" <note>specific subdivisions of the zodiac signs</note> of Mars or Saturn. 

Some, indeed, do not want the Moon in the sixth, twelfth, ninth, or fourth houses, but they approve of her in the other regions. Where you cannot encompass all these conditions, wait at least for Jupiter or **Venus** to be in the Ascendant or the tenth house; for in this way they help remedy the Moon's weaknesses. Nor would it be out of place to remember that as the Moon increases in light, so too in us not only moisture, but also spirit <note>the vital pneuma or life-force</note> and virtue are increased, and these expand to the periphery <note>the surface of the body or limbs</note> most especially in her second quarter. 

When she decreases, however, the opposite happens, especially in the final quarter. Her first **Trine** <note>an aspect of 120 degrees</note> to the Sun is superior to the second, this one is superior to the first **Sextile** <note>60 degrees</note>, and this to the second sextile; as the Moon is filled with light, so she is filled with heat. Therefore, some seem to observe not so much how the Moon gazes upon the Sun—for she is always gazing—but rather that she should have her "first light," especially while she is increasing. Meanwhile, let her look upon Jupiter or Venus with a Trine or Sextile aspect. Accordingly, fiery things help the attractive power, earthy things the retentive, airy things the digestive, and watery things the expulsive. If you wish to assist all these in yourself, indeed the attractive through fir[y]...

**Agate** <note>original: "Achatem"</note> possesses many of its powers, and therefore some solar relief can be hoped for from **Mercury**. They also say that **Mars** sometimes imitates the **Sun** in certain duties, and that **Venus** bestows those things that pertain to the **Moon**. Remember these things when acting, and never neglect the *terms* <note>astrological subdivisions of zodiac signs that modify a planet's power</note>. For they say that the planets act in opposite ways in different terms, as if in light or dark spaces. Finally, where you fear Mars, oppose him with **Venus**; where you fear **Saturn**, apply **Jupiter**. Strive to remain in a constant state of motion according to your strength—avoiding exhaustion—so that you may oppose your own internal motion against external motions that would secretly cause harm, thereby imitating celestial activity. If you are able to cover wider spaces in your movements, you will better imitate the heavens and reach more of the celestial forces scattered everywhere.

### *How the limbs are fostered within us by comparing the Moon to the signs and to the fixed stars. Chapter VII.*

You will be able to foster the whole body (as we have said), but the head especially if you observe the planets in **Aries**, or each in its first house; the chest <note>the region of the heart and diaphragm</note> if they are in **Leo**; the stomach and liver if in **Cancer** and **Sagittarius**, or at least in **Virgo**. You should also take those things which specifically seek out that limb. It is also useful to know which limbs each planet governs in any given sign. You can also specifically consult for anyone according to the difference of their age through the **four ages of the moon**. For from the new moon until the first quarter, she is "youthful"; then until the full moon, she is "youthful and virile"; from there to the second quarter, she is "virile and senile" at once; and from then until the conjunction <note>the return to a new moon</note>, she is "senile." Therefore, you will successfully apply the age of the Moon to the age of the body being treated if you then catch her looking toward one of the **Three Graces** <note>In Ficino’s astrology, the "Three Graces" are the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus</note>; for such aspects of the Moon always and quickly bestow favors. 

However, these benefits are not easily long-lasting or very great unless, besides the gaze of the Moon, the Graces themselves look upon each other, or are just about to look upon each other—either all three or at least two of them. Long-lasting benefits are especially provided by the **fixed signs**, namely **Aquarius**, **Taurus**, and **Scorpius**. If by chance you cannot opportunely direct the Moon toward the gracious planets at the present time, choose **fixed stars** possessing the nature of the Graces—that is, of Jupiter, Venus, or the Sun—and choose a Moon directed toward them. It is safer, however, for the Moon to nearly approach Jupiter or Venus in the meantime. For if the fixed stars look toward the Sun, they far exceed the human proportion—that is, the scale of a single man—but they maintain a proper moderation for the scale of cities <note>Fixed stars were believed to influence large-scale events and nations more than individual health</note>.

## On the virtues and the use of the fixed stars. Chapter VIII.

Astrologers report that certain major stars, discovered by Mercury, possess the greatest authority. Such is the star at the 22nd degree of Aries: the **navel of Andromeda** <note>original: "umbilicus Adromedae," the star Mirach</note>, which has the nature of Mercury and Venus. Likewise, at the 18th degree of Taurus is **Algol’s head** <note>original: "caput algol"</note>, possessing the nature of Saturn and Jupiter; they claim that the diamond <note>original: "adamantem"</note> and mugwort are subject to it, and that it provides audacity and victory. At the 22nd degree of the same sign [Taurus] are the **Pleiades**, a lunar and Martial constellation <note>influenced by the Moon and Mars</note>, to which they subject crystal, the herb *diacedon* <note>a term from old pharmacopoeia, likely a specific medicinal mixture or a corruption of a plant name</note>, and fennel seed; they think these help to sharpen the sight. As for what some say about this star being useful for summoning demons, I judge it to be a fiction. **Aldebaran** <note>original: "Aldeboram"</note>, at the first or third degree of Gemini, is of the nature of Mars and Venus. **The Goat** <note>original: "Hircus," the star Capella</note> at the 13th degree of the same sign is Jovial <note>of Jupiter</note> and Saturnine; to this they subject sapphire, leek-green stone <note>original: "prassium," likely prase or chrysoprase</note>, mint, mugwort, and mandrake. They trust it to help in obtaining dignity and the favor of princes, unless perhaps their opinion deceives them. To the next <note>Ficino is referring to Sirius here</note> they assign the ruby, spurge, and honeysuckle <note>original: "matri sylvam"</note> to increase riches and glory. At the 6th or 7th degree of Cancer, the **Greater Dog** <note>Sirius</note>, being of the nature of Venus, presides over beryl, savin, mugwort, and dragonwort; it bestows favor. Likewise, at the 17th degree of the same sign, the **Lesser Dog** <note>Procyon</note>, being of the nature of Mercury and Mars, to which they assign the agate stone, the heliotrope herb <note>original: "solsequiam," literally 'sun-follower'</note>, and pennyroyal, and it grants favor. At the 21st degree of Leo is the **Heart of the Lion** <note>Regulus</note>, a royal star of the nature of Jupiter and Mars; to this they subject the garnet, celandine, and mastic; it is said to repress melancholy and make one temperate and gracious. At the 19th degree of Virgo is the **Tail of the Great Bear** <note>Alkaid</note>, having the nature of Venus and the Moon; they think its stone is the magnet [lodestone], and its herbs are chicory and mugwort, which protect against robbers and sorcerers. At the 7th degree of Libra is the **Right Wing of the Raven**, and at the 12th or perhaps 13th of the same sign is the **Left Wing** <note>Algorab</note>. These are of the nature of Saturn and Mars; they say its herbs are dock and henbane, along with frog’s tongue, which increase an audacity that may be harmful. At the 15th or 16th degree of the same sign is **Spica**, of the nature of Venus and Mercury, followed by the emerald, sage, trefoil, mugwort, and mandrake; it may increase riches and victory, and deliver one from distress. Finally, at the 17th or 18th degree of the same sign is **Alchamet** <note>Arcturus</note>; to this they subject jasper and plantain, hoping to staunch blood and expel all fevers. At the 4th degree of Scorpio is **Elpheia** <note>Alphecca</note>, of the nature of Venus and Mars—though according to another calculation at the 5th degree of the same is Cornea, perhaps the same one—presiding over topaz, rosemary, trefoil, and ivy; they believe it increases favor, chastity, and glory. At the 3rd degree of Sagittarius is the **Heart of the Scorpion** <note>Antares</note>, of the nature of Mars and Jupiter, presiding over sardonyx, amethyst, long birthwort, and saffron. They are of the opinion that it creates a good complexion, makes the mind joyful and wise, and drives away demons. At the 7th degree of Capricorn is the **Falling Vulture** <note>Vega</note>; this is followed by chrysolite, savory, and fumitory. The star is of the nature of Mercury and

You will be able to nourish the whole body (as we have said), but the head especially if you observe the planets in Aries, or each in its first <term>domicile</term> <note>the zodiac sign where a planet is most "at home"</note>; the midriff <note>original: "praecordia," the area around the heart and diaphragm</note> if they are in Leo; the stomach and liver if in Cancer and Sagittarius, or at least in Virgo. Therefore, you will successfully apply the age of the Moon to the age of the body being treated, if you then catch its <term>aspect</term> <note>the geometric angle between celestial bodies</note> to any of the <term>three Graces</term> <note>Ficino identifies these as the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus</note>, for a gaze from the Moon always and quickly bestows grace. However, these effects are not easily lasting or very great unless, besides the gaze of the Moon, the Graces themselves also behold each other, or are just about to do so—either all three, or at least two. Lasting signs are provided primarily by the **fixed signs**, namely **Leo, Aquarius, Taurus, and Scorpio**. If by chance you cannot conveniently direct the Moon toward the gracious planets at the present time, choose **fixed stars** having the nature of the Graces (that is, of Jupiter, Venus, or the Sun) and choose a Moon directed toward them. However, it is safer meanwhile for the Moon to nearly approach Jupiter or Venus. For if the fixed stars regard the Sun, they exceed human proportion too much (that is, the scale of a single man), though they maintain moderation in proportion to cities.

### On the virtues and use of the fixed stars. Chapter VIII.

**A**strologers report that certain major stars discovered by Mercury <note>The god Mercury was traditionally credited with the invention of astronomy and astrology</note> possess the greatest authority, such as the one at the 22nd degree of Aries: the **navel of Andromeda**, which is of the nature of Mercury and Venus. At the 19th degree of Virgo is the **Tail of the Great Bear**, of Venus and the Moon; they think its stone is the **lodestone**, and its herbs are **chicory** and **mugwort**, to protect against robbers and poisoners. ->ON THE VITALITY OF THE HEAVENS. COMPENDIUM.<-

and a tempered Venusian influence in the Ascendant or the Mid-heaven is beneficial. However, as for what they say regarding the authority to cast spells <note>original: "excātandi auctoritatem," referring to incantations or magic</note>, I think nothing of it. At the 16th degree of Aquarius is the **Tail of Capricorn** <note>the star Deneb Algedi</note>, which is of the nature of Saturn and Mercury. They believe the stones and herbs subject to it—**chalcedony** <note>original: "calcidonius"</note>, **marjoram**, **catnip**, **mugwort**, and **mandrake**—offer grace in legal cases, increase riches, and return a man safely to his home. At the third degree of Pisces is the **Shoulder of the Horse** <note>the star Markab in the constellation Pegasus</note>, of the nature of Jupiter and Mars.

**Thebit** the philosopher <note>Thabit ibn Qurra (826–901 AD), a famous Sabian scholar and astronomer from Harran known for his work on talismans</note> teaches that to capture the virtue of any of the stars just mentioned, one should take its stone and its herb and make a ring of gold or silver. You should place the small stone into the ring with the herb placed underneath it, and wear it so that it touches the skin. You should perform this when the Moon is passing under the star, or beholds it in a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>Trine and sextile are favorable astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively</note>, and while the star is running through the mid-heaven or the ascendant.

I, however, believe that matters relating to such stars should be composed into the form of **medicine** to be applied internally or externally, rather than a ring—observing, of course, the opportunity of the aforementioned timing—even though they have praised the rings for Pisces. For **Damis** and **Philostratus** <note>Philostratus wrote the "Life of Apollonius of Tyana"; Damis was Apollonius's disciple</note> relate that **Iarchas** <note>Hiarchas</note>, the prince of the Indian sages, made seven rings by a similar method, named after the names of the seven stars <note>the seven classical planets</note>, and gave them to **Apollonius of Tyana**. Apollonius then wore each one on its specific day, distinguishing them according to the names of the days. Indeed, Iarchas told Apollonius that his own grandfather, a philosopher, had lived for one hundred and thirty years, perhaps relying on a heavenly gift of this kind. Apollonius himself, having used them, was said to still look like a young man even in his hundredth year.

Finally, if such rings have any power from on high, I do not think it pertains as much to the soul, or to the gross body, as it does to the **spirit** <term>spiritus</term> <note>In Ficino's medical philosophy, the "spirit" is a subtle, airy vapor that acts as the bridge between the physical body and the immaterial soul</note>. As the ring is gradually warmed, the spirit is affected this way or that, so that it becomes firmer, or brighter, more vehement, or milder, more serious, or more joyful. These affections certainly pass entirely into the body and, in a certain way, into the sensory soul, which for the most part indulges the body. As for the promise that these rings are useful against demons or enemies, or for obtaining the favor of princes: this is either a fiction, or it is derived from the fact that they make the spirit fearless and firm, or even gentle, lovable in its obedience, and gracious.

Indeed, if I were to say that celestial things—beyond physical health—contribute anything to intellect, art, or fortune, I would not disagree with our own **Thomas Aquinas**. In the third book of *Against the Gentiles* <note>Summa Contra Gentiles, Book III, Chapter 92</note>, he proves that something is imprinted upon our body by the celestial bodies, by whose gift we are often disposed toward choosing what is better, even if we do not know the reason or the end. In this matter, he calls such people "well-fortuned," and, in agreement with **Aristotle**, "well-born." He even adds that by celestial virtue, some become effective in certain results of the arts (to use his words), just as a soldier is effective in conquering, or a farmer

### *Dignities of the planets in the signs to be observed for the use of medicines. Chapter IX.*

The house of **Saturn** is **Aquarius** and **Capricorn**, and its exaltation <note>original: "exaltatio," a position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is particularly strong</note> is **Libra**. The house of **Jupiter** is **Sagittarius** and **Pisces**, and its exaltation or kingdom is **Cancer**. The domicile of **Mars** is **Scorpio** and **Aries**, and its exaltation is **Capricorn**. The seat of the **Sun** is **Leo**, and its kingdom is **Aries**. The dwelling of **Venus** is **Taurus** and **Libra**, and its exaltation is **Pisces**. The house of **Mercury** is **Virgo** and **Gemini**, and its kingdom is **Virgo**. The house of the **Moon** is **Cancer**, and its exaltation is **Taurus**. **Saturn** and **Jupiter** have their triplicity <note>original: "triplicitatem," a grouping of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> in the fire and air signs. The **Sun** is in the fire signs only, **Mercury** in the air signs only, while **Mars**, **Venus**, and the **Moon** are in the water and earth signs.

Any planet, except for the Sun and the Moon, possesses certain bounds <note>original: "fines," also known as "terms," which are specific segments of degrees within a sign where a planet has subsidiary influence</note> of its own in every sign. Therefore, in **Aries**, **Jupiter** holds the first six bounds, **Venus** the next six, **Mercury** the following eight, **Mars** the next five, and **Saturn** the final five. In **Taurus**, in a similar subsequent order, **Venus** has eight bounds, **Mercury** six, **Jupiter** eight, **Saturn** five, and finally **Mars** three. In **Gemini**, **Mercury** has six, **Jupiter** six, **Venus** five, **Mars** seven, and **Saturn** six. In **Cancer**, **Mars** has seven, **Venus** six, **Mercury** six, **Jupiter** seven, and **Saturn** four. In **Leo**, **Jupiter** has six, **Venus** five, **Saturn** seven, **Mercury** six, and **Mars** six. In **Virgo**, **Mercury** has seven, **Venus** ten, **Jupiter** four, **Mars** seven, and **Saturn** two. In **Libra**, **Saturn** has six, **Mercury** eight, **Jupiter** seven, **Venus** seven, and **Mars** two. In **Scorpio**, **Mars** has seven, **Venus** four, **Mercury** eight, **Jupiter** five, and **Saturn** six. In **Sagittarius**, **Jupiter** has twelve, **Venus** five, **Mercury** four, **Saturn** five, and **Mars** four. In **Capricorn**, **Mercury** has seven, **Jupiter** seven, **Venus** eight, **Saturn** four, and **Mars** four. In **Aquarius**, **Mercury** has seven, **Venus** six, **Jupiter** seven, **Mars** five, and **Saturn** five. In **Pisces**, **Venus** has twelve, **Jupiter** four, **Mercury** three, **Mars** nine, and finally **Saturn** two. The **Sun** and the **Moon**, however, have their bounds by a different rule: for the Sun indeed has six signs for its bounds...
