...**Leo**, **Virgo**, **Libra**, **Scorpio**, **Sagittarius**, and **Capricorn**. The **Moon**, however, claims the remaining signs: **Aquarius**, **Pisces**, **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Gemini**, and **Cancer**. The **Sun**, therefore, and the **Moon** hold in these signs that same leadership and effect which the other planets are thought to possess in their own boundaries <note>original: "finib[us]," also known as "terms," which are specific degrees within a sign governed by a planet</note>. In addition to these boundaries, the planets have their **faces** in the signs, which the Greeks call **decans** <note>original: "decanos," 10-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note>, each occupying ten degrees of a sign. In **Aries**, the first face belongs to **Mars**; the second to the **Sun**, who follows **Mars** in the heavens according to the order of the **Chaldeans** <note>The "Chaldean Order" is the traditional sequence of planets by speed: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon</note>; and the third to **Venus**, who succeeds the **Sun** in the sky. In **Taurus**, the first face is **Mercury's**, following **Venus**; the second is the **Moon's**, which succeeds **Mercury**; the third is **Saturn's**. For we must return to him once the number of planets has been completed. In **Gemini**, the first face belongs to **Jupiter**, following **Saturn** of course; the second to **Mars**; the third to the **Sun** in the same order, and so on similarly thereafter.

### How we must use the planets in medicines. Chapter X.

We have mentioned what dignities the planets have in the signs so that whenever we are about to perform a task or compose something pertaining to a specific planet, we know how to place that planet within its own dignities. This is especially important when a planet holds leadership in our own yearly revolution or at our birth <note>original: "genesi," referring to the natal horoscope</note>. Even **Saturn** and **Mars**—who otherwise ought to be restrained by us—must nevertheless be strengthened if they happen to be the "significators" <term>significator: a planet that represents the person or a specific area of their life in a chart</term> of our birth. We shall, however, gain the greatest benefit from this reminder if, when we intend to use the favor of the **Moon**, **Venus**, and **Jupiter** in preparing medicines, we take care that they are not located in the boundaries of **Saturn** or **Mars**. An exception is made if we are perhaps forced either to check a bodily dissolution and repress heat through **Saturn**, or to warm the coldest things and rouse the sluggish through **Mars**; otherwise, we shall choose the boundaries of **Jupiter** and **Venus**. We shall also accept the boundaries of **Mercury**, primarily to benefit "mercurial" men; nor should it escape our notice that highly mercurial men—such as those who excel in talent, craftsmanship, and eloquence—are also significantly "solar." For **Mercury** is always full of **Apollo** <note>Ficino identifies Apollo with the Sun, suggesting that the intellect (Mercury) is powered by the light of the spirit (Sun)</note>.

Now, so that anyone may understand how we describe the figures in the heavens at any given hour: the sign that rises from the east we call the **first house** and the **house of life**. That which follows into the ascent is the **second**, and then the **third**, and so on for the others, such that the **seventh house** is the sign which is now setting in the west, directly opposite the rising sign. The **eighth** succeeds this, while the **ninth** falls away from the middle of the sky <note>original: "medio... cœlo," the Midheaven or 10th house</note>, which forms the **tenth house**. The **eleventh** succeeds this, but the **twelfth** falls away from the rising sign. Therefore, for the planets to be powerful, they must be held in the **angles**: either the East (Ascendant), the West (Descendant), or the Midheaven on either side <note>The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the most active parts of a chart</note>. They are most powerful in the angle of the **ascendant**, or the **tenth house** occupying the middle of the sky above one's head, or at least in the regions that immediately follow the angles. However, they believe the **Sun** rejoices in the **ninth house** (which falls from the Midheaven) and the **Moon** rejoices in the **third** (which is also falling). Keep two rules among these in mind—

<header>BOOK III.</header>

...what the astrologers intend: one consideration regarding the patient, and the other regarding the physician. Namely, where the seventh house <note>In a medical astrological chart, the seventh house represents the physician</note> of the patient is afflicted by **Saturn** or **Mars**, or if its ruler is unfortunate, separate the physician from the patient, if you believe **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the foundational second-century authority on astronomy and astrology</note>. Furthermore, when choosing a physician, he orders one to avoid those of a **Saturnine** or **Martial** nature <note>Saturn and Mars were considered "malefics" or naturally harmful planets</note>, and to seek one in whose birth chart the sixth house <note>The sixth house traditionally governs illness and health</note> has been made fortunate by the aspect of the **Sun**, or by **Venus**, or **Jupiter**.

We call a sign or a planet "unfortunate" [afflicted] by **Saturn** or **Mars** unless they are in their own domiciles or kingdoms; that is, when they are either present there or looking toward that place in **opposition** or **square** aspect. We call an "opposition" the aspect between those things which are separated by the longest possible distance; and a "square" is where one is distant from the other by a fourth part of the sky, that is, a space of three signs. However, **Saturn** and **Mars** do less harm to other planets through conjunction, opposition, or square when they receive them as "guests" in their own domicile, kingdom, or term <note>original: "terminove," referring to specific degrees within a zodiac sign governed by a specific planet</note>. 

Just as the fortunate planets are more beneficial when, besides the **sextile** or **trine** aspect and conjunction, they also (as we said) receive others in this way; planets fear conjunction with the **Sun** <note>This refers to "combustion," where a planet's power is overwhelmed by being too close to the Sun</note>, but they rejoice in its aspect, namely the **Trine** or **Sextile**. 

Therefore, it is necessary to remember that **Aries** presides over the head and face, **Taurus** the neck, **Gemini** the arms and shoulders, **Cancer** the chest, lungs, stomach, and upper arms; **Leo** the heart and stomach, as well as the liver, back, and rear ribs; **Virgo** the intestines and the base of the stomach; **Libra** the kidneys, thigh, and buttocks; **Scorpio** the genitals, vulva, and womb; **Sagittarius** the thigh and groin; **Capricorn** the knees; **Aquarius** the shins and legs; and **Pisces** the feet <note>This is the concept of the "Zodiacal Man," mapping the signs of the zodiac onto the human anatomy from head to toe</note>. 

Mindful of this order, you will beware of touching a limb with **iron** [surgery], or **fire** [cautery], or **cupping glasses** <note>original: "cucurbitulis," glass vessels used to draw blood or humors to the surface</note> when the **Moon** is passing through its corresponding sign; for then the **Moon** increases the **humors** <note>The four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—believed to control health and temperament</note> in that limb, preventing their flow and consolidation, and weighing down the limb's vital power. At that time, however, you will treat the limb with certain friendly remedies, applied either externally or internally, opportunely and successfully. 

It is indeed beneficial to know which sign was rising <note>The Ascendant or rising sign</note> at the time of your birth; for besides **Aries**, this rising sign also signifies the head for you, and in this sign, the **Moon** regards your head. Furthermore, when the **Moon** enters **Aries**, you may opportunely try baths and washings; when it is in **Cancer**, you may successfully let blood <note>original: "minue sanguinem," the practice of phlebotomy</note> or take medicine, especially in the form of an **electuary** <note>A medicinal paste made by mixing powders with honey or syrup</note>. When it is in **Leo**, do not induce vomiting; while in **Libra**, it is fit for **enemas** <note>original: "clysteribus"</note>; in **Scorpio**, do not try baths. There are those who neither forbid nor command giving laxative medicine [in Scorpio]; in **Capricorn**, taking medicine is harmful, and similarly in **Aquarius**, but in **Pisces**, it is beneficial. Which limbs each of the planets occupies in any given sign, though necessary to know, would be tedious to relate; however, in the purging of the bowels, it must not escape our notice...

<header>ON THE LIFE OF THE HEAVENS. COMPENDIUM.</header>

...[We] hold the precept of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text of astrology</note> to take purgative medicine when the **Moon** is in **Cancer**, **Pisces**, or **Scorpio**. We approve of this, especially if the lord of the sign then ascending <note>The "Ascendant," or the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time</note> applies itself to a planet running beneath the earth. But if the lord of the Ascendant is joined meanwhile overhead with a planet holding the midheaven <note>The highest point in the sky at a given time</note>, nausea and vomiting will be immediately incited. Finally, let us conclude with **Galen** <note>The most influential physician of antiquity</note> that astrology is necessary for the physician; for, when disputing on "critical days" <note>Days during an illness when a change or "crisis" is expected, which Galen linked to lunar cycles</note>, he says the opinion of the **Egyptians** is certain: that is, that the Moon signifies the condition of the sick and the healthy from day to day, so much so that if the rays of **Jupiter** and **Venus** are mixed with the Moon, both the sick and the healthy are well affected; but if the rays of **Saturn** or **Mars** are mixed, the opposite occurs. But having wandered widely enough, let us finally return to spirit, life, and the **Graces**.

### *In what ways our spirit can draw the most from the spirit and life of the world; which planets procreate and recreate the spirit; and what things belong to each of the planets. Chapter XI.*

All these things tend toward this goal: that our spirit, rightly prepared and purified through natural means, may receive as much as possible from the worldly life itself through the rays of the stars received at the opportune time. Indeed, the life of the world, implanted in all things, is evidently propagated into herbs and trees, which are like the hair and tresses of its body. Furthermore, it sprouts in stones and metals, like teeth and bones; it also buds in the living shells of the earth that cling to stones. For these live not so much by their own life as by the common life of the whole. This common life flourishes much more upon the earth in subtler bodies that are closer to the soul, through whose inward vigor water, air, and fire possess their own living qualities and are moved. This life fosters air and fire even more than earth and water, agitating them with perpetual motion. And finally, it enlivens the celestial bodies most of all, as if they were the world's head, heart, or eyes; from these, it diffuses rays everywhere through the stars—rays that are not only visible, but also "visual" <note>Ficino follows the ancient theory of "extramission," where eyes emit active rays that "touch" what they see</note>. By these rays, in the manner of an ostrich <note>It was a common medieval and Renaissance belief that the ostrich hatched its eggs simply by staring at them intensely</note>, as we have said elsewhere, the world looks upon lower things and fosters them by looking; indeed, by "touching" them in this way, it generates, shapes, and moves them in every possible way. Therefore, you will receive the life of the world through the motion of shining water, clear air, and fire at a moderate distance, as well as the motion of the heavens. This is possible if you yourself also move gently and in a similar manner, performing certain circular turns according to your strength (avoiding dizziness), observing the celestial things and turning them over in your mind with your eyes. Likewise, through the frequent use of plants and similarly living things, you can draw very much from the spirit of the world—especially if you are nourished and fostered by them while they are still living, fresh, and as if still clinging to Mother Earth. Stay as frequently as possible among plants that smell sweet, or at least not badly; for all herbs, flowers,

trees and fruits are fragrant, although you may often not notice it. By this scent, as if by a breath <note>original: "flatu"</note>, they refresh and enliven you from every side with the spirit of the worldly life. This scent is naturally very similar to your own spirit; because the spirit is a medium <term>medium: a middle-ground substance connecting the immaterial soul to the heavy physical body</term> between the body and the soul, these scents easily refresh the body and wonderfully benefit the soul. Among these things, you should spend as much time as possible during the day under the open sky, as long as it can be done safely and comfortably in high, clear, and temperate regions. For in such places, the rays of the Sun and the stars reach you more directly and purely from all directions, filling your spirit with the spirit of the world, which shines out more abundantly through those rays.

Furthermore, the natural motion of the air itself—which is a perpetual circular motion—can hardly be perceived by anyone because of its gentleness and our long habituation to it. Yet, when you are walking under the open sky during the day, or living in open and elevated places, this air freely brushes against you <note>original: "lambit," literally "licks"</note>, penetrates you purely, and wonderfully provides a worldly motion and vigor to your spirit. I specifically said "during the day," for we have found that the night air is hostile to our spirits. The use of the daylight will be beneficial, especially if you walk a great deal in the open, first avoiding excessive weather conditions, and then moving frequently within it at times when, besides the air being temperate and clear, the position of the stars is more healthy for human beings. Likewise, you should choose places that are more fragrant than others, changing your location daily through a sought-out route, while you yourself move continuously and gently.

Change your location: although I have always taught this with careful selection, for the gifts of the heavens and of all nature are distributed among us in various things and different places, all of which should ultimately be enjoyed. I should also mention that variety prevents boredom <note>original: "tædium"</note>, which is hostile to the spirit and characteristic of **Saturn** <note>the planet associated with melancholy and stagnation</note>. Variety, however, brings pleasure, through which (if I may put it this way) **Venus** herself, the friend of pleasure, enters into the spirit; as soon as she has entered, she performs her duty and propagates health.

In short, if one considers the account of Paradise and the use of the fruit of life in the writings of **Moses**; likewise the similar lifestyle proposed by **Plato** in the *Phaedo*; and what **Pliny** says about peoples who live on scent alone, he will understand that what we are saying is true. But let us descend to the nature of the spirit itself: the quality of the spirit is undoubtedly **Jovian** <note>related to Jupiter, the planet of growth and health</note>, for it is infused into us during Jupiter's hour; it is also **Solar**. For **Jupiter** infuses this spirit insofar as he tempers the immense power of the **Sun** within himself. It is also Jovian for another reason: because it is hot and moist, though it abounds in heat rather than moisture; it is born from the blood and is called a certain "sanguineous vapor." Again, because it glows, is exceedingly subtle and bright, and arises from the heart, it is undoubtedly judged to be **Solar**. It also possesses a certain **Venereal** <note>related to Venus</note> power within itself: for it flows out, moves, and is transferred through the motions of Venus to propagate offspring; it expands itself toward the pleasure of every sense and flees from pain. In summary, insofar as the spirit leads the body toward life, motion, and propagation, it is considered <note>original: "existimatur"</note> **Jovian**, **Venereal**, and **Solar**.

->### ON DRAWING DOWN LIFE FROM THE HEAVENS (ABRIDGED)<-

is valued. Insofar as it serves the soul's senses and imagination, it is considered solar and mercurial, and it is mercurial everywhere. Indeed, because it is so mobile, easily changed, and shaped, a healthy spirit does not usually have much of the qualities of Saturn, Mars, or the Moon. Otherwise, it would often be stupid from Saturn, furious from Mars, or in a way dull from the Moon. For this reason, lunar things—being thicker and simultaneously damper—are quite foreign to the subtle and volatile nature of the spirit. Those things which are Saturnine are far too material and are almost like poisons, naturally hostile to the spirit: some on account of extreme cold and dryness, others because of dryness and a consuming heat. Therefore, the nature of the spirit is considered to be primarily Jovial <note>associated with Jupiter</note> and Solar, then Mercurial, and in some way Venereal <note>associated with Venus</note>. By a specific distinction, the **natural spirit** is properly dedicated to Jupiter, the **vital spirit** to the Sun, and the **animal spirit** to Mercury. <term>animal spirit: from the Latin 'anima' (soul); the refined substance in the brain responsible for thought and movement</term> 

When, therefore, the situation requires you to assist one of these three spirits, you will not easily be able to help the "little client" <note>original: "clientulo," a metaphor for the human spirit seeking protection</note> if its patron is unfortunate or weak. It is most difficult to help the animal spirit when Mercury is unfavorably positioned, for he has such authority over the animal spirit that he is said to be able to both lull souls to sleep and wake them with his caduceus <note>the staff of Mercury, often depicted with two snakes</note>. That is to say, by his astrological aspect being one way or another, he can wonderfully dull or sharpen the intellect, weaken or strengthen it, and trouble or calm it. 

Whenever you study how to cultivate a particular spirit, you must not only observe that its patron planet is fortunate and powerful, but you should also choose a time when the Moon is favorably directed toward it. At times, the substance of the spirit is not properly created by the influence of Saturn alone, but it is always called back from the external to the internal, and often from the lowest to the highest; hence, Saturn is conducive to contemplating more secret and elevated things. However, although rarely, the power of Mars and Saturn can benefit the spirit as a medicine, either by warming it when necessary, or by exciting and expanding it, or conversely by restraining a spirit that is too volatile. 

The nature of the spirit is created and refreshed primarily through those things which are in harmony with those four planets <note>Jupiter, Sol, Mercury, and Venus</note>. But if you turn toward Solar things excessively and without discretion, you will sharpen the spirit and eventually dry it out and dissolve it. Similarly, if you turn to Venereal things, you will gradually liquefy or dull it; if you rely only on Mercurial things, you will gain very little from them. It will, therefore, be worthwhile to use Jovial things as much as possible, and to mix the others with them in moderate amounts, and to more frequently use things that are either common to all of these or belong properly to Jupiter—for these are also, in a way, common to everyone. Generally, however, this pertains to all things that have a substance that is neither too fiery, nor entirely earthy, nor simply watery, nor of a very sharp or very dull quality, but of a moderate and...

# BOOK III.

...soft to the touch, and in a certain way gentle, or at least not hard or rough; likewise, sweet in taste, pleasant in smell, pleasing to the sight, soothing and delightful to the hearing, and joyful in thought. Therefore, a certain sweetness of flavor and grace is common to all these things. If the sweetness is watery and simultaneously fatty, it pertains more to Venus; if it is somewhat tasteless or slightly austere, it pertains rather to Mercury. These are not very beneficial to the spirit, yet they are sometimes necessary to dull its excessive sharpness. 

If the sweetness is manifest and subtle, and has a little of an astringent and sharp flavor, it is properly judged as Jovial <note>associated with the planet Jupiter</note>. To this belongs the substance of sweet almond, pine nut, hazelnut, pistachio, starch, licorice, raisins, egg yolk, the meat of chicken, pheasants, peacocks, partridges, and similar things. Likewise, the roots of ben <note>likely *Centaurea behen* or *Moringa*, used in traditional medicine</note> and elecampane <note>original: "enulae," a herb used for digestion and respiratory health</note>, as well as clear fragrant wine that is somewhat sweet and astringent, the whitest sugar, and the whitest wheat. Manna <note>a sweet resin used as a mild laxative and tonic</note> also pertains to Jupiter, provided it is strengthened with the infused power of the myrobalan <note>original: "myrobalani," a dried fruit used in ancient pharmacology</note>; otherwise, it pertains no less to Venus than to Jupiter. 

This is certainly the substance and sweetness of Jupiter, and it contributes above all to the creation and restoration of the spirit. Indeed, most things are Jovial which we discussed in the book *On Long Life* as being able to preserve youth and be healthy for the elderly. 

But if the sweetness is very slight and it has much of a sharp and astringent quality, or even some bitterness, it is considered to be Solar <note>associated with the Sun</note>. A similar reasoning and distinction applies to smells, for these are the siblings of flavors. The same is true of colors. Colors that are watery, white, green, and somewhat saffron-colored—similar to the colors of violets, roses, and lilies—as well as smells of this kind, relate to Venus, the Moon, and Mercury. 

The colors of sapphire (which are also called airy), fuller purples, gold mixed with silver, and evergreen relate to Jupiter. However, glowing saffron, pure gold, and brighter purples relate to the Sun. Indeed, any colors, if they are vivid or at least silky, are more "stellar" <note>possessing the refined, potent quality of the stars</note>; they are also powerful in metals, stones, and glass because of their heavenly resemblance. 

But to return to Jupiter: its flavor and smell are like what is found in the golden peach, and similar pears, or oranges, and in lighter Malmsey wine <note>original: "maluatico," a sweet, high-quality wine</note> and light Vernaccia <note>original: "vernaceo," a popular white wine of the Renaissance</note>. They are like the taste of green ginger, or cinnamon, or sweet fennel <note>original: "maratro"</note>, or leopard’s bane <note>original: "doronico"</note>, if these are tasted preserved in plenty of sugar. For these four, and fresh nutmeg, if they are alone, are rather Solar. Cloves <note>original: "gariophilus"</note> and musk are also Solar, but in smell, not in taste or appearance; ambergris <note>original: "ambra," a rare aromatic substance</note> is mostly Solar and Jovial. Saffron <note>original: "crocus"</note> is Solar in everything, although its color and smell are dedicated to all the Graces among astrologers; however, the taste properly belongs to the Sun. Finally, all fragrant and aromatic things, insofar as they bear a pleasing scent, relate to Jupiter and Venus, etc.

pertain to Mercury, as they do to the Sun. However, among these, the sharper qualities belong more to the Sun, while the blunter ones belong rather to Venus and Mercury; those properly tempered belong to Jupiter, whether experienced through smell, taste, hearing, sight, or touch. Furthermore, graceful and pleasant sounds and songs belong to all the Graces <note>the *Charites*, representing the beneficial and harmonizing influences of the planets</note> and to Mercury, while very threatening or mournful sounds manifest the influence of Mars and Saturn. You should not wonder that we attribute so much to colors, odors, and voices: for flavors belong primarily to the <term>natural spirit</term> <note>the subtle vapor responsible for digestion and growth</note>, while odors belong rather to the <term>vital spirit</term> <note>the vapor in the heart and pulse</note> and <term>animal spirit</term> <note>the most refined vapor in the brain, responsible for thought and movement</note>; colors, shapes, and voices belong specifically to the animal spirit. Movements of the soul, whether joyful, sad, or steady, also stir the spirit powerfully into their own likeness. It first affects the animal spirit, then through this the vital spirit, and finally through that the natural spirit; because the entire spirit, due to its somewhat fiery, entirely airy, clear, and mobile nature, is similar to light, and therefore to colors, airy voices, odors, and the movements of the soul. For this reason, it is suddenly moved and shaped in either direction by these things. And whatever state the spirit itself becomes, it in turn creates a corresponding emotion in the soul and a general quality in the body. Finally, when the spirit is appropriately exposed to the Graces through those things that belong to them—since it was already naturally inclined toward them—it immediately receives the wonderful gifts of the Graces through their rays, which are both active everywhere and akin to the spirit itself.

### *Natural things, and even artificial ones, have hidden virtues from the stars, through which*
### *they expose our spirit to those same stars. Chapter XII.*

When we say that the spirit is exposed to the Graces through things that belong to the Graces, we believe it is adapted not only through qualities that are seen, heard, smelled, or tasted, but also through those that are touched. Remember, therefore, that **Heat** in the first degree belongs to Jupiter; in the second, to the Sun with Jupiter; in the third, to Mars with the Sun; and in the fourth, to Mars. **Cold** in the first degree belongs to Venus; in the second, to the Moon; in the third, to the Moon with Saturn; and in the fourth, to Saturn. **Moisture** in the first degree belongs to Mercury with Jupiter; in the second, to Venus with the Moon; in the third, to the Moon with Venus; and in the fourth, to the Moon. When joined with Venus and Mercury, **Dryness** in the first degree belongs to Jupiter; in the second, to Mercury with the Sun; in the third, to the Sun with Mars; and in the fourth, to Mars with Saturn. Summarizing from the planetary qualities which Ptolemy describes in his *Quadripartitum* <note>original: "quadripartito," the Latin title for the *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text of ancient astrology</note>, we gather that the harmony forged from all these tends toward heat and moisture: for the immense heat of Mars and the Sun, and the tempered heat of Jupiter, overcomes the immense coldness of Saturn and the slight cold of Venus and the Moon, so that the heat there exceeds the cold. Likewise, the abundant moisture of the Moon and Venus, which is close to us, and the tempered moisture of Jupiter, overcomes the great dryness of Saturn and Mars and the tempered dryness of the Sun; therefore heat and moisture dominate cold and dryness...

# BOOK III.

[...is moved], and similarly heat to moisture. Just as in a healthy human body, tempered to a celestial harmony, a certain temperament coalesces from the heat and dryness of the heart, the heat and moisture of the liver, and the cold and moisture of the brain. This temperament leans moderately toward heat and moisture because heat reigns supreme: for the heat of the heart and liver overcomes the cold of the brain, just as the moisture of the liver and brain exceeds the dryness of the heart. 

I would not want us to overlook the fact that a harmony exists among the fixed stars, common to all things, just as we have described regarding the planets; for astrologers believe the stars possess qualities similar to the planets. Why mention this? So that you may remember that our spirit and body—whether through a natural state or one sought through art—can be accommodated to the heavens through a certain temperament leaning toward heat and moisture, and can thus claim celestial gifts for themselves. 

We do not say, however, that our spirit is prepared for celestial influences only through the qualities of things known to the senses <note>such as heat, cold, or color</note>, but also—and much more so—through certain properties implanted in things from heaven. These are hidden from our senses and are ultimately barely known even to reason. For since such properties and their effects cannot be explained by elemental power alone, it follows that they proceed uniquely from the life and <term>spirit of the world</term> <note>the *spiritus mundi*, a subtle substance that connects the physical world to the World Soul</note> through the rays of the stars themselves. Therefore, the spirit is affected by these properties as much as possible and as quickly as possible, and is powerfully exposed to celestial influences.

By this very reasoning, the emerald, hyacinth <note>likely zircon or sapphire in this context</note>, sapphire, topaz, ruby, unicorn horn, and especially the stone called **bezoar** <note>original: *bezaar*; a mass found in the digestive systems of certain animals, highly prized in the Renaissance as a universal antidote</note> among the Arabs, are endowed with hidden properties of grace. Therefore, these are not only taken internally, but if they touch the flesh and are warmed there to bring out their virtue, they instill a celestial power into the spirits, by which they defend themselves against the plague and poisons. 

The fact that these and similar things perform such acts through celestial virtue is proven by this: even when taken in a tiny weight, they have a significant effect. This is a power hardly ever granted to a simple elemental quality—except perhaps to a very "celestial" fire. Material power requires a large amount of matter to act significantly; however, "formal" power <note>power derived from a thing's "form" or heavenly archetype rather than its physical bulk</note> is worth the most even with the minimum amount of matter. 

By a similar virtue, the solar **peony** <note>original: *phœbæa peonia*; the "herb of Apollo," used to treat brain disorders</note>, when touching the flesh, arms the spirit against the **falling sickness** <term>falling sickness</term> <note>epilepsy</note> by a vapor infused within them. Similarly, **coral** and **chalcedony** act against the illusions of "black bile" <note>melancholy</note>, especially through the power of Jupiter and Venus. Other things act similarly: by a property of this kind, **myrobalans** <note>original: *myrobalani*; astringent plum-like fruits used in medieval medicine</note> preserve youth, sharpen the senses, and benefit the intellect and memory. This is primarily due to Jupiter (who tempers the influence of Saturn) and Mercury (who is a friend to the senses). Someone might even believe that this tree existed in Paradise for the purpose of prolonging life. They also consecrate the **agate** stone to Mercury,

# ON THE CELESTIAL LIFE. COMPILED.

Wherefore natural philosophers <note>original: *physici*</note> agree that it is powerful for eloquence, vision, and against poisons. Serapio <note>likely Serapion the Younger, a 12th-century Arabic medicinal author</note> writes that he who carries a hyacinth <note>original: *hiacyntum*; in this period, likely referring to a blue sapphire or a zircon</note>, or a seal made from it, is safe from lightning, and that this virtue of it is very widely known; we believe it possesses this power from Jove <note>Jupiter</note>. The eagle-stone <note>original: *lapis aetites*; a hollow geode believed to be found in eagles' nests</note> has from Lucina <note>the goddess of childbirth</note>—that is, from Venus and the Moon—the property that, when applied to the womb, it brings forth birth quickly and very easily, which Rhazes <note>original: *Rasis*; the Persian physician al-Razi</note>, with Serapion confirming, says he has frequently experienced. Perhaps also from Phoebus <note>Apollo/the Sun</note>, who pierced the Python, we say Cretean dittany <note>original: *cretea dictamus*</note> has the power both to resist venomous things and to draw iron from a wound. By the power of the Sun, ginger infused in feasts wards off fainting; Gentian calms the madness of a dog <note>rabies</note> and puts serpents to flight. Vervain <note>original: *berbena*</note> is said to grant prophecy, joy, expiations, and vision; rue and zedoary <note>a root similar to ginger</note> act as a <term>theriac</term> <note>a universal antidote or "miracle" medicine</note> against poisons. Frankincense <note>original: *thus*</note> supports the vital and animal spirit against dullness, forgetfulness, and fear. 

Truly, sage and mint possess the power of Jupiter; the former indeed chases away paralysis, while the latter strengthens the mind by its scent alone. By the same power, cinquefoil <note>original: *pentaphilon*; literally "five-leaf"</note> resists poisons, and one of its leaves drunk twice daily in wine cures a one-day fever, three leaves cure a tertian fever, and four cure a quartan fever. Ancient priests used this herb in purifications on account of its purity. The chaste tree <note>original: *agnus castus*</note>, by the power of Saturn, halts sexual desire, while jasper stops blood. 

Wondrous effects are usually produced where an elemental property secretly serves a hidden property. For example, in the myrobalan <note>a plum-like medicinal fruit</note>, it is not only that celestial power that acts to strengthen the spirit and body, but also a greatly styptic <note>astringent</note> and significantly aromatic quality, which wonderfully prevents putrefaction and dissolution, and corroborates the spirit. Now truly, that saffron <note>original: *crocus*</note> seeks the heart, expands the spirit, and provokes laughter is due not only to the hidden power of the Sun, but the very nature of saffron—subtle, expansive, aromatic, and bright—conduces to the same end. What I say of simple medicines, I wish to be understood similarly of compounds. 

Tell me, then, how does <term>theriac</term> help us against poison? It does not draw out the poison—for it binds the bowels—nor does it entirely change the nature of the poison so suddenly. For the poison's nature is not so weak and changeable. Rather, the theriac suddenly strengthens the vital spirit—which is very thin and changeable—through a certain conforming proportion to it. It does this so effectively that the spirit, now empowered as an agent, together with the theriac acting as its instrument, partly overcomes the poison, partly changes it, and partly wards it off from the heart <note>original: *præcordijs*</note>. But by what proportion or power does theriac achieve this? By one that is both Jovial <note>of Jupiter</note> and Phoebean <note>of the Sun</note> at once, which it seems to have claimed for itself from the mixing of many things blended together according to a certain proportion. There is, I say, a threefold power in it: this very celestial one I just mentioned, and another celestial property previously in the herbs and aromatics from which it is properly composed, which serves the power previously mentioned...

### BOOK III.

To the same effect. There is moreover another virtue in many of its parts that is elemental rather than celestial, yet it is such that it contributes to the protection of the spirit. I speak of the astringent <note>original: *stipticam*; a quality that contracts tissues and stops bleeding</note> and aromatic quality; the former firms the spirit, while the latter nourishes it. Theriac <term>theriac</term> <note>original: *theriaca*; a famous ancient "miracle" medicine made from dozens of ingredients, including viper flesh, used as a universal antidote and anti-aging tonic</note> has thus obtained a wonderful power against hastening old age and poison, namely due to three virtues in it conspiring together toward the same end. One of these is indeed celestial, acquired through skillful mixing; another is celestial as well, but naturally inherent in its parts; and the third is entirely elemental. But that first one I mentioned—the virtue acquired from heaven—would be even more admirable if it were not only composed of Jovian <note>relating to the planet Jupiter</note> and Solar proportions and such things, but also if an opportune time were chosen for this through the observation of the celestial bodies. For just as the body relates to place and time, so motion and action relate to time. Just as certain bodies and their forms coalesce and are preserved in specific places and times, so too do certain actions gain efficacy from specific proper times. Socrates signifies this in the *Alcibiades* <note>a dialogue by Plato</note>, and Proclus <note>a Neoplatonist philosopher</note> explains it. Pythagoras, observing this clearly, nicknamed the "good" and the "perfection of things" as "Opportunity" <note>original: *opportunitatem*; likely referring to the Greek concept of *Kairos*</note>. For the primary principle, according to Pythagoras and Plato, is the measure of all things in such a way that it distributes different places and times to different bodies and actions. 

Whence, just as certain things are not born successfully or preserved except in this place and at that time, so too a material action, movement, or such-and-such an event does not obtain efficacy and a perfect effect except when the harmony of the heavens resonates with it from every side. This harmony is indeed thought to have such great power that it bestows a frequently miraculous virtue not only upon the labors of farmers and the art of physicians (compounded through herbs and spices), but even upon the "images" <note>astrological talismans or amulets</note> which are made by astrologers from metals and stones; however, these "images" now require their own specific chapter. 

As for what pertains to choosing hours for actions and works, it is strongly confirmed by Ptolemy <note>the famous 2nd-century astronomer and geographer</note> where he says in the *Centiloquium* <note>a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms attributed to Ptolemy</note>: "he who chooses what is better seems to differ in no way from one who has this by nature." In these words, he seems to confirm the power both of the heavens and of our own judgment and choice. Albertus Magnus <note>a 13th-century Dominican friar and polymath</note> also says in his *Mirror* <note>original: *speculum*; referring to the *Speculum Astronomiae*</note>: "For the freedom of choice is not constrained by choosing a praiseworthy hour; rather, to despise the choice of an hour in the beginnings of great undertakings is a rashness of will, not freedom."

->ON THE LIFE OF HEAVEN. COMPENDIUM.<-

### *On the power of images according to the ancients, and of medicines acquired from heaven. Chapter XIII.*

Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer and geographer</note> says in his *Centiloquium* <note>original: *centiloquio*; a famous collection of 100 astrological aphorisms</note> that the forms of lower things are subject to the "faces" of the heavens. He claims that ancient sages were accustomed to fashioning certain images at the precise time when planets were entering similar faces in the sky, which served as the celestial models for things on earth. Haly <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> confirms this in his commentary, saying that an effective image of a serpent can be made when the Moon enters the celestial serpent <note>likely the constellation Serpens or the Moon's Nodes</note> or looks upon it favorably. Similarly, he says an image of a Scorpion is effective when the Moon enters the sign of Scorpio and this sign holds one of the four "angles" <note>the most powerful points in an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, or Imum Coeli</note>. 

He says this was done in Egypt in his own time, and that he was present when a figure of a Bull was impressed from a scorpion-seal made on a bezoar stone <term>bezoar stone</term> <note>original: *lapide bezaar*; a stony mass found in the stomachs of animals, highly prized as a universal antidote to poison</note>. This was given in a drink to a man who had been stung by a scorpion, and he was suddenly cured. The physician Hahameh affirms that such things are done usefully, a point confirmed by Serapio <note>likely the 9th-century physician Yahya ibn Sarafyun</note>. Furthermore, Haly relates that a wise man known to him used similar industry to make images that could move, much like the one we read was made—I know not how—by Archytas <note>an ancient Greek philosopher credited with building a mechanical flying pigeon</note>. 

Hermes Trismegistus <note>the legendary "Thrice-Great" Egyptian sage and father of Hermeticism</note> also says that the Egyptians used to make such images from certain materials of the world, and at the opportune time, they were accustomed to insert the souls of demons into them. He claims the souls of his grandfather Mercury, as well as those of a certain Phoebus <note>the Sun</note>, Isis, and Osiris, descended into statues in this way to either benefit or harm humanity. Similar to this is the story of Prometheus, who, with a certain figure of clay, stole life and celestial light. 

Furthermore, the Magi who followed Zoroaster used a certain golden ball marked with celestial characters to call forth a spirit from Hecate <note>the goddess of magic and the underworld</note>; a sapphire was inserted into it, and it was spun with a whip made of bull’s hide while they performed incantations—though I shall gladly omit the songs themselves. For even Psellus the Platonist <note>Michael Psellus, a 11th-century Byzantine scholar</note> disapproves of and mocks them. Even the Hebrews, having been raised in Egypt, learned to build a Golden Calf; their astrologers believe they did this to catch the favor of Venus and the Moon against the influence of Scorpio and Mars, which they believed were hostile to the Jews. 

Porphyry <note>a 3rd-century Neoplatonist</note> also testifies in his *Letter to Anebo* that images are effective, adding that airy demons were accustomed to being drawn in immediately by certain vapors exhaling from specific ritual fumigations. Iamblichus <note>Porphyry's student and a proponent of theurgy</note> confirms that in materials which are naturally in harmony with the higher powers—when they are gathered from all sides and blended at the right time—forces and effects can be received that are not only celestial, but also demonic and divine. Proclus and Synesius <note>later Neoplatonist philosophers</note> say the same. Indeed, the wonderful works for health which can be performed by physicians skilled in astrology through things composed of many ingredients—that is, powders, liquids, ointments, and electuaries <note>medicinal pastes mixed with honey or syrup</note>—seem to have a more probable and better-known logic within them than images do. This is because these powders, liquids, ointments, and electuaries, when made at the opportune...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on how to capture celestial influences. While the previous page introduced the concept of astrological images (talismans), Ficino here argues that medical mixtures are often more effective because they combine many different materials that share the same planetary "order."</meta>

BOOK III.

...portunely composed, they receive celestial influences <note>original: *influxus cœleſtes*</note> more easily and more quickly than the harder materials from which images <note>astrological talismans</note> are usually made. This is because they are either taken internally, having already been affected by the heavens and then converted into our own nature, or they are at least applied externally where they cling more closely and eventually penetrate. Furthermore, images are constructed from only one or a few substances, whereas medicines can be blended from as many as you choose. For instance, if a hundred gifts of the Sun or Jupiter were scattered across a hundred plants, animals, and similar things, you could gather all hundred together once discovered and combine them into a single form, in which you would seem to possess nearly the whole Sun or Jupiter.

You certainly know that a lower nature cannot grasp all the powers of a higher nature in a single thing; therefore, those powers are dispersed among many natures here among us. These powers can be gathered more conveniently through the works of physicians and similar preparations than through images. Consequently, images made of wood perhaps have little power. For wood is perhaps too hard to easily capture celestial influence and less tenacious at retaining it if it has received it; and once it is torn from the bowels of mother earth, it loses almost all the vigor of worldly life <note>original: *mundanæ vitæ*; the animating spirit of the cosmos</note> in a short time and is easily changed into another quality.

Precious stones and metals, however, even if they seem harder to receive a celestial gift, retain it for a longer time—as Iamblichus <note>A 4th-century Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote on theurgy and the power of material objects</note> confirms—if they have received it. Indeed, by their very hardness, they contain the traces and gifts of worldly life for a very long time after being extracted, which they once possessed while attached to the earth. For this reason, at least, they are judged to be suitable materials for capturing and holding celestial things.

It is also probable, as I said in the previous book, that things so beautiful cannot be forged beneath the earth except by some great effort of the heavens, and that the power once impressed upon them by that effort remains within them; for heaven labored for a very long time in "cooking" and compressing them. But since you cannot easily combine many such things, you are forced to search diligently for which metal among others belongs most to the "order" of a certain star, or which stone is highest in that order. Thus, at least in one supreme example of a whole genus and order, you may encompass the remaining powers as much as possible, and borrow from such a vessel the celestial things consistent with it.

For example, in the solar order <note>the hierarchy of things governed by the Sun</note>, beneath the "Solar Man" <note>original: *homine phœbeo*</note>, the hawk <note>original: *auſtur*</note> or the rooster holds the highest place among animals. Among plants, it is balsam or laurel; among metals, gold; among stones, the carbuncle <note>a glowing red gemstone, often garnet or ruby</note> or the pantaura <term>pantaura</term> <note>a legendary "all-bright" stone mentioned in ancient texts as having magnetic and solar powers</note>; and among elements, burning air—for fire itself is considered to be Martian <note>governed by the planet Mars</note>. When we say that the influence of the Sun, Jupiter, or Venus should be increased, we mean this as a general rule; however, it does not apply to someone in whose nativity <note>original: *geneſi*; birth chart</note> one of these appears as a "killer" <note>original: *interfector*; the specific planet in a horoscope that signifies the end of life or health</note>.

### The orders of things hanging from the stars, such as solar things and the like, and how the spirit becomes solar. Chapter XIV.

I have indeed stated elsewhere that from every single star—to speak in the <term>Platonic manner</term><note>Ficino refers to the Neoplatonic concept of "seira" or chains, where a single divine source influences a series of related things across all levels of reality, from gods to minerals.</note>—there hangs a series of things proper to it, descending all the way to the lowest depths. Under the very **Heart of the Scorpion** <note>The star Antares</note>, after the <term>daemons</term> <note>original: *dęmonas*; in this context, these are mediating spirits or intelligences, not necessarily evil beings</note> and men of that kind, and the scorpion animal itself, we can also place the herb **asterion**—that is, the "stellar" herb, similar in shape to a star and shining at night—which physicians claim possesses the quality of a rose and holds a marvelous power against diseases of the genitals. 

Under the celestial **Serpent** or **Serpent-bearer** <note>The constellation Ophiuchus</note>, they place **Saturn**, and in a certain way **Jupiter**, followed by daemons who often take on the forms of serpents. Furthermore, there are similar men, serpent-like living creatures, the **serpentaria** herb, the **draconite** stone <note>original: *draconitem*; a mythical "dragon-stone" supposedly found in the heads of dragons</note> born from the head of a dragon, as well as the stone commonly called **serpentine**, and others which I shall bring forward in what follows. 

Under the **solar star**—that is, **Sirius**—they place the **Sun** first, then also **Phoebeian** <note>original: *phębeos*; relating to Phoebus Apollo, the sun god</note> daemons, whom **Proclus** <note>A 5th-century Neoplatonist philosopher who greatly influenced Ficino’s theories on magic and theurgy</note> testifies have sometimes appeared to men under the form of lions or roosters. Next are men who are very similar to these, solar beasts, then Phoebeian plants, metals likewise, and small stones, as well as steam and glowing air. 

By a similar reasoning, they believe that from any star in the firmament, through some planet, a woven context of things descends step by step under that star's particular property. Therefore, if (as I was saying) you opportunely grasp all solar things through any level of that order—namely such men (or something from such a man), likewise brute animals, plants, metals, stones, and those things pertaining to them—you will drink in the power of the Sun everywhere, and in a way, the natural faculty of solar daemons. 

Assume the same has been said for others. Indeed, solar men are those such as I described before: those born when **Leo** is ascending and the Sun is either occupying or aspecting it, and those born under **Aries** in a similar way. Solar, too, is the blood taken from the left arm of such healthy people. Phoebeian also are the crocodile, the hawk, the **Lion**, the **rooster**, and the **swan**, and the **crow**. Nor does the Lion fear the rooster for any other reason than that in the Phoebeian order, the rooster is a "superior" Lion <note>In the hierarchy of solar things, the rooster was thought to possess a more concentrated or "higher" solar spirit than the lion, despite the lion's physical strength.</note>. For the same reason, Proclus says that an Apollonian daemon which had appeared in the form of a lion immediately vanished when a rooster was presented. 

Most especially among animals, the **heart** is solar. I also judge that the **seal** <note>original: *marinum vitulum*; literally "sea-calf"</note> is subject to the celestial **Heart of the Lion** <note>The star Regulus</note>; for this very reason, its skin—which a bare buckle made of the same animal's bone cinches—immediately relieves pain of the kidneys. For astrologers use the Sun's influence from that star against such pain; by the same logic, perhaps, the <unclear>hępelis</unclear> <note>original: *hępelis*; likely a corrupted reference to the seal-skin or a specific herb known to protect against lightning</note> is said to protect us from lightning. Among plants, the **palm** is Phoebeian, and especially the **laurel**, which by its power repels poisons and lightning. The **ash tree** also, by a similar faculty, keeps poisons at a distance. That the **lotus** <note>original: *loton*</note> is Phoebeian is testified by its round leaves and fruit, and the unfolding of its leaves by day, [repl...] <note>The text cuts off mid-sentence; the catchword indicates the next word relates to the folding or closing of the leaves at night.</note>

signification at night. That the **Phoebean Peony** <note>original: *Peoniam phœbeam*; the peony was traditionally linked to Apollo/Phoebe, the god of healing and the Sun</note> is solar is indicated not only by its medicinal power but also by its name. To this same category belong flowers and herbs that close when the Sun departs and immediately unfold when it returns, turning continually toward the Sun. Furthermore, there is **gold**, and the **aetites** stone <note>original: *lapis elitis*; likely referring to the eagle-stone, believed to be found in eagles' nests and possessed of solar virtues</note> which imitates the Sun with its golden rays. Likewise, there is the stone called the **Sun's eye**, which has the shape of a pupil from which light flashes. Again, there is the **carbuncle** <note>A term used historically for red gemstones like rubies or garnets believed to glow in the dark</note> which glows at night, or the **pantaura** stone <note>A legendary gem mentioned in ancient texts as attracting other stones and containing all powers</note> which contains within itself all the powers of stones, just as gold does for metals and the Sun for stars—many of which have been pointed out by us in the preceding sections.

Therefore, if it is permitted under the rule of the Sun, you will be able to compose an **electuary** <note>A medicinal paste or syrup mixed with honey</note> or an ointment from that blood, and the hearts of those animals, and the leaves and fruits of the aforementioned trees. Likewise, from the flowers and gold-leaved herbs, as well as the powders of these gemstones, you may add saffron, balsam, aromatic reed, frankincense, musk, ambergris, aloe wood, ginger, mastic, spikenard, cinnamon, **leopard's bane** <note>original: *doronico*</note>, citron peel, **zedoary** <note>An aromatic root similar to ginger</note>, nutmeg, mace, and cloves. Mix these with yellow honey or with oils of balsam, mastic, laurel, or nard to soothe the heart, stomach, and head—either internally or externally—so that the **solar spirit** <note>original: *spiritus solaris*; for Ficino, the 'spirit' is a subtle vapor in the body that connects the soul to the physical world and can be 'tuned' to different planets</note> may emerge from them. I say that such a compound should be made from all these things, or at least from many of them, while the Sun is dominant.

You should also begin to use this compound during the Sun's reign, provided that you also wear solar clothing, live in solar places, and see, hear, smell, imagine, think of, and desire solar things. Likewise, you should imitate the dignity of life and the gifts of the Sun, dwell among solar people and plants, and touch laurel frequently. However, for the sake of health, it would be safer to mix **Jovian** <note>related to Jupiter</note> and **Venereal** <note>related to Venus</note> things with the solar ones; specifically, the moisture of Venus serves as a moderator for the solar heat, such as the water and juice of roses and violets. I have composed some of these medicines in my book *On Caring for the Health of the Studious*, and others in the book *On Long Life*; some I have recorded as composed by others, and some I have tempered myself. Likewise, we have spoken in the book *Against the Plague* about which herbs belonging to the Sun and Jupiter have miraculous powers against epidemics and poison, among which is the "perforated" herb called **demon-flee** <note>original: *perforata fugademon*; commonly known as St. John’s Wort (*Hypericum perforatum*), historically used to ward off evil spirits</note>. It is thought to ward off the harmful vapors of evil daemons from us by no other faculty than that of celestial graces—as do any other herbs or stones, such as **coral**, that seem to achieve the same effect. There is even a **lunar herb** passed down by **Mercury** <note>Hermes Trismegistus</note> with round, sky-blue leaves; it produces one leaf daily as the Moon waxes and sheds one as it wanes, promising "lunar years" <note>An ancient calculation of lifespan based on lunar cycles</note> to the user. But let us now return to the subject of images with a new starting point.

### *On the power of images according to the ancients, and of medicines, and how medicines are far more powerful than images. Chapter XV.*

If you obtain the gemstones which I described a moment ago as "Phoebean," there will be no need to engrave images upon them. You shall simply hang them from your neck, set in gold and tied with threads of saffron-yellow silk, when the Sun is passing through **Aries** or **Leo**...

# ->ON THE LIFE OF HEAVEN. ACQUIRED.<-
<meta>catchword: venera- (venerates)</meta>

...runs through, and ascends, or holds the midheaven, and looks upon the Moon. However, **Proclus** <note>Proclus (412–485 AD) was a Neoplatonist philosopher who taught that all things in the universe are connected via "chains" (series) of sympathy reaching down from the stars</note> relates that there are much more powerful small stones in the <term>chain</term> <note>original: *serie*; a Neoplatonic concept of a vertical hierarchy of things sharing the same nature</note> of the Moon. First among these is the **selenite** <note>original: *selinitim*; likely what we call moonstone, named for the Greek moon goddess Selene</note>, which he says not only imitates the Moon in its shape, but also in its motion, circling along with the Moon. If you happen to find this stone, and it is encased in silver and hung from the neck by a silver thread while the Moon is entering Cancer or Taurus <note>Astrological signs where the Moon is considered strongest (its "home" and "exaltation")</note>, and is holding suitable angles, you will then render your own <term>spirit</term> <note>In Renaissance thought, the *spiritus* was a subtle vapor in the body that acted as a bridge between the physical soul and the material body, capable of being "tuned" to different planets</note> lunar. This occurs because the lunar stone, having been warmed by your body, continually inserts its own power into your spirits.

He describes another small stone by the name of **helioselion** <note>A name combining the Greek words for Sun (*Helios*) and Moon (*Selene*)</note>, which naturally possesses the image of the Sun joined to the Moon. Therefore, whoever places this stone—encased in gilded silver and hung from the neck by similar threads—at the time when the Moon is in her own house, or the Sun's, and meets the Sun in the same degree and minute, and holds both solar and lunar angles, that person will acquire a spirit that is both solar and lunar at once; or at least, a spirit such as the Moon becomes when she is joined to the Sun through the center. Here you see the scattered gifts of **Phoebus** <note>The Sun</note> and, like the limbs of **Osiris** <note>A reference to the Egyptian myth where Osiris's body was scattered and his wife Isis gathered the pieces; here, the magician gathers the Sun's scattered powers</note>, his solar lot being gathered together as if by **Isis**.

But if only we could easily find a solar or lunar stone somewhere that was as powerful in its order as the **magnet** and iron are within the chain of the northern pole. Indeed, they say that **Apollonius of Tyana** <note>A famous 1st-century philosopher and reputed miracle-worker</note> found a solar stone among the Indians—a stone named **pantaura** <note>original: *pantauram*; a legendary gem said to possess all the powers of other stones</note> that glitters like fire. It is born four paces beneath the earth, and so much <term>spirit</term> is within it that the earth swells and is often split open where such a stone is conceived. It draws other stones to itself just as a magnet draws iron.

But this **Herculean stone** <note>original: *lapis herculeus*; a common historical name for the lodestone or magnet, named for its great strength</note> captures our attention even more forcefully at present. We see the needle, which serves as the sailors' guide to the pole, balanced and touched at its tip by a magnet, moving toward the **Bear** <note>The constellation Ursa Major (the Great Bear), which ancient navigators used to find the North Star</note>; for the magnet draws it there because the power of the Bear prevails in this stone. From here it is transferred into the iron, and it draws both toward the Bear. Such power was both infused from the beginning and is continuously nourished by the rays of the Bear. Perhaps **amber** <note>original: *succinum*</note> relates in the same way to the other pole and to straws <note>A reference to static electricity, where rubbed amber attracts light objects</note>.

But tell me meanwhile, why does the magnet everywhere attract iron? Not because it is similar—otherwise a magnet would attract a magnet much more, and iron would attract iron—nor because it is higher in the order of bodies, for a metal is actually higher than a small stone. What then? Both are indeed enclosed in the order that follows the Bear, but the magnet holds a higher rank in that specific property of the Bear, while iron holds a lower one. In the same context of things, the higher attracts the lower and turns it toward itself, or agitates it in some other way, or affects it with a power previously infused; the lower, in turn, is turned toward the higher by that same infusion, or is otherwise moved or completely affected. Thus, in the chain of the Sun, a lower man admires a higher one; in the **Jovian** <note>original: *iouio*; relating to the planet Jupiter</note> order, he respects...

# BOOK III.

In the <term>series</term> <note>original: *serie*; the Neoplatonic "chain" of things linked to a specific planet</note> of the Sun, the lower man admires the superior; in the **Jovian** <note>related to Jupiter</note> order, he venerates him; in the **Martial** <note>related to Mars</note>, he fears him; in the **Venereal** <note>related to Venus</note>, the lower is drawn to the superior by the heat of love and offers himself up. In the **Mercurial** order, the lower is always learning from or being persuaded by the higher; in the **Lunar**, movement is often started by the higher; in the **Saturnine**, rest is commanded. 

When I had explored these matters thus far, I was greatly pleased. While still a young man, I considered carving the figure of the **Celestial Bear** <note>The constellation Ursa Major</note> into a **magnet** <note>original: *magneti*; lodestone</note> with all my might, at a time when the Moon would best look upon it. I hoped that by hanging it from my neck by an iron thread, I would finally become a master of that star’s power. But when I investigated further, I eventually found that the influences of that star are mostly **Saturnine** and **Martial**. I learned from the **Platonists** that evil <term>demons</term> <note>original: *dæmones*; in this context, these are not necessarily "devils" but intermediary spirits or natural forces that can be harmful or disruptive</note> are mostly Northern. Even the Hebrew astronomers confess this, placing harmful and Martial demons in the North. However, I learned from theologians and from **Iamblichus** <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher (c. 245–325 AD) who wrote on theurgy and the power of divine images</note> that those who make images are often possessed and deceived by evil demons, and that the benevolent and **Jovian** demons are located in the South. 

I myself saw a small stone brought to Florence from India, which had been taken out of the head of a **dragon**. It was round, like the shape of a coin, and naturally marked with many points in an orderly way, like stars. When vinegar was poured over it, it moved a little in a straight line—or rather, obliquely—and then it was carried in a circle until the vapor of the vinegar evaporated. I truly thought that a stone of this kind possessed the nature and, as it were, the form of the **Celestial Dragon** <note>The constellation Draco</note>, and that it received its motion from it, provided that the spirit of the vinegar (or of a stronger wine) made it more familiar to that dragon or to the firmament. Therefore, whoever wore this stone and frequently doused it in vinegar might perhaps receive some power from that Dragon, which winds in twin coils, embracing the **Greater Bear** on one side and the **Lesser Bear** on the other. 

There is also the **Serpent-bearer** <note>The constellation Ophiuchus; original: *serpentarius*</note> near the Scorpion, appearing as a man encircled by a serpent, holding the head of the serpent in his right hand and the tail in his left, with his knees as if bent and his head tilted back slightly. I have read that the Magi advised a Persian king to engrave this image into a **hematite** stone, which he should then enclose in a gold ring—but in such a way that he inserted the root of the **serpentaria** <note>The herb birthwort or snakeroot</note> plant between the stone and the gold. They said that the person wearing this ring would be safe against poison and poisonous diseases, provided, of course, that you make it while the Moon is looking upon the Serpent-bearer. **Pietro d'Abano** <note>original: *Petrus Aponensis* (1250–1316); an Italian physician and astrologer</note> confirmed the power of this image. I, however, believe that if that ring has such power, it claims it for itself from heaven not so much through the figure, but through materials of this kind, composed in such a way and at such a time. 

Remember that stones born inside animals—and which do not cause them to waste away—such as those in the **dragon**, the **rooster**, the **swallow**, and others, are almost as effective as stones born in the earth, and they are referred to the same stars to which these animals belong. Hence the **alectorius** <note>original: *alectorius*; a "cock-stone" supposedly found in the gizzards of old roosters</note>, taken from the stomach of an old rooster, is powerful with Solar authority. **Dioscorides** <note>A Greek physician and botanist (c. 40–90 AD)</note> says it has often been found that a person who carries this stone in their mouth fights unconquered. He says the same of the **celidonium** <note>The "swallow-stone," found in the bellies of young swallows</note>...

# ON THE LIFE OF THE HEAVENS. COMPENDIUM.

...a red stone extracted from a swallow cures the melancholic and makes them lovable and pleasant <note>original: *neumque*; likely a typo or variant of *lenemque* (gentle/mild)</note>, which it surely derives from Jupiter. This is possible through those principles we have discussed: that stellar things exist everywhere beneath the Moon. This confirms that very Platonic saying: that this machine of the world is so interconnected with itself that on earth there are earthly things of a celestial condition, and in heaven, conversely, there are terrestrial things with a celestial dignity. Furthermore, in the hidden life of the world and in the Mind—the queen of the world—celestial things are present, yet with a vital and intellectual property and excellence at once. 

Through these principles, some even confirm that magical principle: that through lower things that are in harmony with the higher, celestial influences can in some way be drawn down to humans at opportune times; and even through celestial things, "super-celestial" <note>divine or metaphysical powers beyond the physical planets</note> things can be reconciled or perhaps entirely instilled in us—though let those authors see to that last point. 

But it seems probable enough (as we have said) that this can happen through a certain art that rightly and opportunely gathers many things into one. This is likely both for the reasons we assigned above and because many such ingredients, when they are gathered, crushed, mixed together, and <term>concocted</term> <note>original: *concoquuntur*; a technical term for "cooking" or "digesting" substances so they undergo a chemical and spiritual transformation</note> by a physician and astrologer under a certain star, undergo a new form. While they themselves, by reason of this "cooking" and fermentation, gradually take on a new form, they acquire this very form through a certain celestial nourishment <note>original: *fomento*; literally "kindling" or "warmth"</note>, with rays acting within them at that time, and thus the form is celestial. 

In contrast, a metal or a small stone, when it is engraved in a single moment, does not seem to receive a new quality, but only a figure. That movement does not proceed through the proper degrees of "digestion" <note>original: *digestionis*; the natural process of change or ripening</note> which natural alteration and generation usually observe. Since celestial nature, as the rule of lower nature, prefers to proceed by a certain natural tenor and to breathe upon those things that proceed in such a way, many people rightly doubt that <term>images</term> <note>original: *imagines*; here referring specifically to astrological talismans or amulets engraved with symbols</note> of this kind possess any celestial power. 

I myself am often in doubt, and unless all antiquity and all astrologers thought they possessed a wonderful power, I would deny it; yet I would not deny it entirely. For I am of the opinion (unless someone persuades me otherwise) that they have at least some power for physical health, especially by reason of the materials chosen, although I think a much greater power exists in medicines and ointments prepared under the favor of the stars. 

What I meant just now by "by reason of the materials chosen," I will declare in what follows. Furthermore, those things which can be alleged in favor of "images" from the opinion of the Magi or astrologers to interpret Plato, I will briefly bring forward next—if I first warn you here not to think that I am approving the use of images, but only describing it. For I use medicines tempered according to the heavens, not images, and I advise others to do the same daily. But if you concede that God has inserted wonderful virtues into things below the Moon, concede even more wonderful ones to celestial things. Moreover, if you judge it permissible for a man to use lower things for physical health, judge it permissible to use superior things as well...

### On the power of the heavens, on the strength of rays, and from where we might think images derive their power. Chapter XVII.

The almost immense magnitude, power, and motion of the celestial bodies ensure that all the rays of all the stars penetrate the mass of the earth—which is like a mere point compared to the heavens—instantly and most easily, straight to its center; this is something all astronomers admit. There (as it pleases the <term>Pythagoreans</term> <note>Followers of Pythagoras, who held that a "central fire" existed at the heart of the universe/earth</note> and Platonists), the rays are at their strongest, both because they touch the center directly from every direction, and because they are all gathered together into a narrow space. 

By their intensity, the dry matter of the earth, far removed from moisture, is set on fire; once ignited, it is thinned out and dispersed through passages everywhere, exhaling fires and sulfur alike. But they think this fire is very murky and like a certain blaze devoid of light—just as in heaven there exists light devoid of blaze. However, fire joins the celestial light and the infernal light together with heat. Moreover, they think the fire blowing from the center is the <term>Vestal fire</term>, since they considered Vesta to be the life and divinity of the earth; for this reason, the ancients used to build the temple of Vesta in the middle of cities and placed a perpetual fire in the center. 

But lest we wander too far, let us now conclude: if the rays of the stars soon penetrate the whole earth, it cannot easily be denied that they also suddenly penetrate metal and small stones when they are engraved with images <note>Ficino is referring here to astrological talismans</note>, impressing upon them marvelous or at least some kind of gifts—especially since they also generate the most precious things <note>i.e., gold and gemstones</note> in other parts of the earth. 

Indeed, who would deny that rays penetrate through these things, since air, and its quality, and sound—which is less powerful—pass through solids suddenly and affect them with their own particular quality? Now truly, if hardness stood in the way of penetrating rays of light, light would pass through air much faster than through water, and through water much faster than glass, and through glass likewise faster than crystal. But since it pierces through all solids at the same moment as liquids, it is clearly evident that hardness in no way resists the rays. Therefore, they will say it must not be denied that metals receive the rays and influences of the heavens and preserve them for a time then destined for them by heaven—preserving, I say, a certain virtue created from the contact of concurrent rays. 

What then? What if a harder material, by the very fact that it seems to resist a more powerful cause, exposes itself more to the blows? Just as a sword cuts wood beneath wool without the wool being cut, or as a lightning bolt sometimes melts the metal inside a leather pouch without the leather being harmed <note>This was a common Renaissance scientific "fact" used to explain how invisible forces can bypass a container to act upon its contents</note>. Since, indeed, celestial nature is incomparably more excellent than this fire of ours, we must not think that the function of celestial rays is mere—

<summary>Ficino argues that celestial rays effortlessly penetrate the Earth to its core, fueling a central "Vestal" fire and imbuing metals and stones with planetary powers. He uses the transparency of crystal and the behavior of lightning to prove that physical hardness cannot block these spiritual and astral influences.</summary>
