These total 14 hours and 21 minutes. This is the post-meridian and astrological time <note>Astrologers of this period traditionally began their day at noon rather than midnight.</note>, and it is the time we were seeking. This calculation must always be performed once the semi-diurnal arc has been found. <note>The "semi-diurnal arc" is half the time the Sun remains above the horizon on a given day.</note> However, if this total exceeds 24 hours, subtract 24; the remainder is the post-meridian time of the following day. But when you have the semi-nocturnal arc <note>Half the length of the night.</note>, the semi-diurnal arc must be found through it. This is done by subtracting the semi-nocturnal arc from 12 hours. Whatever remains will be the semi-diurnal arc. For example: When the Sun is at the 1st degree of <margin>X</margin> Aries, the semi-nocturnal arc will be 6 hours and 47 minutes. I subtract this time from 12 hours in this way:

| | | |
|:---|:---|:---|
| | Hours 12 | Minutes 0 |
| Semi-nocturnal Arc | Hours 6 | Minutes 47 |
| Semi-diurnal Arc | ----------- | ----------- |
| | Hours 5 | Minutes 13 |

I use this arc as stated above.

Once this time is found, another time must also be found, which is called the "time from noon." This is nothing other than the time elapsed since the beginning of Aries began to move away from the meridian line on that same day—the point from which Astrologers begin the measurement of the day. It is found in this way:

With the degree of the sun mentioned above, enter the tables of the houses in the ephemerides <note>An "ephemeris" is a book of astronomical tables.</note> (those of Magini <note>Giovanni Paolo Magini (1555–1617) was a prominent Italian astronomer and mathematician.</note> begin on page 113). First, look at the top of the tables for the latitude of your city; if it is not present, use the nearest one. In this case, it is 45 degrees. Since every latitude has twelve tables inscribed for the twelve signs, you must use the one that has the Sun in your sign at the top—namely, in Aries. In the second column on the left, labeled 10 <note>This refers to the 10th House, or the Midheaven.</note>, find the degree (in this case, the 17th degree). The time located directly to the left in the first column, titled "time from noon," is what you seek. In our example, this is 11 hours and 16 minutes. Add this time to the post-meridian time in this way:

| | |
|:---|:---|
| Post-meridian time | Hours 14, Minutes 21 |
| Time from noon | Hours 11, Minutes 16 |
| | ----------- |
| Sum of the times | 25, Minutes 37 |
| Subtract | 24 |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| Time for erecting the theme | Hours 1, Minutes 37 |

It must be noted here that whenever the sum of these two times exceeds 24 hours, those 24 hours must be subtracted, and the remaining time used for constructing the twelve houses of heaven, as shown below.

Once this time is found, as stated, you must enter the same house tables calculated for your latitude, and in the first column on the left, inscribed...

### ON ASTROLOGY

Once the time is recorded, you must search for your calculated time from noon in the tables. In our earlier example, this was 1 hour and 37 minutes. If this exact time is listed, use it; if it is not, you must use the closest value, whether it is the slightly smaller one or the slightly larger one. In our example, the closest smaller time is 1 hour, 36 minutes, and 25 seconds, and the closest larger time is 1 hour, 40 minutes, and 12 seconds. Since the smaller value is closer to our time, I will use it. The numbers found in the six columns to the left of this time give you the six <term>cuspides</term> <note>A 'cusp' is the boundary line that marks the beginning of an astrological house.</note> of the ascending houses: namely the 10th, 11th, 12th, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd houses. The other six descending houses are recorded using the opposite signs and degrees in the square chart, as we taught in the first book. In our example, the cusp of the 10th house will be 26 degrees of Capricorn (♑); the 11th, 7 degrees of Gemini (♊); the 12th, 14 degrees of Cancer (♋); the 1st, 10 degrees and 17 minutes of Leo (♌); the 2nd, 2 degrees of Virgo (♍); and the 3rd, 25 degrees of Virgo (♍). The others are found by their opposites.

Once the celestial figure is erected in this manner, it remains for the planets to be written into their places in the zodiac. For this to be done correctly, you must attend to two things: first, the location in the zodiac where they are at <term>noon</term> <note>Astrologers traditionally began their 24-hour day at noon rather than midnight.</note> (that is, the beginning of that day according to astrologers) for which you wish to have the chart; and second, how much they have traveled through the zodiac after noon during those hours you have, if you wish to set the chart for a time after noon. If you are setting the chart exactly at noon, the planets are placed exactly as they appear in the <term>ephemeris</term> <note>An ephemeris is a book of tables providing the daily positions of the sun, moon, and planets.</note>. You can find the first part without labor in the ephemerides by looking up the year, month, and day; in that row, you will have the location of all the planets as they are in the heavens at noon on that day.

To know exactly how far they have moved after noon from that position, you must proceed as follows. First, you should transfer the location of each individual planet separately onto a small page. Then, to each of those locations, you must add as much zodiacal space as each planet can travel during the hours you have after noon—which, in our example, is 14 hours and 21 minutes. This space is found by subtracting the planet's location on the day we are seeking from the planet's location on the following day. The remainder is the motion of the planet in 24 hours. Once this is known, calculate the proportional part that belongs to the 14 hours; that will be the amount which, when added to the planet's initial location, gives you their true position. The matter will be made clearer by an example using the Sun (☉) in Virgo (♍).

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Location of the Sun on the 10th day is 17 deg. 32 m. 52 s. of Virgo (♍).
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;on the 9th day, 16 deg. 34 m. 25 s. of Virgo (♍).

->Daily motion of the Sun (☉): 0 deg. 58 m. 27 s.<-

->Distribute the calculation thus:<-

24 Hours &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0 deg. 58 m. 27 s. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;14 Hours 21 Min.

If you wish to avoid the labor of calculation and using the tables found in the ephemerides, you may simply note that in any given hour, the Sun travels approximately 2 and a half minutes. Therefore, 14 hours will give you 35 minutes; when these are added to the Sun's [noon] location, they result in 17 degrees and 9 minutes.

<header>INTRODUCTION</header>

September 9th (♍). Therefore, on the 9th day of September at 2:00 PM <note>original: "H. 14. post meridiem" — 14 hours after noon.</note> the Sun (☉) will be at that specific place in the Zodiac. The same must be said for the Moon (☽), which generally travels 12 degrees every day. Therefore, for every two hours, you should add 1 minute <note>original: "m. 1" — arc-minutes</note> in its proper place. In our example, therefore, 7 minutes must be added, which results in 18 degrees and 22 minutes of Libra (♎). If you place the remaining planets according to how they appear in the <term>ephemeris</term> <note>An ephemeris is a table providing the daily positions of celestial bodies.</note>, it will not be inconvenient, especially for a physician. However, in the case of someone’s birth chart <note>original: "genesi"</note>, I do not approve of this shorthand method at all; once the locations of each individual planet are known, they must each be placed in the figure in their specific Zodiacal locations, just as you have found them.

## On Extracting the Part of Fortune

In almost every positioning of the heavens, there is a certain point in the zodiac called the **Part of Fortune**. Astrologers say that from this point, they can foreknow the fortune and the <term>genius</term> <note>In this context, "genius" refers to the guiding spirit or innate nature of a person.</note> of the one born. You may see this discussed by Marsilio Ficino <note>Ficino (1433–1499) was a famous Italian scholar and priest who sought to reconcile Platonism with Christianity.</note> in the book *On Obtaining Life from the Heavens*, chapter 24. This same Part of Fortune is used by Hasfurtus <note>Johann Virdung of Hassfurt, a 16th-century physician and astrologer.</note> in Book 3, chapter 1, to find the **Almuten** <note>The 'Almuten' is the planet that has the most dignity or "power" over a specific point in the chart, often used here to diagnose the nature of an illness.</note> of the sick person. Therefore, one must carefully observe how this is found; but before that is handed down, one must first be taught what it is. It is, therefore, nothing other than a point in the zodiac that is as far distant from the ascending degree of the zodiac as the Sun (☉) is from the Moon (☽), or the Moon from the Sun. For during the day, the calculation is drawn from the Sun to the Moon, and at night from the Moon to the Sun, although Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the foundational authority on Western astrology and astronomy.</note> always extracts it from the Sun to the Moon regardless.

Once the nature of the Part of Fortune is known, we must see how it is found, since that is what we then desire to know. If you wish to extract it from the Sun to the Moon, first see in your figure (drawn according to custom) how many signs, degrees, and minutes <note>original: "scrupula"</note>, if present, the Moon (☽) is distant from the beginning of Aries (♈). Next, do the same for the Sun (☉), and subtract the Sun's distance from the Moon's distance. What remains is the distance that should exist between the ascending degree and the Part of Fortune. If it is extracted from the Moon to the Sun, you must subtract the Moon's distance from the Sun's distance. However, this caution must be applied: if the top number (from which the lower must be subtracted) happens to be smaller, you must add 12 <note>This refers to the 12 signs of the Zodiac to allow for the subtraction.</note>. In our example, one can see that the Moon is at 17 degrees and 9 minutes of Virgo (♍), and the Sun is at 18 degrees and 22 minutes of Libra (♎). The Sun, therefore, is this far from the beginning of Aries:

| | |
|---|---|
| Sun (☉) | 7 Signs, 18 degrees, 22 minutes |
| Moon (☽) distance | 5 Signs, 17 degrees, 9 minutes |
| | **2 Signs, 1 degree, 13 minutes** |

### The Distance of the Sun from the Moon

Once this distance is known, one must see where it falls, which is done if it is projected from the ascendant. This will be done in this manner: See in the erected figure how many degrees of the emerging sign in the **Horoscope** <note>In Renaissance astrology, the 'Horoscope' specifically refers to the Ascendant, or the point rising over the eastern horizon.</note> have ascended above the horizon, and add those to the distance found above in this way.

Distance of the Sun (☉) from the Moon (☽): 2 Signs, 1 degree, 13 minutes.
The 2nd degree of Cancer (♋) rising: 0 Signs, 2 degrees, 0 minutes.

Distance of the Part of Fortune (⊗) from the <term>Horoscope</term> <note>In traditional astrology, the "horoscope" refers specifically to the Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note>: 2 Signs, 3 degrees, 13 minutes.

### On Extracting the Part of the Liver

Even though anyone who understood what was said regarding the Part of Fortune from the words of Hasfurtus <note>Johann Virdung of Hassfurt (c. 1463–1538/39) was a famous German physician and astrologer whose works were widely used for medical prognosis.</note> will easily understand how the Part of the Liver (♂) <note>original: "♂ pars hepatis" — the author uses the symbol for Mars to represent this specific "lot" or point related to the liver.</note> is found, I will nevertheless provide an example of this matter to satisfy the scholars who urged this of me while the previous books were being printed. Therefore, as our Hasfurtus left written in Book 3, Chapter 1, the Part of the Liver is always extracted from Jupiter (♃) to Mars (♂), and is cast <note>Projected from a starting point.</note> from Venus (♀). In our example, it stands as follows: Mars is at the 23rd degree, 45th minute of Taurus (♉). Jupiter is at the 29th degree, 29th minute of Aries (♈).

| | |
|:---|:---|
| Therefore, Mars (♂) is distant from the start of Aries (♈). | 1 Sign, 23 degrees, 45 minutes. |
| Jupiter (♃) is distant. | 0 Signs, 29 degrees, 29 minutes. |

---

Distance of Mars (♂) from Jupiter (♃): 0 Signs, 24 degrees, 16 minutes.

This distance must then be cast from the location of Venus (♀). This is done by adding the degrees which Venus has completed in her sign in this manner:

| | |
|:---|:---|
| Distance of Mars (♂) from Jupiter (♃). | 0 Signs, 24 degrees, 16 minutes. |
| The degree in which Venus (♀) is located. | 0 Signs, 5 degrees, 22 minutes. |

---

Total: 0 Signs, 29 degrees, 38 minutes.

Since this number does not exceed 30, the Part of the Liver will be at the 29th degree, 38th minute of Gemini (♊), which is the sign Venus is in.

->THE END.<-

### On extracting the Part of the Liver.

Although anyone who has understood what was said about the Part of Fortune from the words of **Hasfurt** <note>Johann Virdung of Hasfurt (c. 1463–1543), a celebrated German mathematician and astrologer to the Elector Palatine.</note> will easily understand how the **Part of the Liver** <note>One of many "Arabic Parts" or "Lots"—mathematical points used to predict specific life areas; the liver was traditionally associated with Jupiter (the organ) and Mars (the bile/heat).</note> (associated with Mars ♂) is found, nevertheless, to satisfy the students who urged me to do so while the previous books were being printed, I will also provide an example for this matter. ->Jupiter ♃ is distant: 0 Signs, 29 degrees, 29 minutes.<-

Distance of Mars ♂ from Jupiter ♃: ->0 Signs, 24 degrees, 16 minutes.<-
->The degree in which Venus ♀ is: 0 Signs, 5 degrees, 22 minutes.<-

## On the planets.

Some of the planets are:
{
Masculine: Saturn ♄, Jupiter ♃, Mars ♂, the Sun ☉.
Feminine: Venus ♀, the Moon ☽.
Promiscuous: Mercury ☿, alone. <note>original: "Promiscui." In astrology, Mercury is considered neutral or adaptable, taking on the gender of the planets it is associated with.</note>
}

Some of the planets are:
{
Diurnal: Saturn ♄, Jupiter ♃, the Sun ☉. <note>original: "Diurni." These planets belong to the "day faction" or sect.</note>
Nocturnal: Venus ♀, the Moon ☽, Mars ♂. <note>original: "Nocturni." These planets belong to the "night faction" or sect.</note>
Common: Mercury ☿, alone.
}

Some of the planets are:
{
Good or fortunate: Jupiter ♃ and Venus ♀, but Jupiter is better. <note>These are the "benefics" believed to bring positive influence.</note>
Bad or unfortunate: Saturn ♄ and Mars ♂, but Saturn is worse. <note>These are the "malefics" traditionally associated with hardship.</note>
Mediocre: The Sun ☉, the Moon ☽, Mercury ☿. <note>These are considered neutral or variable in their influence.</note>
}

The essential qualities of the planets:
{
**Saturn ♄**: Cold and dry, earthy, and melancholic.
**Jupiter ♃**: Temperate, hot and moist, airy, and sanguine.
**Mars ♂**: Hot and dry, fiery, and choleric.
**The Sun ☉**: Hot and dry, choleric, with a temperate disposition.
**Venus ♀**: Cold and moist, phlegmatic with a temperate disposition.
**Mercury ☿**: Versatile—now dry, now moist—and melancholic.
**The Moon ☽**: Cold and moist, watery, and phlegmatic.
}
<note>These qualities align the planets with the four humors of ancient medicine: melancholic (black bile), sanguine (blood), choleric (yellow bile), and phlegmatic (phlegm).</note>

**Accidental dignities of the planets, and their opposites.** <margin>Dignitates planetarum accidentales, & e contra.</margin>
> **Direct** is when it moves according to the sequence of the signs.
> **Retrograde** is when it moves against the order of the signs.
> **Stationary** is when it appears to stand still.
> **Fast** is when it advances more in a day than its mean <note>average</note> motion.
> **Slow** is when it advances less in a day than its mean motion.

# ON ASTROLOGY

->The accidental qualities of the planets by reason of their aspects.<-

☌ **Conjunction** <note>original: "conjunctio"</note> occurs when two or more planets are united in the same sign, degree, and minute. This happens either:
* **Partile** <note>original: "Partiliter"</note>, when it occurs in the exact same degree and minute of the sign.
* **Platick** <note>original: "Platicè"</note>, which occurs within the range of the half-orb of the planets.

<image-desc>These aspects are either Platick or Partile; and they are either Right-handed (Dexter), which are against the order of the signs, or Left-handed (Sinister), which follow the order of the signs.</image-desc>
* **Sextile** (*) contains 2 signs, or 60 degrees.
* □ **Square** <note>original: "Quadratus"</note> contains 3 signs, or 90 degrees.
* △ **Trine** <note>original: "Trigonus"</note> contains 4 signs, or 120 degrees.
* ☍ **Opposition** <note>original: "Oppositus"</note> contains 6 signs, or 180 degrees.

Of these aspects, some are:
* **Good:** Sextile (*), Trine (△), but the Trine is stronger.
* **Bad:** Square (□), Opposition (☍), but the Opposition is worse.

**Application** <note>original: "Applicatio"</note> to a conjunction or aspect is said to occur when a lower (faster) planet approaches a superior (slower) planet so that the orbs of both touch.
**Separation** <note>original: "Separatio"</note> occurs when the planet has moved away by the quantity of its orb, yet in such a way that the orbs of both still touch.

->Table of the orbs of the planets.<-
<note>In astrology, an "orb" is the sphere of influence surrounding a planet. The values here represent the distance in degrees at which a planet's influence begins to "touch" another.</note>

| Planet | | Casts its rays beyond and before. | Value |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|

| ♃ Jupiter | ) | | 12 |

->The accidental qualities of the planets by reason of the Sun.<-

**Combust** <note>original: "Combustus"</note> describes a planet when it is more than 16 minutes away from the Sun, but less than half of its own orb. <note>This was traditionally considered a position of great weakness, as if the planet were "burned up" by the Sun's heat.</note>
**In the Heart of the Sun** <note>original: "In corde Solis," also known as Cazimi</note> occurs when the planet is closest to the Sun, within 16 minutes before or after. <note>Unlike combustion, being "in the heart" was considered a position of great strength.</note>
**Under the Rays** <note>original: "Sub radijs"</note> describes a planet that is within 17 degrees before or after the Sun.
**Oriental** <note>original: "Orientalis"</note> is when the planet appears above the earth in the morning time before sunrise.
**Occidental** <note>original: "Occidentalis"</note> is when it is seen above the earth in the evening after sunset.
Planets are also called **Oriental** when they are between the Ascendant (horoscope) and the Midheaven <note>original: "medium cœli"</note>, and from the Descendant (setting) to the Bottom of the Sky <note>original: "imum cœli"</note>. In these places, they are also called **Masculine**.
They are **Occidental** and **Feminine** when they are in the remaining two quarters of the chart.
**Increasing in Light** <note>original: "Auctus lumine"</note> is said while the planet moves away from the Sun, or the Sun from it.
**Decreasing in Light** <note>original: "Minutus lumine"</note> is when it approaches the Sun, or the Sun approaches it.

# INTRODUCTION

☉ The Sun <note>The symbol ☉ represents the Sun.</note> is said to be *increased in numbers* <note>In traditional astronomy, this means the planet is moving faster than its average daily motion.</note> when the equation of the argument is added to the mean motion. This is determined from the tables of Alfonso <note>original: "tabulis Alfonsi," referring to the Alfonsine Tables, a major medieval astronomical resource.</note>, Stadius, the Prutenic tables, and especially Magini, which you will soon be able to obtain from the "Workshop of the Salamander" <note>original: "officina Salamandræ," likely a reference to a specific printing house using a salamander as its printer's mark.</note>.

### *Essential debilities of the planets.*

*Peregrine* <note>original: "Peregrinus"</note> is a planet when, in the place where it is currently located, it possesses no essential dignity or strength.
*In detriment* <note>original: "In detrimento"</note> is when a planet is in the zodiac sign opposite its own house.
*In fall* <note>original: "In casu"</note> is when it is in the sign that is opposite the sign of its exaltation.

->Concerning the accidental qualities of the Moon:<-

<image-desc>A hierarchical diagram using brackets to classify the accidental qualities of the Moon. The primary classification is by motion (Diurnal and Monthly). The diurnal motion is divided into four quadrants relative to the houses (10th, 7th, 4th, 1st). The monthly motion is divided by aspects: from the Moon to the first square, first square to conjunction, conjunction to second square, and second square back to the Moon.</image-desc>

*   **The accidental qualities of the Moon are known from its motion:**
    *   **Diurnal motion. For while it moves from the house:**
        *   First to the 10th, it is hot and moist.
        *   Tenth to the 7th, it is hot and dry.
        *   Septima to the 4th, it is cold and dry.
        *   Fourth to the first, it is cold and moist.
    *   **Monthly motion, from the Moon:**
        *   Moon (☾) to the first square (□) is hot and moist.
        *   First square (□) to conjunction (☌) is hot and dry.
        *   Conjunction (☌) to the second square (□) is cold and dry.
        *   Second square (□) to the Moon (☾) is cold and moist.

Make the same judgment concerning the other planets, provided however that their original or essential nature is preserved; to that nature, something is either added or taken away by reason of their placement according to this doctrine.

*   The **animal virtue**, which resides in the brain, [is strengthened] especially by airy things with fiery things joined to them, and when the Moon is in similar houses or seats and gazes upon Jupiter: especially if it closely embraces Jupiter and Venus <note>The symbol ♀ represents Venus.</note>.

->On the letting of blood.<-

Other things being observed, which will be mentioned below, it will be useful to extract blood when the Moon travels through that quarter [of the zodiac] which is similar either to the age or the temperament <term>complexioni: the specific balance of the four humors—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—in an individual</term> of the person from whom blood is being extracted; for this reason, that rule is also observed.

**Blood is extracted:**
*   **Pure [Blood]**, at sunrise.
*   **Choleric** <note>Yellow bile</note>, at midday.
*   **Melancholic** <note>Black bile</note>, at sunset.
*   **Phlegmatic**, at the middle of the night.

**Blood is to be extracted:**
1.  **For Phlegmatic types**, from all parts of the body when the Moon is in:
    *   Aries (♈) Except for the head.
    *   Sagittarius (♐) Except for the hips.
2.  **For Melancholic types**, from all parts of the body when the Moon is in:
    *   The first 15 degrees of Taurus (♉).
    *   Libra (♎) Except for the buttocks.
    *   Aquarius (♒) Except for the legs.
3.  **For Choleric types**, from all parts of the body when the Moon is in:
    *   Cancer (♋) Except for the chest.
    *   Scorpio (♏) Except for the genitals.
    *   Pisces (♓) Except for the feet.

**Do not extract blood while the Moon is in Gemini (♊) or Leo (♌).**
**Do not touch a limb with iron** <note>original: "ferro," referring to the surgical blade or lancet used in phlebotomy.</note> **while the Moon is in the zodiac sign that rules that limb.**
Which limbs they rule, you have below:
Aries (♈) rules the head and face.
Taurus (♉) [rules] the neck and the knot of the throat <note>The Adam's apple.</note>.
Gemini (♊) [rules] the shoulders, arms, and hands.

# INTRODUCTION

♌ **Leo** <note>The Lion; governs the mid-body.</note> governs the *stomach, heart, back, and side.*
♍ **Virgo** <note>The Virgin.</note> governs the *belly and internal organs.*
♎ **Libra** <note>The Scales.</note> governs the *loins, the lower abdomen, the navel, the groin <note>original: "pectinem"</note>, the private parts, the hips, the flanks, and the buttocks.*
♏ **Scorpio** <note>The Scorpion.</note> governs the *private parts, the testicles, the bladder, the anus, and the thighs.*
♐ **Sagittarius** <note>The Archer.</note> governs the *thighs.*
♑ **Capricorn** <note>The Horned Goat.</note> governs the *knees.*
♒ **Aquarius** <note>The Water-Bearer.</note> governs the *legs down to the lower ankles.*
♓ **Pisces** <note>The Fish.</note> governs the *feet.*

The Moon (☽) in **conjunction** (☌) <note>When the Moon and another planet are in the same degree of the zodiac.</note> with:
*   The Sun (☉): *Prevents bloodletting <note>original: "Sanguinis missionem"</note> three days before and three days after.*
*   Saturn (♄): *Prevents it for one day before and one day after.*
*   Mars (♂): *Same as Saturn.*
*   Venus (♀): *Only while she is "combust" <note>When a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is "burnt up."</note>.*
*   Mercury (☿): *Same as Venus.*

The Moon (☽) in **opposition** (☍) <note>When the Moon and a planet are 180 degrees apart.</note> to the Sun (☉), Saturn (♄), or Mars (♂): *Prevents bloodletting for one day before and one day after.*

The Moon (☽) in **square** (□) <note>A harsh 90-degree angle between celestial bodies.</note> with the Sun (☉), Saturn (♄), or Mars (♂): *Prevents it as long as the Moon is within 8 degrees of them.*

The Moon (☽) **regarding** <note>Forming an aspect with.</note> Jupiter (♃) in any aspect signifies a *favorable time for bloodletting.*

The Moon (☽) in **sextile** (✶) or **trine** (△) <note>Harmonious angles of 60 and 120 degrees.</note> with the Sun (☉) or Mars (♂) *gives a favorable bloodletting.*

->**On medicines.**<-

When about to **stimulate the bowels** <note>original: "Citaturus aluum"</note> with medicines—whether *solid, liquid, or moderate*—choose the signs of **Pisces (♓), Scorpio (♏), or Cancer (♋)** <note>These are the Water signs, traditionally associated with the movement of fluids.</note>.

When about to **purge** through either the *lower or upper parts* of the body: choose **Pisces (♓), Scorpio (♏), or Cancer (♋)**.

In every purging, you shall take care that the Moon (☽) is not regarded by any aspect from **Saturn (♄)** or **Mars (♂)**. For Saturn troubles the stomach, while Mars dissolves the intestines <note>i.e., causes excessive or violent diarrhea</note>.
Neither should the Moon be joined to **Jupiter (♃)** or **Venus (♀)**. For these planets strengthen the body so much that the medicine is overcome by them <note>making the treatment ineffective</note>.
Nor should the Moon be in **Aries (♈), Taurus (♉), or Capricorn (♑)**; however, while the Moon is in these signs, you may induce vomiting.
When you wish to purge any specific part of the body, beware that the planet ruling that limb is not strong, nor in its own hour; however, make the sign ruling that limb either the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and fortunate, or ensure the Moon is located within it.

*When you wish to have the favor of any planet, ensure that it is strong in one of the angles* <note>The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of an astrological chart, considered the most powerful positions for a planet.</note>, *and let this be done on the day and in the hour of that same planet, and in those matters over which it rules; also, let it be in a good aspect* <note>A favorable geometric relationship, like a trine or sextile.</note> *to the Moon (☽).*

# ON ASTROLOGY

When you wish to secure the favor of a particular planet, ensure that it is positioned strongly in one of the <term>angles<note>In astrology, the 'angles' are the four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st (Ascendant), 4th (Imum Coeli), 7th (Descendant), and 10th (Midheaven).</note></term>, and perform your work on the day and hour belonging to that planet, using items over which it holds dominion, and ensuring it forms a favorable <term>aspect<note>An 'aspect' is the geometric angle between two celestial bodies, which determines their influence on one another.</note></term> with the Moon.

☾ When the Moon is in signs presiding over specific parts of the body <note>This refers to the 'Zodiacal Man,' an ancient concept where each sign of the zodiac rules a specific limb or organ.</note>, those parts should not be disturbed, but rather comforted.
☾ When the Moon enters Aries, it is an appropriate time for bathing.
☾ When the Moon is in ♌ <note>Leo</note>, do not induce vomiting.
☾ When the Moon is in ♏ <note>Scorpio</note>, make use of enemas.
☾ When the Moon is in  Pisces, do not attempt bathing.

In every undertaking, take care that the rising sign <note>The Ascendant</note> does not correspond to the 12th, 8th, or 6th house of your <term>radix<note>Latin: *radix*, meaning 'root'. In astrology, this refers to the natal or birth chart.</note></term> <note>These three houses were traditionally considered 'unfortunate' or 'malefic,' associated with illness, enemies, and death.</note>.

Avoid a Saturnian or Martian physician <note>original: *Medicum saturnium, vel Martium*. These are doctors whose temperaments or astrological charts are dominated by Saturn or Mars, planets traditionally associated with hardship and aggression.</note>; for they are unfortunate in their works. If the seventh house of your birth chart is afflicted, change your doctor.

The remainder can be easily gathered through diligent study, both from these small volumes and from others that treat these subjects. Let these points, however, suffice for beginners.

<meta>This page provides practical assembly instructions for the astronomical volvelles (paper instruments) mentioned in the previous section's astrological guidelines. It bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge of planetary influences and the physical tools required to calculate them.</meta>

<column-break/>

To be as helpful as possible to as many people as we can—since not everyone has access to these—we have seen to it that these four <term>volvelles<note>Latin: *rotulas*. These are rotating paper discs used as analog calculation tools in early books.</note></term> are printed. These discs depict the twelve <term>celestial houses<note>Segments of the sky used in astrology to determine different areas of life.</note></term>, the hours measured from noon, and what are known as <term>planetary hours<note>An ancient system where each hour of the day and night is ruled by one of the seven classical planets.</note></term>, all calibrated for various latitudes. Therefore, everyone should find out the latitude of their own city and use the specific volvelle that has their latitude—or the closest one to it—marked in the center, ignoring the other three. You can find your city's latitude in an <term>Ephemeris<note>Latin: *Ephemeridibus*. A table providing the positions of celestial bodies and geographical coordinates.</note></term>; if your specific city is not listed, look for the latitude of the nearest city to you.

To use them, you must assemble all the volvelles in their proper place. To do this, refer to page 28b. There you will find a disc divided into 24 parts; a thread must be fixed through its center. The "center" is the point where the two lines cross at right angles. Onto this disc, using the same thread, you should stack the one of these four volvelles that matches your latitude, aligning it where its diagonal lines cross. On top of that, attach the smaller disc that features the twelve signs of the Zodiac, aligning it at the intersection of the lines in its center. Finally, atop the whole assembly, fix the small pointer (the "rule") labeled <term>line of faith<note>Latin: *Linea fiduciæ*. In navigation and astronomy, this is a 'fiducial line'—a fixed reference line or a pointer used for taking measurements.</note></term>, marked with the symbol for the Sun (☉). Once arranged, they should be tied together with the thread so they can turn easily without coming apart. When you have set them up this way, use them as instructed in the first book.
